calls.title: VAiF26 — Photography Portfolio Open Call 2026
calls.description: Free international open call from the Visual Arts International Festival (VAiF) in Thessaloniki, Greece, for cohesive photographic portfolios with a strong artistic vision and personal storytelling. Selected portfolios are presented in a group exhibition at VAiF26 in November 2026. The organization covers production and exhibition costs. Jury: independent curator and photographer Stergios Karavatos; Stefanos Kesidis (Artistic Director of VAiF and Deputy Director of esp+ photography school); Anastasia Markidou (Associate Professor and Director of the MA program 'Photography: Research and Methodology'); Manolis Skoufias (Director of Studies at esp+, PhD in Photography). Open to photographers 18+ worldwide. One portfolio of up to 10 cohesive images, each minimum 1500 px on the longest side at 150 dpi or higher, .jpg/.jpeg/.png/.pdf, total submission under 25 MB. Each submission includes project title, artist statement, biography, artist portrait, and contact information.
jury: Stergios Karavatos, Independent Curator & Photography Educator
Stefanos Kesidis, Artistic Director, VAiF / Deputy Director, esp+
Anastasia Markidou, Associate Professor; Director, MA 'Photography: Research and Methodology'
Manolis Skoufias, Director of Studies, esp+; PhD in Photography
calls.summary: Free open call from Visual Arts International Festival in Thessaloniki. Group exhibition in November 2026. Academic and curatorial jury.
prose: The Visual Arts International Festival (VAiF) is an annual festival of contemporary visual arts held in Thessaloniki, Greece, organised by the esp+ photography school. The 2026 edition (VAiF26) is built around a Photography Portfolio Open Call seeking cohesive bodies of work with a strong artistic vision, a contemporary approach, and a personal mode of storytelling.

Selected portfolios are exhibited together as part of VAiF26 in Thessaloniki in November 2026. The festival covers production and exhibition costs; entries are free and open to photographers aged 18 or over from anywhere in the world. Notification of results is sent by email and announced on the festival website and social channels.

The 2026 jury combines curatorial and academic voices in Greek photography: independent curator, photographer and photography educator Stergios Karavatos; Stefanos Kesidis, Artistic Director of VAiF and Deputy Director of the esp+ photography school; Anastasia Markidou, Associate Professor and Director of the MA programme 'Photography: Research and Methodology'; and Manolis Skoufias, Director of Studies at esp+ and PhD in Photography.

Photographers submit one portfolio of up to 10 cohesive images, each at least 1500 pixels on the longest side and 150 dpi or higher, in .jpg, .jpeg, .png or .pdf format, with the total ZIP under 25 MB. Each entry requires a project title, artist statement, biography, artist portrait and full contact information. The deadline is Sunday, May 31, 2026 at 23:59 GMT.

calls.title: LensCulture Street Photography Awards 2026
calls.description: Annual international street photography competition with $10,000 total cash prizes across Series and Single Image categories. Nine international jurors from Magnum Photos, the New York Times, Getty Images, Le Monde, Leica Gallery, Travel + Leisure, Women Street Photographers and more. Series prizes: 1st $3,500, 2nd $2,000, 3rd $1,000. Single image prizes: 1st $2,000, 2nd $1,000, 3rd $500. Nine Jurors' Picks and 25 Finalists receive worldwide promotion via LensCulture's network of editors, curators, and 250,000+ followers. Winning photographers exhibit at Photo London 2027 with an opening reception for artists, media, and industry professionals. One free single image entry per photographer; additional singles $10 each or 5 for $35; series of up to 10 images $45. Optional expert written review $25. 30% student discount. Work must be created in the last 10 years; street genre across all approaches welcome.
jury: Eslah Attar, The New York Times
Gulnara Lyabib Samoilova, Women Street Photographers
calls.summary: LensCulture annual street photography awards. $10,000 in prizes, 9 international jurors, exhibition at Photo London 2027. Free single entry.
prose: The LensCulture Street Photography Awards is one of LensCulture's flagship annual competitions, drawing entries from across the world to a panel of editors, curators, gallerists, and Magnum photographers. The 2026 edition runs alongside LensCulture's wider awards programme and culminates in a winners' exhibition at Photo London 2027 — the UK's premier international photo fair — with an opening reception for artists, photo editors, curators, and industry insiders.

There are two competition categories. Series accepts up to 10 images on a single concept or project, with prizes of $3,500 (1st), $2,000 (2nd) and $1,000 (3rd). Single Image accepts standalone photographs, with prizes of $2,000, $1,000 and $500. Beyond the top six, an additional 9 Jurors' Picks are highlighted with individual quotes and 25 Finalists are promoted across LensCulture's editorial channels and global network of partners.

The 2026 jury panel is unusually broad: Nanna Heitmann (Magnum Photos), Eslah Attar (The New York Times), Michael Foley (Leica Gallery), Dr. Rebecca Swift (Getty Images), Audrey Delaporte (Le Monde), Scott Hall (Travel + Leisure), Gulnara Lyabib Samoilova (Women Street Photographers), Australian photographer-educator Sam Ferris, and Laura Sackett (LensCulture).

Entry is via lensculture.com. Every photographer gets one free single image entry. Additional single images cost $10 each (or 5 for $35), and a series of up to 10 images is $45. Optional written reviews from a photo expert can be added for $25 per submission, and full-time students receive a 30% discount on entry fees. Work must have been created within the past 10 years. The deadline is Wednesday, June 17, 2026, at 23:59 UTC.

calls.title: Expand and Contract 2026 — American Documentary Photography
calls.description: LACP's annual virtual juried open call focusing on American documentary photography in the 21st century. The brief asks how America sees itself, what it highlights, and what might be missing from the frame. Open internationally to all skill levels and to any photographic medium. Juror Dr. Rotem Rozental, LACP's Executive Director and Chief Curator, selects works for a virtual exhibition on LACP's website running July 16–October 16, 2026, with top three winners invited to show in an in-person component. Prizes: 1st place $500 cash plus in-person invitation; 2nd place $250 LACP gift card, one-year membership, and in-person; 3rd place $250 LACP gift card and in-person. Honorable mentions placed in the online gallery for three months. AI involvement beyond basic editing must be disclosed; no watermarks accepted. Members receive a 25% fee discount across all tiers.
jury: Dr. Rotem Rozental, Executive Director and Chief Curator, LACP
calls.summary: LACP virtual exhibition on American documentary photography in the 21st century. Juried by Dr. Rotem Rozental. $500 1st prize.
prose: Expand and Contract is the Los Angeles Center of Photography's recurring open-call series that uses contemporary themes to widen the conversation around photographic practice. The 2026 edition turns to American documentary photography, asking how America sees itself today — what it highlights, what it forgets, and what might be missing from the frame.

The juror is Dr. Rotem Rozental, LACP's Executive Director and Chief Curator. The selected works are presented in a virtual exhibition on LACP's website, running July 16 to October 16, 2026. The top three winners are also invited to show their work in an in-person component at LACP's DTLA gallery.

Prizes: 1st place receives $500 cash plus the in-person invitation; 2nd place $250 LACP gift card, a one-year LACP membership, and the in-person invitation; 3rd place $250 LACP gift card and the in-person invitation. Honorable mentions are placed in the online gallery for three months.

Submission is via Submittable. Fees are tiered: $25 for a single image up to $200 for 31–35 images. LACP members receive a 25% discount across all tiers. AI involvement beyond basic editing must be disclosed in the submission description; watermarks are not accepted. The deadline is June 16, 2026 at midnight PST; acceptances are announced June 30, 2026.

calls.title: The Illume Awards 2026
calls.description: Adventure and action sports photography awards, formerly Red Bull Illume, now operating as an independent contest with environmental NGO partners (Leave No Trace, World Bicycle Relief). Sixteen categories — eight sports (Adventure, Aerial, Bike, Climb, Skate, Snow, Surf, Trail) and eight themes (Close-Up, Emerging, Innovation, Lifestyle, Masterpiece, Playground, RAW, Spirit). Sixty international judges; 160 finalists are featured in the physical Illume Photobook and may be selected for the Illume Exhibit Tour. The overall winner is announced at a global awards ceremony in December 2026. Prizes from media partners include Leica cameras and Angelbird storage gear. Free to enter; open to all levels from amateur to professional. Since 2006 the contest has received nearly 250,000 submissions.
calls.summary: Adventure and action sports photography awards (formerly Red Bull Illume). Free entry, 16 categories, Leica prizes, photobook, exhibition tour.
prose: The Illume Awards is the new, independent continuation of what was Red Bull Illume — a long-running, high-profile competition focused on adventure and action sports photography. The 2026 edition is the first under the new branding, with an expanded environmental focus and partnerships with Leave No Trace and World Bicycle Relief.

There are sixteen categories total: eight sports — Adventure, Aerial, Bike, Climb, Skate, Snow, Surf, Trail — and eight themes — Close-Up, Emerging, Innovation, Lifestyle, Masterpiece, Playground, RAW, Spirit. Photographers can submit images to multiple categories. Sixty international judges review submissions.

160 finalists are featured in the physical Illume Photobook and may be selected for the Illume Exhibit Tour, which travels internationally. Prizes from media partners include Leica cameras and Angelbird storage gear. The overall winner is announced at a global awards ceremony in December 2026.

Submission is via the contest's website and is free. The competition is open globally to all levels, from amateur to professional. Since the first edition in 2006, the contest has received nearly 250,000 submissions. The deadline is July 31, 2026; semifinals and finalists are announced in fall 2026.

calls.title: Read Against the Machine — Arles 2026
calls.description: Der Greif × Foundation Manuel Rivera-Ortiz open call for Les Rencontres d'Arles 2026, themed Read Against the Machine. Invites work that resists automated interpretation and reclaims the social act of looking — how meaning is shaped through conversation rather than algorithms. 12–16 selected artists join an intensive collective image-reading workshop on July 8; an additional cohort is invited to 1:1 Face-to-Face portfolio reviews on July 10. All selected work is presented in a collective screening at the MRO Foundation during the festival. Applicants must already be attending Arles — travel and accommodation are not covered. Voluntary 15€ donation; vouchers available on request.
jury: Caroline von Courten, Artistic Director, Der Greif
Alejandro León Cannock, Artistic Director, MRO Foundation
Ilaria Sponda, Managing Editor, Der Greif
Francesca Hummler, Programme Curator, Der Greif
Diana Poole, Co-Founder, Der Greif Studio
Carolina Semprucci, Assistant Editor, Der Greif
calls.summary: Der Greif × MRO Arles 2026 workshop & 1:1 portfolio reviews. Group screening at MRO Foundation. PWYC; deadline 7 June 2026.
prose: Read Against the Machine is a Der Greif × Foundation Manuel Rivera-Ortiz collaboration for the 57th Rencontres d'Arles. The brief invites photographic work that resists automated interpretation and reclaims the social act of looking, asking what happens when meaning is shaped through conversation rather than algorithms.

The programme has two strands. 12–16 selected artists join a collaborative editing workshop on July 8 led by Der Greif's jury and MRO's Artistic Director Alejandro León Cannock — an intensive collective image-reading session. A separate cohort is invited to one-on-one Face-to-Face portfolio reviews on July 10 with Der Greif editors and an MRO guest reviewer.

All selected participants' work is included in a collective screening at the MRO Foundation during Arles, on July 10. The screening sits within the wider Rencontres programme and brings the workshop conversations into a public, communal viewing.

Submission is through Picter. The fee is voluntary, with a 15€ suggested donation; vouchers are available on request via voucher-special@dergreif.org. Applicants must already be attending Les Rencontres d'Arles — travel and accommodation are not covered. The deadline is June 7, 2026 at 11:59 PM CET.

calls.title: Queer Quintessential 2026
calls.description: Der Greif's Pride Month 2026 open call, initiated by queer Program Curator Francesca Hummler. Invites LGBTQIA+ lens-based artists to explore queer life, identity, intimacy, and forms of community through photography and image-based practices. Welcomes work engaging with self-representation, chosen family, visibility, and the relationship between public and private space. Selected artists featured in an online exhibition on Der Greif's homepage and invited to join small-group Face-to-Face critique sessions, with opportunities for future collaborations through Der Greif Studio. Voluntary submission fee with 10€ suggested donation; 50% or 100% discount vouchers available on request. Open globally.
jury: Francesca Hummler, Queer Program Curator, Der Greif
calls.summary: Pride Month open call for LGBTQIA+ lens-based artists. Online exhibition + Face-to-Face critique. PWYC; deadline 15 June 2026.
prose: Queer Quintessential is Der Greif's Pride Month 2026 open call, initiated by the platform's queer Program Curator Francesca Hummler. The brief invites LGBTQIA+ lens-based artists to explore queer life, identity, intimacy, and forms of community through photography and image-based practices.

The call welcomes work engaging with self-representation, chosen family, visibility, and the relationship between public and private space. Submissions are evaluated on artistic quality, conceptual clarity, openness to dialogue and process, and engagement with themes of identity and community.

Selected artists are featured in an online exhibition on Der Greif's homepage and invited to join small-group Face-to-Face critique sessions — direct conversation rather than written feedback. Selection also brings visibility within Der Greif's international community and possibilities for future collaboration through Der Greif Studio.

Submission is through Picter. The fee is voluntary (Pay-What-You-Can) with a 10€ suggested donation; financial-assistance vouchers for 50% or 100% discount are available by emailing voucher-special-2@dergreif.org. Eligibility is open globally to LGBTQIA+ lens-based artists. The deadline is June 15, 2026 at 11:59 PM CET.

calls.title: PhotoVogue Global Open Call 2026 — Brave New Visions
calls.description: PhotoVogue's annual global open call from Vogue Italia, themed Brave New Visions: Creativity as Rebellion. Photographers, video makers, and multimedia artists worldwide invited to submit work that responds to the present through a distinct visual language. All genres welcome — fashion, documentary, portraiture, fine art, experimental. $12,000 total in three grants: $6,000 Outstanding Vision Grant, $4,000 Vision Grant, $2,000 Rising Voice Grant. Selected artists are presented at the next PhotoVogue Festival, published across Vogue's global editions, and offered virtual portfolio reviews. Open May 14 – September 11, 2026.
calls.summary: PhotoVogue's 2026 global open call. $12,000 in three grants, festival exhibition, Vogue publication. Free; deadline 11 September 2026.
prose: PhotoVogue is the global photography platform run by Vogue Italia under editorial direction Alessia Glaviano. The Global Open Call is the platform's annual flagship, and the 2026 cycle is themed Brave New Visions: Creativity as Rebellion. PhotoVogue frames the brief as a stance rather than a subject — it is asking for work where the way the artist sees is itself an act of resistance against visual indifference, not adherence to a specified theme.

Three grants split $12,000: the Outstanding Vision Grant of $6,000 for an artist expanding the boundaries of visual language; the Vision Grant of $4,000 for an artist with a strong and singular perspective; and the Rising Voice Grant of $2,000 for an emerging artist showing clarity, originality, and promise. Selected artists are presented at the next PhotoVogue Festival in Milan, with the possibility of publication across Vogue's global editions and an invitation to PhotoVogue's Virtual Portfolio Reviews.

The call welcomes photography, video, and multimedia projects across all genres — fashion, documentary, portraiture, fine art, and experimental practice. Submissions may include up to 15 images, an optional 60-second video trailer, or a combination for multimedia projects. Artists must be 18 or older; AI-generated work is not eligible.

Submissions are free and hosted on Picter, open May 14 through September 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM CET. Contact for the call is Daniel Rodríguez-Gordillo at Condé Nast (daniel.rodriguez-gordillo@condenast.es).

calls.title: BWP x Nikon Grant Fund 2026 — Quarter 2
calls.description: Second-quarter 2026 cycle of the Black Women Photographers x Nikon $50K Grant Fund — a year-long program supporting Black women photographers globally through four quarterly grant opportunities. The Q2 recipient receives a $2,500 USD unrestricted cash grant plus a Nikon Z6III with 24-70mm f/4 lens kit. Funding can support photography projects, production, travel, equipment, or other professional needs. BWP is a global membership community founded in 2020 by Polly Irungu, with members across 60+ countries and 35 U.S. states. To date, the program has awarded over $230,000 in financial grants plus $80,000 in camera equipment. Applications for Q2 close June 5, 2026.
calls.summary: Quarterly grant for Black women photographers worldwide. $2,500 cash + Nikon Z6III kit. Q2 2026 cycle.
prose: Black Women Photographers (BWP) is a global community founded in 2020 by Polly Irungu — a Kenyan-American photo editor — to combat the underrepresentation of Black women photographers in the industry. BWP's membership directory now spans more than 60 countries and 35 U.S. states. The BWP x Nikon Grant Fund is the organization's flagship support program, structured as four quarterly grant cycles running across 2026.

Each quarterly recipient receives a $2,500 USD unrestricted cash grant plus a Nikon Z6III with 24-70mm f/4 lens kit. The funds carry no project restrictions — past recipients have used them for production, travel, gear replacement, studio setup, and other professional needs. The Q2 2026 deadline is June 5.

Eligibility is for Black women photographers globally, including emerging, independent, and professional practitioners as well as visual storytellers and content creators. There is no application fee. To date, the program has distributed more than $230,000 in cash grants and $80,000 in Nikon mirrorless gear across previous cycles.

Applications are submitted via the BWP grant fund page. The program is run jointly with Nikon USA and is one of the most consistent direct-funding initiatives for Black women photographers in the field.

calls.title: 2026 Black & White Award
calls.description: The Independent Photographer's monthly themed competition cycle, this round dedicated to black and white photography in any genre — landscape, portrait, street, documentary, or abstract — emphasizing mastery of light, composition, and shadow. Total prize pool $2,700: 1st prize $1,000, 2nd $600, 3rd $400, plus seven $100 finalist prizes. Winners exhibited internationally at PBC Gallery London and featured to the platform's 965k+ Instagram and 200k+ Facebook followers. All entrants receive a free online portfolio. Judge: Monica Denevan. Submissions are tiered: $15 for 1 image, $30 for 3, $45 for 6. AI-generated work not accepted; photography-based submissions only (film, digital, smartphone). JPEG or PNG, minimum 1200px longest side, maximum 10MB.
calls.summary: Black & white photography competition. $2,700 prize pool, PBC Gallery London exhibition. Judge: Monica Denevan.
prose: The Independent Photographer (TIP) is a London-based online photography platform that runs themed monthly competitions and publishes editorial work, interviews, and book reviews. The 2026 Black & White Award is the platform's monochrome-themed cycle, focused on mastery of light, composition, and shadow across any genre — landscape, portrait, street, documentary, or abstract.

Total prize pool is $2,700: first place receives $1,000, second $600, third $400, and seven runners-up receive $100 each. Winners are exhibited at PBC Gallery in London and featured across The Independent Photographer's Instagram (965k+ followers) and Facebook (200k+) channels. All entrants receive a free online portfolio on the platform.

Selection is by Monica Denevan, the American fine-art photographer known for her striking monochrome work in Burma and beyond. TIP's broader jury roster has historically included names like Steve McCurry, Ed Kashi, Maggie Steber, Magdalena Herrera, and Fiona Shields — useful context for emerging entrants weighing this competition against others at similar price points.

Eligibility is open globally. Submissions are tiered: $15 for one image, $30 for three, $45 for six. JPEG or PNG, minimum 1200 pixels on one side, maximum 10MB per file. AI-generated work is not accepted — photography-based submissions only, with film, digital, and smartphone all welcome. The final deadline is May 31, 2026.

calls.title: Passage Art-Residency-Programme 2026
calls.description: Four-week residency in Wittenberg, Germany in October 2026 for two photographers or filmmakers. €5,000 grant per resident plus four-week accommodation; additional €1,000 childcare supplement if accompanied by a child. Run by Polygona Kunstverein e.V. as part of the KOBRA Cultural Network Wittenberg. Two themes to choose from: Ferropolis (the historic Zschornewitz coal power station — energy history and industrial transformation) or RFB (Research Library of Reformation Studies — knowledge production and visual representation in historical scientific texts). On-site support from Polygona staff plus topic-specific expert guidance. Residents develop an artistic project, conduct a one-day workshop for young people, give a public artist talk, and contribute to documentary filming over two days. National and international artists welcome (18+); students not eligible. Submit 10 final project photographs by December 31, 2026. Jury decision announced from June 20, 2026.
calls.summary: 4-week residency in Wittenberg, Germany. €5,000 grant + accommodation. Themes: Ferropolis power station or Reformation archive.
prose: The Passage Art-Residency-Programme is run by Polygona Kunstverein e.V., a Wittenberg-based art association, as part of the KOBRA Cultural Network Wittenberg (2025–2029). The 2026 cycle offers two four-week residency positions in October at Wittenberg in Saxony-Anhalt, Germany — open to photographers and filmmakers, with no upper age limit and no application fee.

Each resident receives a €5,000 grant plus four weeks of accommodation. An additional €1,000 childcare supplement is available for residents accompanied by a child — a relatively rare provision among comparable programs. Travel, local transport, materials, and living expenses beyond the grant are applicant-funded.

Applicants choose between two research contexts. Theme One is Ferropolis — the historic Zschornewitz coal power station, framed around energy history and post-industrial transformation. Theme Two is the Research Library of Reformation Studies (RFB), framed around knowledge production and visual representation in historical scientific texts. The thematic structure means the program is best suited to artists with an existing or readily adaptable interest in industrial heritage or archive-based practice.

The residency carries program obligations beyond studio work: a one-day workshop for young people, a public artist talk, and two days of contributing to documentary filming. Selected artists also submit 10 final project photographs by December 31, 2026. Applications close May 30, 2026; the jury decision is announced from June 20.

calls.title: CCI Fellowships 2026
calls.description: Sixth annual cycle of fellowships from the Green Family Foundation Caribbean Cultural Institute (CCI) at Pérez Art Museum Miami (PAMM). Three parallel tracks: CCI Artist Fellowship (residency at Bakehouse Art Complex Miami for up to two months, stipend, travel, $4,000 production budget); CCI Research Fellowship (hybrid in-person/remote over four months, travel and two-week Miami residency covered, research stipend, up to $1,000 in research expenses); and CCI + WOPHA Fellowship — the photography track, open to emerging and mid-career women and nonbinary photographers from the Caribbean or its diaspora. The CCI + WOPHA Fellowship runs September through November 2026, hybrid format, with September residency at El Espacio 23 in Miami; includes stipend, $4,000 production funds, round-trip airfare if not Miami-based, plus mentorship and collaboration with Green Space Miami and FIU-LACC. Photographic practice is defined broadly: cameras and cameraless work, automated/computational processes, augmented photography, and image collecting/archiving/circulation. International applicants must secure their own visas — PAMM cannot sponsor.
calls.summary: Three CCI fellowships at Pérez Art Museum Miami. WOPHA photography track for women & nonbinary Caribbean photographers.
prose: The Green Family Foundation Caribbean Cultural Institute (CCI) is the Caribbean-focused research and curatorial arm of Pérez Art Museum Miami (PAMM). The 2026 fellowships are the program's sixth annual cycle, run across three parallel tracks: CCI Artist Fellowship, CCI Research Fellowship, and CCI + WOPHA Fellowship — the photography-specific track operated jointly with Women Photographers International Archive (WOPHA).

The CCI + WOPHA Fellowship is reserved for emerging and mid-career women and nonbinary photographers from the Caribbean or its diaspora. The fellowship runs September through November 2026 in hybrid format, with the in-person residency component held at El Espacio 23 in Miami during September. Funding includes a stipend, up to $4,000 in production funds, and round-trip airfare for non-Miami-based fellows. Mentorship and collaboration opportunities extend through Green Space Miami and the FIU Latin American and Caribbean Center (FIU-LACC).

The brief's definition of photographic practice is deliberately expansive: image-making with or without cameras, automated and computational processes, augmented photography, and the collecting, archiving, and circulation of images. The framing fits both traditional photographic projects and research-led or post-photographic work.

All three CCI fellowships share a June 1, 2026 deadline (11:59 PM EDT) and require a 500-word cover letter, CV, 500-word artist statement, 1,000-word project proposal with budget and timeline, and a portfolio. Application is free. International applicants must secure their own visas — PAMM cannot sponsor.

calls.title: Photography+ Emerging Talent 2026
calls.description: Open call for the Emerging Talent issue of Photography+, Photoworks' online magazine. Open to BA and MA graduates, plus image-based artists within the first five years of their practice and/or graduation. Ten awardees featured in the next Photography+ issue; all 10 included in an evening projection at Kranj Foto Fest. One selected artist receives a one-year Photoworks membership plus curatorial and editorial mentoring. A second selected artist receives a £200 printing voucher from Spectrum Photographic and an Instagram takeover. Submit up to 15 images from a single project plus a 200-word artist statement via Picter; one project per applicant. Free to enter. Jury: Emma Bowkett (Director of Photography, Financial Times), Louise Fedotov-Clements (Director, Photoworks), Fernanda Prado Verčič (Founding Director, Kranj Foto Fest), Maryam Wahid (Head of Programs and Outreach, Tasweer Photography Festival), and Amin Yousefi (Assistant Curator and Editor, Photography+). Funded by Photoworks, Spectrum Photographic, and Picter.
jury: Emma Bowkett, Director of Photography, Financial Times
Fernanda Prado Verčič, Founding Director, Kranj Foto Fest
Maryam Wahid, Head of Programs and Outreach, Tasweer Photography Festival
Amin Yousefi, Assistant Curator and Editor, Photography+
calls.summary: 10 awardees featured in Photography+ magazine and Kranj Foto Fest projection. BA/MA grads or first 5 years of practice.
prose: Photoworks is the UK photography agency based in Brighton — a major commissioning, publishing, and development organization for photography in Britain. Photography+ is the agency's online magazine, and the Emerging Talent issue is its annual open-call edition dedicated to early-career image-makers. The 2026 cycle is open to BA and MA graduates and to image-based artists within the first five years of their practice and/or graduation.

Ten awardees are selected. All ten are featured in the next Photography+ issue and included in an evening projection at Kranj Foto Fest in Slovenia. Two additional awards are layered on top: one selected artist receives a one-year Photoworks membership plus curatorial and editorial mentoring; a second receives a £200 printing voucher from Spectrum Photographic and an Instagram takeover.

The 2026 jury is Emma Bowkett (Director of Photography, Financial Times), Louise Fedotov-Clements (Director, Photoworks), Fernanda Prado Verčič (Founding Director, Kranj Foto Fest), Maryam Wahid (Head of Programs and Outreach, Tasweer Photography Festival), and Amin Yousefi (Assistant Curator and Editor, Photography+). The panel mixes editorial, institutional, and festival-side perspectives — useful for emerging photographers thinking about where their work fits next.

Applications are made through Picter: up to 15 images from a single project plus a 200-word artist statement. Only one project per applicant. The call is free to enter. The deadline is June 15, 2026 at 11:59 PM. Program funding comes from Photoworks, Spectrum Photographic, and Picter.

calls.title: No Theme Open Call 2026
calls.description: Open theme — any subject matter or photographic medium (digital, film, alternative process). No generative AI. 30–45 pieces selected for in-person gallery exhibition at Oakland Photo Workshop, plus 10–20 additional for online exhibition. Eligibility restricted to Bay Area artists 18+. Opening reception August 7, 2026, 6–9 PM. Submission fee waivers available on request; fees support the gallery and a scholarship fund for printing and framing. Submissions reviewed blind. Framed work cannot exceed 24 inches wide.
calls.summary: Open-theme show at Oakland Photo Workshop. 30–45 in-person + 10–20 online. Bay Area artists. Opening Aug 7, 2026.
prose: East Bay Photo Collective (EBPCO) is an Oakland-based photography nonprofit founded in 2017, operating the Oakland Photo Workshop gallery in Chinatown and a darkroom in downtown Oakland. The mission centers on access — facilities, education, and community for East Bay photographers, including those who are under-served or without a creative community elsewhere. The Oakland Photo Workshop gallery has shown over 200 local artists since opening in 2021.

The No Theme Open Call is EBPCO's annual open-theme exhibition — any subject, any photographic medium (digital, film, alternative process) — with one process restriction: generative AI is not accepted. The brief is deliberately broad to surface the range of Bay Area practice rather than steer toward a single mood or genre.

Selection structure: 30 to 45 pieces are chosen for the in-person gallery exhibition at Oakland Photo Workshop (312 8th St., Oakland), plus an additional 10 to 20 for the online exhibition. The opening reception is August 7, 2026, from 6 to 9 PM. Submissions are reviewed blind by volunteer jurors.

Eligibility is geographic: artists must be 18 or older and based in or around the Bay Area — this is a regional show by design. Submission is through Artwork Archive: up to 3 images for $35, or $20 for students and low-income artists. Fee waivers are available on request — emailing info@ebpco.org. Framed work cannot exceed 24 inches wide. The deadline is May 21, 2026 at 11:59 PM.

calls.title: MUUS Collection Research Fellowship 2026
calls.description: Inaugural research fellowship from the MUUS Collection, a New York-area photography archive holding nearly half a million images from the archives of André de Dienes, Fred W. McDarrah, Larry Fink, Rosalind Fox Solomon, Deborah Turbeville, and Alfred Wertheimer. $20,000 grant to one curator or academic to spend time in the archives and the new MUUSEUM Research Portal developing an exhibition or publication concept. Travel costs to the archive fully covered as part of the grant. Mentorship from an advisory board of leading curators and directors. Grant runs November 2026–November 2027. Winner announced at Paris Photo in October 2026. Open globally to curators and academics.
jury: Mark Sealy OBE, Executive Director, Autograph ABP
Sophie Wright, Executive Director, MUUS Collection
calls.summary: $20,000 grant for a curator or academic to develop an exhibition or publication using MUUS Collection's archives. Travel covered.
prose: The MUUS Collection is an American 20th-century photography collection based just outside Manhattan, holding nearly half a million images and supporting ephemera — contact sheets, personal papers, manuscripts, and publications. The current archives include the work of André de Dienes, Larry Fink, Fred W. McDarrah (the downtown New York scene, Dylan, Ginsberg, Warhol, and the Stonewall Uprising), Rosalind Fox Solomon, Deborah Turbeville, and Alfred Wertheimer.

The Research Fellowship is the Collection's inaugural grant program, launched in 2026. One $20,000 grant is awarded to a curator or academic for time in the physical archives and on the new MUUSEUM Research Portal, with the goal of producing an exhibition or publication concept drawn from the holdings. The grant covers travel to the archive in full, separately from the cash award.

The fellowship runs November 2026 through November 2027, with mentorship sessions across the year from the advisory board: Nathalie Herschdorfer (Director, Photo Elysée), Sarah Meister (Executive Director, Aperture), Paul Roth (Director, Image Centre), Mark Sealy OBE (Executive Director, Autograph ABP), and Sophie Wright (Executive Director, MUUS Collection).

Eligibility is restricted to curators and academics — this is a research grant, not an artist's fellowship. Applications open May 1 and close July 31, 2026. The winner is decided in October 2026 and announced publicly at Paris Photo in November.

calls.title: LUMINEX 4.0
calls.description: Fourth edition of LUMINEX, NOW Art's outdoor art and technology exhibition in Los Angeles. Open call for artists working at the intersection of art, light, and technology. Selected artists receive a $1,000 stipend plus production fees based on approved project. Free to apply.
calls.summary: Outdoor art and technology exhibition in Los Angeles. $1,000 stipend per artist plus production support based on approved project.
prose: LUMINEX is an outdoor art and technology exhibition staged in Los Angeles, produced by NOW Art — the LA-based public art organization. The 2026 cycle is the program's fourth edition (LUMINEX 4.0).

The brief is positioned at the intersection of art, light, and technology — projection, immersive installation, and light-based work made for public outdoor space rather than gallery interiors. The audience is the city itself.

The financial structure is two-part rather than a single award. Each selected artist receives a $1,000 stipend. Production fees are negotiated separately based on the approved project — so an ambitious installation can be resourced beyond the stipend, while a simpler proposal stays lean. The split lets the organization fund work at different scales without forcing a flat budget.
Eligibility is open. Application is free.
Submission is through the Fillout RFP at nowart.fillout.com/luminex4. The 2026 deadline is June 5 at 11:59 PM PST.

calls.title: SlowExposures 2026 — Photography of the Rural South
calls.description: 20th annual Main Exhibition of contemporary photography of the American South. Submissions must be made in 16 Southern US states (AL, AR, DE, FL, GA, KY, LA, MD, MS, NC, OK, SC, TN, TX, VA, WV). Up to 6 images. Selected work shown September 18–20, 2026 at the historic R.F. Strickland Building in Concord, GA, then travels to Cochran Gallery in LaGrange, GA. Jurors Dennis Kiel and Coco Conroy.
calls.summary: 20th SlowExposures festival's Main Exhibition. Photography made in 16 Southern US states. Concord, GA. Up to 6 images.
prose: SlowExposures is a long-running annual photography festival in Pike County, Georgia dedicated to images of the contemporary American South. Founded in 2003 and now in its 20th year, the festival anchors a weekend of exhibitions, talks, and the popular PopUp Tour in and around the small town of Concord.

The 2026 Main Exhibition is regionally focused: photographs must be made in one of sixteen Southern states — Alabama, Arkansas, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maryland, Mississippi, North Carolina, Oklahoma, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Virginia, or West Virginia. The brief invites work that captures the diversity, contradictions, and complexity of the South rather than a fixed theme.

Selected images — typically 70 to 90 prints — are displayed at the historic R.F. Strickland Building in downtown Concord during the festival weekend, September 18–20, 2026, then move on to a month-long run at the Cochran Gallery in LaGrange, Georgia.

Jurors for the 2026 edition are Dennis Kiel and Coco Conroy. The entry fee is $50 for up to six images and underwrites venue rental, juror expenses, receptions, publicity, and awards. All entrants — selected or not — are invited as honored guests to the private Soiree on Friday night at Split Oak Farm.

calls.title: Focus 2026 — Atlanta Photography Group
calls.description: Open-themed juried exhibition for APG members based in Georgia. Juror Anne Leighton Massoni, Executive Director of the Houston Center for Photography. 2 to 8 images per entry. Exhibition runs July 21 – August 21, 2026 at the APG Gallery on Piedmont Avenue in Atlanta, with an opening reception July 23. The $1,000 APG/MOCA GA Purchase Award adds the winning work to the Museum of Contemporary Art of Georgia's permanent collection.
jury: Anne Leighton Massoni, Executive Director, Houston Center for Photography
calls.summary: APG's open-themed juried show. $1,000 MOCA GA purchase award + permanent collection. Members-only, Georgia artists.
prose: Atlanta Photography Group (APG) is a long-standing nonprofit photography organization in Atlanta, Georgia, with its own gallery on Piedmont Avenue. Focus is APG's open-themed juried members' exhibition, programmed annually to recognize work by Georgia photographers.

The 2026 juror is Anne Leighton Massoni, Executive Director of the Houston Center for Photography, who selects from across the open-themed submissions without a prescribed subject. Eligibility is restricted to APG members who are based in Georgia, and to artists whose work hasn't appeared in APG's Main or Maloof galleries within the past three years.

Selected work is exhibited July 21 through August 21, 2026 at the APG gallery at 1544 Piedmont Avenue NE, Atlanta, with an opening reception on July 23. The top award is the $1,000 APG / Museum of Contemporary Art of Georgia Purchase Award, with the winning work entering MOCA GA's permanent collection.

Entries accept 2 to 8 images. Fees scale by submission window: $35–$75 early (May 7–15), $40–$85 regular (May 16–31), $50–$95 late (June 1–5), with reduced student rates of $30–$70. The deadline is June 5, 2026 at midnight Eastern.

calls.title: Light on Cut Paper: Photography & Collage
calls.description: Third in a NOPA series exploring the intersection of photography and collage. Seeks artists who collage their own photographs, make photomontage, or use a collage-like process in composition or in the darkroom. Selected work exhibited June 10 – July 10, 2026 at the NOPA gallery in New Orleans. 60/40 sales split (artist/gallery). Juror Jan Kather.
calls.summary: Third in a NOPA series at the intersection of photography and collage. Photomontage, darkroom collage, hybrid composition. New Orleans.
prose: The New Orleans Photo Alliance (NOPA) is a long-running nonprofit photography organization in New Orleans, Louisiana that runs themed juried exhibitions, the Michael P. Smith Fund for documentary photography, and educational programs. "Light on Cut Paper: Photography & Collage" is the third call in a NOPA series focused on artwork at the intersection of photography and collage.

The brief is medium-specific: work by artists who collage their own photographs, make photomontage, or use a collage-like process — whether in the composition of photographs or in the darkroom itself. Applicants must submit a brief statement explaining how the work demonstrates this intersection rather than only sending images. NOPA states openness to any work where the artist feels the image speaks to this hybrid practice.

Selected work is exhibited June 10 through July 10, 2026 at the NOPA gallery. The gallery takes 40% commission on sales; artists receive 60%. All work must be delivered framed and ready to hang by June 5, 2026 — international shipping logistics are the artist's responsibility.

Juror is Jan Kather, with notifications sent May 18, 2026. The deadline is May 12, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. MDT. Entry fees: $25 for NOPA members, $35 for non-members; combined membership-plus-entry options are also available.

Eligibility is international; all ages welcome; NOPA membership is not required to apply. Image specs: 1 to 5 images per entry, JPEG/JPG, under 5MB, minimum 1200 pixels on the longest side. Digitally manipulated photographs are permitted; AI-generated photographs are not accepted.

calls.title: SHOTS Magazine #172 — The Human Figure
calls.description: Fall 2026 issue (#172) of the black & white photography quarterly, in print since 1986. Theme is the human figure — no need to be literal. Submit up to 8 grayscale images at 300ppi (color files converted to B&W upon receipt). Free for current/renewing subscribers; $25 for non-subscribers ($28 international). All processes, formats, and experience levels welcome. All submitting artists receive a complimentary copy of the issue. Initial selection by editor Elizabeth Flinsch.
calls.summary: B&W photography quarterly since 1986. Issue #172 themed The Human Figure. Up to 8 grayscale images. Free for subscribers.
prose: SHOTS Magazine is a black-and-white photography quarterly that has been in print since 1986 — long-running among indie B&W publications. The 2026 fall issue is #172, themed The Human Figure.
The brief leaves room: human figure does not need to be literal. The selection welcomes interpretations that bend or abstract the figure rather than restricting to traditional portraiture or nudes.

The publication is process-restricted: black-and-white only. Submitted color files are converted to grayscale on receipt — applicants should consider how their work translates rather than assume color information will carry.

All processes, formats, and experience levels are welcome. All submitting artists receive a complimentary copy of the issue regardless of selection — a small but meaningful gesture for a paid-subscription publication.

Initial selection is by editor Elizabeth Flinsch, with publisher Douglas Beasley involved. Submission is through the SHOTS website with up to 8 grayscale images at 300 ppi. Submission is free for current and renewing subscribers; $25 for non-subscribers ($28 international). The 2026 deadline is June 1.

calls.title: Collection 2026 - Decode Gallery
calls.description: Decode Gallery's open-theme exhibition — no themes, no limits. At least 26 images selected. Selected artists receive complimentary professional printing on Epson printers with Ultra Premium Luster paper, museum-quality framing and matting handled by the gallery. 50% commission on sales. Open worldwide to all skill levels. Exhibition August 1–29, 2026 in Tucson, AZ. Juror: Holly Hart, Decode Gallery founder.
jury: Holly Hart, Conceptual Fine Art Photographer & Decode Gallery Founder
calls.summary: Open-theme show — no themes, no limits. 26+ selected. Free pro printing on Epson + museum framing. Tucson, AZ.
prose: Decode Gallery is a Tucson, Arizona photography gallery founded by conceptual fine art photographer Holly Hart, who also serves as juror for the gallery's calls. "Collection 2026" is the gallery's open-theme exhibition — no themes, no subject restrictions, no limits beyond technical quality.

The selection structure is generous: at least 26 images are selected for the physical exhibition. What's unusual: the gallery covers all professional printing on Epson printers with Ultra Premium Luster paper, plus museum-quality framing in 22×22 inch white frames with precut white mats — the artist provides only the high-resolution JPEG. Prints are retained in the gallery's flat files for two years after the exhibition for further promotion and sales.

Sales terms split commission 50/50 between artist and gallery. Selected work is also promoted across Decode's website, social media, and editorial publications. The 2026 exhibition runs August 1 through 29 in Tucson.

Entry fee is $40 for up to 5 images. Eligibility is open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers at all skill levels. The deadline is June 27, 2026; selected artists are notified within two weeks of the deadline.

calls.title: SE Center for Photography — The Art of Architecture
calls.description: Virtual juried exhibition seeking architectural photography in all forms — urban or rural, B&W or color, analog, digital or antique processes. Juror Michael Pannier (fine art photographer based in Greenville, SC) selects 35–40 images for the virtual gallery. Selected artists receive a portfolio review with the juror. 0% commission on sales. All photographers regardless of location, age, or skill level.
calls.summary: Virtual show on architectural photography — urban, rural, analog or digital. Juror: Michael Pannier. Portfolio review.
prose: The Southeast Center for Photography (SEC4P) is a Greenville, South Carolina photography organization (104 S Main St, Suite 841) that runs themed virtual juried exhibitions. "The Art of Architecture" is the center's open call for architectural photography in all forms — urban or rural, black-and-white or color, analog, digital, or antique processes.

The 2026 cycle is juried by Michael Pannier, a Greenville-based fine art photographer with thirty years' practice. Selection takes 35 to 40 images for an approximately one-month virtual gallery, with social media promotion across SEC4P's Facebook, Instagram, and X channels and an archived online slideshow plus video walkthrough. Selected artists also receive a portfolio review with the SEC4P director.
Entry fees: $35 for non-members for up to 5 images ($6 each additional, max 15), or $28 / $5 for SEC4P members. There is no sales commission.

Eligibility is open to all photographers regardless of location, age, or skill level. Work previously exhibited at SEC4P within the prior two years is ineligible. The 2026 deadline is July 1; results are announced July 15.

calls.title: Ethereal
calls.description: Seeking images that explore the intangible — works that evoke lightness, transience, and the space between what is seen and what is felt. Both traditional and experimental photographic processes welcome. Juror: John Horowitz, photographer and curator whose work resides in Purdue University's permanent collection. Exhibition June 5 – July 1, 2026 at A Photographer's Place in Raleigh, NC. Opening reception June 5, 7–9 PM.
calls.summary: Images that explore the intangible — lightness, transience, the space between seen and felt. Juror: John Horowitz.
prose: A Photographer's Place is a Raleigh, North Carolina photography gallery and printing studio. "Ethereal" is the gallery's themed call exploring the intangible — work that evokes lightness, transience, and the space between what is seen and what is felt. The brief is interpretive: both traditional and experimental photographic processes are welcome.

The exhibition runs June 5 through July 1, 2026, with an opening reception on June 5 from 7 to 9 PM. Selection is by John Horowitz, a working photographer and curator with work held in Purdue University's permanent collection.

Selected artists may optionally have their work printed at the gallery on the Canon ImagePROGRAF Pro-1100 (the gallery's in-house printer) for an additional fee — an unusually integrated offering for an open-call exhibition.

Entry fee is $35 for up to 5 images. Eligibility is open to photographers of all skill levels. Submissions are JPEGs at minimum 3,000 pixels on the longest side, color or black and white, with titles for each image. Submissions go through Smarter Entry. The 2026 deadline is May 22; juror selections announced May 25; work delivery June 3; exhibition opens June 5.

calls.title: Critical Mass 2026
calls.fee: $65 early bird / $75 regular; +$200 if Top 200 finalist
calls.description: Photolucida's annual program connecting photographers with the international photography community. Submit 10 images for pre-screening; approximately 200 finalists are then reviewed by up to 200 photography professionals worldwide — curators, gallerists, publishers, editors, educators, and media. The Top 50 are announced each year, alongside book awards and exhibition opportunities. Past finalists have gained acquisitions, exhibitions, and publication features. Open to photographers at any career stage. AI-generated imagery is not accepted for the 2026 cycle.
calls.summary: Photolucida's annual review by 200 photography pros. Top 50 designation, book awards, exhibition opportunities. AI not accepted.
prose: Critical Mass is Photolucida's flagship annual program, structured as a two-stage portfolio review by an unusually large jury. Photographers submit a 10-image portfolio; approximately 200 are advanced to a finalist round, where they are reviewed by up to 200 photography professionals from around the world — curators, gallerists, publishers, editors, educators, and journalists. The wide-jury format means each finalist's portfolio reaches roughly 200 industry-side viewers regardless of whether they place in the top 50.

From the finalist pool, the Top 50 designation is announced each year alongside book awards and exhibition opportunities. Past Critical Mass finalists have used the program to secure acquisitions, gallery representation, monograph publications, and editorial features — the value is partly the awards but more often the introduction itself.

Entry fees are tiered: $65 early-bird (June 1–9, 2026) or $75 regular (June 10 through July 1, 2026). Photographers who advance to the Top 200 finalist round pay an additional $200 to remain in the running.

Eligibility is open to photographers at any career stage. AI-generated imagery is explicitly excluded for the 2026 cycle. Photolucida itself is a Portland, Oregon-based non-profit. The 2026 deadline is July 1 at noon Eastern Time.

calls.title: Immagini e trame d'acqua — Le Stanze della Fotografia Open Call
calls.description: Inaugural open call from Fondazione Le Stanze della Fotografia (Venice) and the Association for the Heritage of the Prosecco Hills of Conegliano and Valdobbiadene, gathering testimonies, stories, and reflections on water as a force and necessity within cultural and landscape heritage. The project starts from the UNESCO World Heritage Prosecco Hills but invites participants to explore the theme in relation to other heritage sites in Italy and worldwide. Two participation formats: a photography-and-text project (3–10 images plus a narrative text up to three pages) or a video-story (max 2 minutes combining images, words, and sound). Submissions made by email; participants must also publish their work on their own social channels tagging the promoters. Three awards per category — Best Visual Narrative, Best Language/Experimentation, and Special Mention for Under-30/Students. Selected works exhibited at Le Stanze della Fotografia and gathered in a brochure distributed at the foundation's bookshop. Open to citizens, students, photographers, videomakers, and storytelling enthusiasts of any age and nationality.
jury: Denis Curti, Photography critic and curator
Marina Montedoro, President, Association for the Heritage of the Prosecco Hills
calls.summary: Free open call from Venice's Le Stanze della Fotografia on water in cultural & landscape heritage. Photography+text or video.
prose: Le Stanze della Fotografia is a Venice-based photography foundation, located on the Isola di San Giorgio Maggiore opposite St Mark's Square, run jointly with the Fondazione Giorgio Cini. Its inaugural open call "Immagini e trame d'acqua" — Italian for "images and weavings of water" — is organized in partnership with the Association for the Heritage of the Prosecco Hills of Conegliano and Valdobbiadene (the UNESCO World Heritage site north of Venice) and Marsilio Arte.

The brief is open in scope: water as a force and a necessity within cultural and landscape heritage, anchored by the Prosecco Hills but extending to any heritage site in Italy or abroad. Two submission formats: a photography-and-text project (3 to 10 images plus a narrative up to three pages) or a video-story (maximum two minutes combining images, words, and sound). There is no entry fee, and the call is open to citizens, students, photographers, videomakers, and storytelling enthusiasts of any age and nationality, individually or in collectives.

Three awards are given per category: Best Visual Narrative, Best Language and Experimentation, and a Special Mention for Under-30 entrants and students. Selected work is exhibited at Le Stanze della Fotografia and gathered in a brochure distributed through the foundation's bookshop and partner cultural venues. The jury includes photographer Maurizio Galimberti, photography critic and curator Denis Curti, writers Antonio G. Bortoluzzi and Sabrina Zuccato, and Marina Montedoro, president of the Heritage Association. Submissions close September 30, 2026; winners are announced within twenty days.

calls.title: EXPOSURE 2026 — 30th Annual Members' Juried Exhibition
calls.description: Photographic Resource Center's 30th annual members' juried exhibition. Twelve photographers selected to exhibit three works each. Juried by Audrey Lee Sands, Richard L. Menschel Associate Curator of Photography at Harvard Art Museums. Exhibition runs July 31 – September 6, 2026 at University Hall, Lesley University in Cambridge, MA. Applicants must be PRC members through September. Awards: Juror's Choice Award ($200) and two PRC Choice Awards ($100 each).
calls.summary: PRC Boston's 30th annual members' juried show. 12 photographers × 3 works. Juried by Audrey Lee Sands of Harvard Art Museums.
jury: Audrey Lee Sands, Richard L. Menschel Associate Curator of Photography, Harvard Art Museums
prose: The Photographic Resource Center (PRC) is a Boston-area photography organization that has run its annual members' juried exhibition for thirty years (the 2026 cycle marks the 30th edition). The show is hosted at University Hall, Lesley University in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

The 2026 cycle is juried by Audrey Lee Sands, the Richard L. Menschel Associate Curator of Photography at the Harvard Art Museums. Twelve photographers are selected from the membership pool, with each chosen photographer exhibiting three works.

Cash awards: a Juror's Choice Award of $200 and two PRC Choice Awards of $100 each. Beyond cash, the exhibition runs July 31 through September 6, 2026 at the Lesley University venue, with selected work catalogued by PRC.
Eligibility is restricted to PRC members through September. The application fee is $35. Submissions go through a Google Form. The 2026 deadline is June 15.

calls.title: Vermont Center for Photography Artist Residency 2026
calls.description: Inaugural artist residency at Vermont Center for Photography (VCP) in Brattleboro, VT. Two-week residency from October 23 to November 6, 2026. Open to photographers and lens-based artists at any career stage, working in analog, digital, or hybrid formats. Priority for artists who would benefit from darkroom and digital lab access, have a focused project proposal, and face barriers to creating elsewhere. Includes 24/7 access to VCP's darkroom, digital lab, and lighting studio; a $500 creation stipend; 14-night stay at the historic Latchis Hotel (4-minute walk from VCP); and a one-month solo exhibition in the Picker Print Gallery.
calls.summary: Inaugural 2-week residency at VCP Brattleboro. Darkroom and digital lab access, $500 stipend, hotel stay, and solo exhibition.
prose: The Vermont Center for Photography (VCP) is launching an inaugural residency program in 2026, based at the center's facility in Brattleboro, Vermont (10 Green Street). The residency runs two weeks — October 23 through November 6, 2026 — with the resident receiving a $500 creation stipend, a 14-night stay at the nearby Latchis Hotel (a four-minute walk from VCP), and 24/7 access to the center's darkroom, digital lab, and lighting studio.

The residency culminates in a one-month solo exhibition at the Picker Print Gallery within VCP, with an opening reception on November 7, 2026. The combination of facilities access, accommodation, modest stipend, and built-in solo show distinguishes the program from purely studio-based residencies — the work made during the residency moves directly to gallery walls.

Eligibility is open to photographers and lens-based artists at any career stage working in analog, digital, or hybrid processes. The selection committee gives priority to applicants who would benefit from VCP's specialized equipment or who face barriers to similar facilities elsewhere — financial, spatial, or technical.

The application fee is $25 ($15 for VCP members). Applications require a CV/résumé, project proposal, and 10 to 15 work samples. The deadline is June 30, 2026 (11:59 PM EST), with notifications sent July 31, 2026.

calls.title: Wild & Free — SaveArtSpace Billboard Exhibition
calls.description: Public art exhibition on billboard ad space throughout New York City, curated by Gigi Chen, a contemporary wildlife-focused artist and nature photographer. Theme explores the close connection between nature, mythology, and civilization — how the natural world coexists with urban environments. Open to artists of all ages and backgrounds. Selected works displayed on NYC billboards for at least one month starting June 26, 2026. SaveArtSpace is a non-profit that has run public art billboard exhibitions since 2015.
calls.prize: Public billboard exhibition (1+ month) in NYC
calls.summary: NYC public art billboard exhibition curated by Gigi Chen. Theme: nature, mythology, and civilization. Opens June 26, 2026.
prose: SaveArtSpace is a non-profit organization that has run public art billboard exhibitions since 2015. The format is unusual: rather than traditional gallery shows, SaveArtSpace places artists' work on commercial billboard advertising space across New York City for at least one month per exhibition.

"Wild & Free" is curated by Gigi Chen, a contemporary wildlife-focused artist and nature photographer. The theme explores the close connection between nature, mythology, and civilization — work that examines how the natural world coexists with urban environments, or how mythology mediates the human-nature relationship.

Selected works are displayed on NYC billboards for at least one month starting June 26, 2026. The format gives artists exposure to a much larger audience than gallery shows reach — billboards in commercial Manhattan and outer-borough corridors are seen by hundreds of thousands of pedestrians and drivers daily.

Eligibility is open to artists of all ages and backgrounds. The program is structured as a tax-deductible donation model rather than a competitive entry fee — submission costs are $35 for 1 to 3 images, $10 for each additional image, with the fees treated as charitable contributions to the non-profit.
Submissions go through JotForm. The 2026 application window runs March 30 through May 11; selected artists are announced after May 25.

calls.title: The Printmaker and the Photographic Image: Dissolving Media Boundaries
calls.description: International juried exhibition for printmakers and photographers working in both traditions. Seeks hand-printed imagery that weds photographic elements with printmaking techniques — cyanotype, photogravure, photopolymer, photocollage, and other alternative processes especially welcome. Final image must be a hand-pulled print; no solely digital output. Successful images should display technical sophistication while conveying emotional valence. Exhibition June 19 – August 1, 2026 at Remarque Print Workshop & Gallery in Albuquerque, New Mexico. Maximum paper size 16×20". Accepted works must arrive by June 4, 2026. 50/50 commission on sales.
calls.summary: Hand-pulled prints combining photographic and printmaking techniques. Cyanotype, photogravure, photopolymer welcome. Albuquerque exhibition.
prose: Remarque Print Workshop & Gallery is an Albuquerque, New Mexico printmaking facility — distinct from a typical photography gallery in that the venue centers around traditional printmaking infrastructure (etching presses, lithography stones, screenprinting setup, photopolymer plate work). "The Printmaker and the Photographic Image: Dissolving Media Boundaries" is the gallery's themed call for hybrid work that combines photographic processes with traditional printmaking.

Eligible techniques are specifically those that produce hand-pulled prints: cyanotype, photogravure, photopolymer, photocollage, and other alternative processes that combine photographic elements with printmaking. The brief is explicit: "the final image must be a hand-pulled print; no solely digital output." Selection criteria favor work that demonstrates technical sophistication while conveying emotional valence.
The exhibition runs June 19 through August 1, 2026 at Remarque in Albuquerque. Sales are split 50/50 between artist and gallery.

Entry fee is $35 (non-refundable) for up to 3 images. Maximum paper size 16×20" or 20×16". Eligibility is open internationally. Submissions go through CaFÉ. The 2026 deadline is May 10 at 11:59 PM MDT; artists notified by May 19; accepted works due June 4.

calls.title: Conversaciones — EMC Magazine Print Edition Open Call
calls.description: Open call for the printed edition of Conversaciones, EMC Magazine's photography open call returning in a new format after three virtual editions. The editorial team seeks images that speak to each other. Free theme. Up to 5 images per participant, analog or digital, submitted via WeTransfer at low resolution for selection and high-resolution TIFF (300 dpi, RGB) if accepted. Open worldwide to photographers of any nationality. Selected participants receive one printed copy of the magazine; international participants cover shipping. Authors retain intellectual property; EMC Magazine receives non-exclusive usage rights for this printed edition. Publication planned for July 2026.
calls.summary: Argentine indie photo magazine's printed edition open call. Free theme, $5 USD international fee, July 2026 publication.
prose: EMC Magazine is an Argentine independent photography publication based in Buenos Aires. "Conversaciones" is the magazine's recurring open call program — the 2026 cycle returns in a new printed format after three earlier virtual editions. The editorial premise is in the title: the editors are seeking images that speak to each other across the issue's pages, with selection emphasizing visual dialogue rather than thematic cohesion.

There is no thematic restriction on submitted work. Each participant submits up to 5 images, analog or digital, with no requirement that images be previously unpublished. Submissions go through WeTransfer at low resolution for review; high-resolution TIFF files (300 dpi, RGB) are required if accepted, named in the format Name_Lastname_01.

Selection is by the EMC Magazine editorial team. Selected participants receive one printed copy of the magazine. International participants cover their own shipping costs. Authors retain intellectual property; EMC Magazine receives non-exclusive usage rights for this printed edition only.

Entry fees are split by region to reflect Argentina's economy: 5,000 Argentine pesos for Argentina residents (paid via Mercado Pago), USD $5 for international participants (paid via PayPal). Payment is non-refundable and does not guarantee selection — the editors stress this explicitly.

Submissions must be original work owned by the photographer; if recognizable people appear in images, participants must secure consent. The 2026 deadline is May 15; the printed magazine publishes July 2026.

calls.title: ESC 2036 — 0—1 Gallery Open Call
calls.description: 0—1 Gallery's annual open call inviting artists to imagine roughly ten years ahead, keeping in mind the pressure points of now — climate, extraction, technology, and what it means to remain human inside all that. Looking for works that speak of nature, technology, or human existence — from subtle gestures to monumental systems. All forms welcome including photography, new media, painting, sculpture, installation, performance, sound, graphics, video, mixed media, AR/VR, and writing. No entry fees; submit one link to portfolio, website, or project page. Open to everyone — artists at any stage from any place; age, gender, location, and background not used as filters. Selected artists included in a curated group exhibition in the Netherlands in 2026–2027 with additional visibility through 0—1's website and social media.
calls.summary: Free open call from The Hague gallery. Theme: nature, tech & humanity ten years ahead. Curated group exhibition 2026–2027.
prose: 0—1 Gallery is a contemporary art gallery in The Hague, Netherlands. "ESC 2036" is the gallery's annual open call inviting artists to imagine roughly ten years ahead — keeping in mind the pressure points of now: climate, extraction, technology, and what it means to remain human inside all of that.

The brief is interpretive and broad: nature, technology, or human existence in any combination. Subtle gestures and monumental systems are equally welcome — the call doesn't favor either intimate or large-scale work, only that it engage with the future-projecting frame.

All forms are eligible: photography, new media, painting, sculpture, installation, performance, sound, graphics, video, mixed media, AR/VR, and writing. The call is unusually inclusive in describing eligibility — "open to everyone" with age, gender, location, and background explicitly not used as filters. Artists at any career stage from any country can apply.

Selection is for a curated group exhibition at 0—1 Gallery in the Netherlands, scheduled for 2026–2027. Selected artists also receive visibility through the gallery's website and social media channels.

Submission is free. Each applicant submits a single link to their portfolio, website, or project page (rather than image attachments) via Google Form. The 2026 deadline is May 20, 2026; results announced June 20.

calls.title: Being Human — Artdoc Magazine Open Call
calls.description: Documentary photography open call inviting photographers to examine how human presence manifests in diverse cultural contexts. Portraits, environmental images, and documentary work — all approaches welcome. Selected work may be featured in curated online exhibitions, the Featured Submissions page, or upcoming magazine issues. Submissions free for Artdoc Magazine members; non-members must subscribe to submit.
calls.summary: Documentary photography open call exploring human presence across cultural contexts. Magazine publication and online exhibitions.
prose: Artdoc Photography Magazine is an online photography magazine (e-ISSN 3050-8029) operating themed open calls, curated exhibitions, and editorial publications for photographers. "Being Human" is the magazine's themed open call inviting photographers to examine how human presence manifests in diverse cultural contexts.

The brief is broad: portraits, environmental imagery, documentary photography, and conceptual work all qualify, provided the work engages with the human condition across distinct settings or communities. The framing favors substantive editorial work over single iconic images.

Selected work may be showcased through three channels: curated online exhibitions on the Artdoc platform, the Featured Submissions page (rolling editorial coverage), or upcoming themed magazine issues. The selection format is editorial rather than a single-prize competition — strong submissions are placed where they best fit Artdoc's ongoing program.

Submission is free for current Artdoc Magazine members; non-members must subscribe to participate. The membership-gating model ensures applicants are also magazine readers — a deliberate alignment between submitter and audience.
The 2026 deadline for the Being Human cycle is May 25, 2026. Eligibility is open globally.

calls.title: Flashes of Humanity — Pragovka Gallery 2027 Open Call
calls.description: Open call for the 2027 exhibition program and International Residency Program at Pragovka Gallery, a contemporary art space in Prague. Theme: Flashes of Humanity / Záblesky lidskosti — what it means to be human today, including subtle, almost imperceptible moments such as brief encounters and small acts of attention. Personal experiences, social questions, and experimental approaches all welcome; no medium restrictions, photography eligible. Two tracks: (1) exhibition projects (authorial or curatorial) at Pragovka Gallery in 2027 with the gallery covering transport, installation, accommodation, travel by agreement, PR, documentation, printed materials, and artist fees; (2) residency projects in the International Residency Program with an 80 m² studio, accommodation, travel by agreement, artist fees, and material cost contributions. Open to Czech and international artists and curators. Submission deadline 11:59 PM on May 17, 2026.
calls.prize: Exhibition or residency at Pragovka Gallery
calls.summary: Czech contemporary art gallery's 2027 open call for exhibition projects or international residencies. Photography eligible.
jury: Nine-member jury (Pragovka representatives, external artists, art theorists/curators)
prose: Pragovka Gallery is a contemporary art gallery in the Vysočany district of Prague (Kolbenova 923/34a, 190 00) — operating in a former factory complex repurposed as artist studios and exhibition spaces. The 2027 open call is themed "Flashes of Humanity / Záblesky lidskosti" — exploring what constitutes humanity today, with a brief that emphasizes subtle, almost imperceptible moments: brief encounters, small acts of attention, and the quiet ways humanness extends through and beyond exclusively human qualities.

The call is structured in two tracks. Track 1 selects exhibition projects (authorial or curatorial) for the 2027 exhibition program at Pragovka Gallery. Selected projects receive: transport and installation costs covered, accommodation and travel costs by agreement, PR and opening event production, design, printing, photographic documentation, and artist fees (amount determined by available funding). Pragovka does not cover artwork creation costs or materials.

Track 2 selects residency projects for Pragovka's International Residency Program. Residents receive an 80 m² studio space, accommodation and travel costs by agreement, an artist fee, and a material cost contribution. Residency outcomes can be Open Studio, lecture, studio presentation, or site-specific intervention.

Personal experiences, social questions, and experimental approaches are all welcome. There are no medium restrictions — photography is eligible alongside painting, sculpture, installation, sound, and other practices.

Selection is by a nine-member jury including Pragovka Gallery representatives, external artists, and art theorists/curators. Applications are free, made via Google Form with two PDFs (project description with visuals; portfolio/bio), each under 10 MB. Eligibility is open to Czech and international artists and curators. The 2026 deadline is May 17 at 11:59 PM; results published by end of June 2026.

calls.title: Rencontres Marrakech + OFF Arles 2026 Open Call
calls.description: 6th edition open call for the Rencontres de la Photographie Marrakech and Festival OFF Arles 2026. Theme: 1826–2026: Two Centuries of Light, inviting work that explores light as origin, medium, language, and possibility — intimate or political, abstract or documentary, conceptual or experimental. 20 winners exhibit five photographs each at Galerie Triptyque in Arles during the opening week of Les Rencontres d'Arles (July 3–20, 2026), present a video at the Rencontres de la Photographie de Marrakech festival (October 7–10, 2026), and receive a dedicated online publication on the festival's official platform. 30 additional finalists also participate in the Marrakech video presentation and online publication.
calls.summary: 20 winners exhibit at Galerie Triptyque in Arles during Rencontres week + video presentation at Marrakech festival.
jury: Marion Parent, Photographer & Co-Director, Divergence Images
prose: The Rencontres de la Photographie Marrakech is a Moroccan photography festival now in its 6th edition. The festival co-organizes its open call with Festival OFF Arles, the parallel program that runs alongside the major Rencontres d'Arles photography festival in southern France — meaning a single submission can land in both Arles and Marrakech.

The 2026 theme is "1826–2026: Two Centuries of Light," marking the bicentennial of Nicéphore Niépce's first surviving photograph. The brief invites work that explores light as origin, medium, language, and possibility across diverse photographic practices — intimate or political, abstract or documentary, conceptual or experimental.

Twenty winners are selected. Each receives an exhibition slot showing five photographs at Galerie Triptyque (12 Rue Jouvene) in Arles during the opening week of Les Rencontres d'Arles, July 3 through 20, 2026 — placement within the official OFF program of one of the world's most important photography festivals. Winners also present a video of up to 3 minutes at the Rencontres de la Photographie Marrakech festival, October 7–10, 2026, and receive a dedicated online publication of their complete series on the festival platform.

Thirty additional finalists also participate in the Marrakech video presentation (up to 2 minutes) and online publication. The festival is co-organized by Voix Plurielles (Casablanca) and Cultures Nomades Production (Arles), both non-profit non-governmental associations.
Entry fee is €15. Submissions go through Picter; the 2026 deadline is May 31, 2026 at 9:59 PM.

calls.title: Guest Room: Auronda Scalera & Alfredo Cramerotti
calls.description: Open call curated by Auronda Scalera (Artistic Director, curator, and lecturer; curator of "Ding Yi: Cosmotechnique" at Fondazione Querini Stampalia for Venice Art Biennale 2026) and Dr. Alfredo Cramerotti (Director, Media Majlis Museum at Northwestern University Qatar; President of IKT) exploring the theme "Shifting Thresholds." Invites photographic and image-based works engaging with displacement as a lived experience and aesthetic condition — migration, body transformation, exile, environmental change, and more subtle forms like digital mediation and algorithmic vision. Open to everyone. Selected work featured on Der Greif's platform with a face-to-face feedback session from the curators. Works must not have been previously selected by past Der Greif Guest Curators.
calls.summary: Theme: "Shifting Thresholds" — displacement, migration, body, exile, ecological change, digital mediation, algorithmic vision.
jury: Auronda Scalera, Artistic Director, curator, and lecturer
Alfredo Cramerotti, Director, Media Majlis Museum at Northwestern University Qatar
prose: Guest Room is Der Greif's recurring curator-led open call format. Each Guest Room is shaped by an external curator or curatorial duo who set the theme and the selection criteria. The 2026 edition is curated jointly by Auronda Scalera and Dr. Alfredo Cramerotti.

Scalera is an Artistic Director, curator, and lecturer; she curates Ding Yi: Cosmotechnique at Fondazione Querini Stampalia for the 2026 Venice Art Biennale. Cramerotti is Director of the Media Majlis Museum at Northwestern University Qatar and President of IKT (the International Association of Curators of Contemporary Art).

The theme is Shifting Thresholds. The brief asks for photographic and image-based work engaging with displacement as both a lived experience and an aesthetic condition: migration, bodily transformation, exile, environmental change — and more subtle forms like digital mediation and algorithmic vision.

Selected work is featured on Der Greif's platform. Selected artists also receive a face-to-face feedback session with the curators — direct rather than written. One artist receives a €250 scholarship. Eligibility is open globally; previously selected works from past Guest Rooms are not eligible.
Submission is through Picter, 1 to 5 images. The fee is voluntary (PWYC); financial hardship vouchers are available by emailing voucher-guestroom-2@dergreif.org. The 2026 deadline was May 7.

calls.title: Headlands Center for the Arts AIR 2027
calls.description: Fully sponsored 4–10 week Artist in Residence program at Headlands Center for the Arts in Sausalito, California. Approximately 60 artists selected each year, including local, national, and international applicants at all career stages. Photography is explicitly listed as an eligible discipline alongside drawing, painting, sculpture, film, video, new media, installation, writing, dance, music, interdisciplinary, social practice, arts professions, and architecture. Residency includes private studio space, chef-prepared meals, on-site housing, travel support, and a living expenses stipend. Application portal opens April 1, 2026; early bird fee ($35) closes May 4, 2026; regular fee ($45) thereafter. All applicants notified by December 11, 2026.
calls.summary: Fully sponsored 4–10 week residency in Sausalito, CA. Studio, meals, housing, travel covered. Photography eligible; ~60 artists/year.
