calls.summary: Inaugural photobook in Shutter Hub's City Series, exploring Cambridge through atmosphere, routines, and personal moments. Pay-what-you-can.
prose: The City Series is a new ongoing publication series from Shutter Hub Editions exploring the people, places, and cultures that shape cities worldwide. Each volume is built around a single city. The 2026 edition is the inaugural volume — Cambridge, the English university town where Shutter Hub is based.

The brief is observational rather than documentary: photographers approach the city openly through people, atmosphere, details, routines, abstractions, or unexpected moments that feel personal. The editorial framing is explicit — show what the city feels like rather than what it looks like.
The publication is a printed photobook available through shutterhub.org.uk and selected stockists. Published in collaboration with Velvet Magazine. AI-generated work is accepted in this volume.

Submission terms are accessible: pay-what-you-can entry with £10 minimum. Free submissions are available on request for photographers with limited income. Open worldwide, with up to 10 images per submission.
Submission is through the Shutter Hub website. The 2026 deadline was April 23; selections communicated within 12 weeks of deadline.

calls.title: The Colour Library: Yellow — Shutter Hub Editions Publication
calls.description: Open call for The Colour Library: Yellow, part of Shutter Hub's curated series exploring the emotional, symbolic, and visual power of individual colours. This edition is dedicated to yellow — bold and joyful, energetic and optimistic, but also capable of signalling caution, unease, or something hauntingly strange. Welcomes all approaches from bold monochromes to subtle glows, conceptual or documentary. Selected photographers featured in a professionally produced photobook held in international collections including the British Library and V&A. 100 images will be selected. Featured photographers receive promotion and a dedicated page on the Shutter Hub website. Pay-what-you-can entry with £15 minimum. Free submissions on request for photographers with limited income. Open worldwide.
calls.summary: Photobook dedicated to the colour yellow, from bold monochromes to subtle glows. Held in British Library and V&A collections.
prose: Shutter Hub is a UK-based photography organization that runs an artist network, exhibition program, and publishing imprint. Their publications are held in the collections of the British Library, the V&A, and the Portuguese Center of Photography, which gives Shutter Hub-published work an unusual archival afterlife — books stay on shelves long past the moment they're released.

The Colour Library is a curated photobook series published by Shutter Hub Editions, with each volume dedicated to a single color and the emotional, symbolic, and visual associations it carries. The Yellow edition welcomes any approach to the color — bold monochromes to subtle glows, conceptual to documentary, the joyful and the cautionary — provided the work is family-appropriate.

Selection is for 100 images. The published book is perfect-bound A5 portrait (148×210mm) on 140gsm matte paper with a 350gsm cover. Featured photographers receive a credit listing with a link to their website on a dedicated promotional page on the Shutter Hub site, and the book is distributed worldwide through Shutter Hub's bookstore network and into national collections.

Submissions are pay-what-you-can with a £15 minimum donation; free submissions are available on request for photographers with limited income. Each photographer can submit up to 10 images as JPEGs (300dpi, CMYK, max 5MB, sized for A5 portrait), with filenames structured as lastname_firstname_imagetitle.jpg. The deadline is 5pm UK time on July 16, 2026; selection is announced within 12 weeks.

calls.title: Lucie Foundation Scholarship Program 2026
calls.description: Annual program offering four cash grants across two categories (Fine Art and Photojournalism/Documentary), each split between Professional and Emerging photographers. Prizes: Fine Art Professional $3,000 + Fine Art Emerging $1,000 + Photojournalism/Documentary Professional $3,000 + Photojournalism/Documentary Emerging $1,000 plus a Sony camera and lens. Winners featured in a group exhibition that travels to House of Lucie Galleries worldwide (Los Angeles, Athens, Budapest, Ostuni, Samui). 'Professional' means earning majority of income from photography; 'Emerging' means enrolled students, photographers in their first five years, or those who don't earn majority from photography. Early bird discounts: 20% off until April 23, 10% off until April 30. Applicants submit a project proposal (1,500 characters max), one-page bio/CV, and 20 digital images. Open to photographers worldwide aged 18+.
jury: Antares Wells, Assistant Curator, Museum of Contemporary Art Australia
calls.summary: Four cash grants for Fine Art and Documentary photographers (pro and emerging). Winners tour House of Lucie galleries worldwide.
prose: The Lucie Foundation is a 501(c)(3) non-profit best known for the annual Lucie Awards and the International Photography Awards (IPA). Its Scholarship Program runs alongside those, awarding four cash grants per year split across two categories: Fine Art and Photojournalism/Documentary. Each category is divided between Professional and Emerging applicants, where "Professional" means earning the majority of one's income from photography and "Emerging" covers students, photographers in their first five career years, or those who do not earn the majority of their income from the medium.

Prize structure: Fine Art Professional $3,000; Fine Art Emerging $1,000; Photojournalism/Documentary Professional $3,000; Photojournalism/Documentary Emerging $1,000 plus a Sony camera and lens. Winners are featured in a group exhibition that travels to the House of Lucie galleries in Los Angeles, Athens, Budapest, Ostuni, and Samui — five physical venues across three continents.

Submissions are open to photographers worldwide aged 18 and older. Applicants submit a 1,500-character project proposal, a one-page biography or CV, and twenty digital images (JPG, 72 DPI, max 4MB each). Entry fees are $25 (Professional) and $15 (Emerging), with early-bird discounts of 20% (through April 23) and 10% (through April 30). The 2026 final deadline is September 30; winners are announced in October.

The 2026 jury comprises Antares Wells (Assistant Curator, Museum of Contemporary Art Australia), Kateryna Radchenko (Ukraine-based curator and photography researcher), and Elizabeth Ferrer (curator and writer specializing in Latinx photography).

calls.title: PLACE/MEMORY — CONTACT Photography Festival
calls.description: Open call photography exhibition at Northern Contemporary Gallery in Toronto, presented as part of the 2026 CONTACT Photography Festival — Canada's largest photography festival. Photographers are invited to submit work that represents their current practice through the medium of photography, responding to the theme PLACE/MEMORY. Physical group exhibition runs May 21 – June 2, 2026, with an opening reception on May 21, 6–9pm. One submission per artist via the official Google form. Work drop-off May 19; pick-up June 3. Part of the CONSTELLATION program curated by Su-Ying Lee and Emilie Croning.
calls.summary: Toronto gallery exhibition during CONTACT Photography Festival on the theme of place and memory. Physical show May 21 – June 2, 2026.
prose: Northern Contemporary Gallery is a Toronto-based contemporary art gallery. "PLACE/MEMORY" is the gallery's photography open call presented as part of the 2026 CONTACT Photography Festival — Canada's largest photography festival, held annually across multiple Toronto venues.

The brief asks photographers to submit work representing their current practice through the medium of photography, responding to the theme of place and memory. The framing is open: literal documentation of specific places, abstract evocations of remembered locations, family or community archive work, and conceptual approaches to memory all qualify.

The exhibition is physical: it runs May 21 through June 2, 2026 at the gallery, with an opening reception on May 21 from 6 to 9 PM. The exhibition is part of the CONSTELLATION program curated by Su-Ying Lee and Emilie Croning, which forms part of the CONTACT festival's broader curatorial framework.
Submission is free of charge. AI-generated work is not accepted. Each artist submits up to 5 images via the official Google Form (one submission per artist).
Logistics: drop-off May 19; pick-up June 3. The 2026 deadline is May 12 at 11:59 PM.

calls.title: Women's Studio Workshop — Art-in-Ed Workspace Residency 2026
calls.description: 6–7 week workspace residency combining teaching with personal studio practice at Women's Studio Workshop in Rosendale, NY. Artists teach intaglio, silkscreen, or hand papermaking to local public school students — fourth and/or eighth graders three days/week for three weeks in Spring (elementary) or high school students one day/week for 4 weeks in Fall (plus school visits). Outside of teaching, artists work independently in any WSW studio including darkroom photography. Residency includes $175/day per teaching day plus $525 for lesson planning, free housing, and 24/7 studio access. Artist covers travel and materials. Fall 2026 cohort teaches high school; Spring 2027 cohort teaches elementary. Applications open February 15; notification in July.
calls.summary: Teaching-artist residency combining printmaking/photo instruction with personal studio work. Daily teaching stipend plus free housing.
prose: Women's Studio Workshop (WSW) is a non-profit print, photo, and book arts center at 722 Binnewater Lane, Kingston, New York (in the Rosendale area), founded in 1974. The Art-in-Ed Workspace Residency combines a teaching residency with personal studio time — artists teach intaglio, silkscreen, or hand papermaking to local K-12 public school students while working in WSW's studios on their own practice.

The teaching schedule splits between two cycles. The Fall 2026 cohort runs 6 weeks teaching high school students one day per week for 4 weeks (plus school visits). The Spring 2027 cohort runs 7 weeks teaching fourth and/or eighth graders three days per week for three weeks in elementary classrooms. Artists are paired with a teaching assistant during contact hours.

Compensation: $175 per day per teaching day plus $525 for lesson planning. Artists receive free on-site housing and 24/7 studio access including the silkscreen studio, darkroom photography facilities, intaglio, letterpress, papermaking, and ceramics studios. Artists cover their own travel and materials.
Eligibility requires the ability to teach intaglio, silkscreen, or hand papermaking. Outside of teaching hours, residents can work in any WSW studio. Application is free.
Applications go through Submittable. The 2026 application window opens February 15 and closes May 15 at 11:59 PM EST; results announced July.

calls.title: BEERS London Group Exhibition 2026
calls.description: Open call for a group exhibition of approximately 12 artists at BEERS London, a contemporary gallery in the heart of the City. All artistic media welcome including photography. Selected artists consigned for exhibition period plus up to three months, with 50/50 commission split on sales. Gallery actively promotes selected work to collectors. No guaranteed representation or sales. Open worldwide. Exhibition runs October 2026 (autumn). Selected artists notified approximately two months before opening.
calls.summary: Group exhibition of ~12 artists at contemporary London gallery. All media including photography. October 2026 show.
prose: BEERS London is a contemporary commercial gallery in the City of London that runs an annual open call for a curated group exhibition. The 2026 cycle selects approximately 12 artists working across all media — painting, sculpture, photography, video, mixed media — for a show in October 2026 (autumn).

Selected artists consign their work for the duration of the exhibition plus up to three months afterward, during which the gallery actively promotes the work to its collector base. Sales split commission 50/50. Insurance is provided by the gallery during the exhibition window.

The application is structured to allow combining tracks: the group exhibition application alone is £10, and the combined residency-plus-exhibition application is £25 (£5 less than applying separately). Selection is by the BEERS London team alongside guest curators. Eligibility is open globally to artists at any career stage.

Inclusion in the group exhibition does not guarantee gallery representation or sales — the format is closer to a curated open submission than to a representation pitch. Selected artists are notified approximately two months before the exhibition opening. The deadline has been extended to August 1, 2026.

calls.title: L'OLTRE 2026
calls.description: Open call from Naples-based photography association The Docks (founded 2020) inviting photographers and visual artists to explore visions that lie at the edges of conventional reality — beyond appearance, logic, and the visible. Winning project published as the first volume of L'OLTRE 2026 in a limited edition by The Docks Publishing. Honorable mentions featured on The Docks' channels as emerging artists. Fee is €15 total (€5 membership + €10 minimum donation). Open to all nationalities, genders, and ages. AI-generated works explicitly accepted.
calls.summary: Photobook call exploring visions beyond conventional reality. Winner published in limited edition by The Docks Publishing.
prose: L'OLTRE — "the beyond" — is a photobook open call from The Docks, a Naples-based photography association founded in 2020. The 2026 edition is the launch of L'OLTRE as a publishing series.

The brief asks photographers and visual artists to work at the edges of conventional reality — visions that exceed appearance, logic, and the visible. The concept is open to interpretation: documentary projects pushed toward the speculative, staged work, abstraction, dream-states, and computational image-making are all on the table.
Notably, AI-generated work is explicitly accepted — a position that distinguishes L'OLTRE from most contemporary photobook calls. Eligibility is fully open: all nationalities, genders, ages.

The selected project is published as the first volume in the L'OLTRE 2026 series, in a limited edition by The Docks Publishing. Honorable mentions are featured on The Docks' channels as emerging artists.
The €15 fee is composed of a €5 association membership and a €10 minimum donation. Submission is through The Docks' website, 10–20 images. The 2026 deadline was May 5; results announced May 30, 2026.

calls.title: Joan Wakelin Bursary 2026
calls.description: Annual £2,000 bursary for the production of a photographic essay on an overseas social documentary issue. Administered by the Royal Photographic Society in partnership with The Guardian. Winner also receives portfolio printing by Metro Imaging (up to 12 C-types at 16×12") and a portfolio review with Creative Director Prof Steve Macleod. Established in 2005 in memory of documentary photographer Joan Wakelin (d. 2003). Funds new original projects only; does not support ongoing projects or travel to/within war zones. Awarded to individuals, not groups. Open to all photographers worldwide.
calls.summary: £2,000 bursary for overseas documentary photo essays. RPS x The Guardian. Free entry, open worldwide. Named after Joan Wakelin.
prose: The Joan Wakelin Bursary is a £2,000 grant for the production of a photographic essay on an overseas social documentary subject, administered by the Royal Photographic Society (RPS) in partnership with The Guardian. The bursary was established in 2005 in memory of documentary photographer Joan Wakelin, who died in 2003.

Beyond the cash, the winner receives portfolio printing by Metro Imaging — up to 12 C-type prints at 16×12 inches — and a portfolio review with Creative Director Professor Steve Macleod. The combination is designed to fund production of the work and prepare it for editorial placement.
The bursary funds only new original projects; ongoing work is not eligible. Travel to or within war zones is excluded. The award is given to individuals rather than groups or collectives.

There is no application fee, and the bursary is open to photographers worldwide. The 2026 deadline is July 6. Applications go through RPS's awards platform; applicants submit a project proposal rather than completed images.

calls.title: Women's Studio Workshop — Studio Residency Grant 2026
calls.description: 4–6 week fully funded residency for artists at any career stage at Women's Studio Workshop in Rosendale, NY. Work independently in one of five studios: intaglio, letterpress, papermaking, screenprinting, or darkroom photography. Grant includes $350/week stipend, up to $500 for materials, up to $250 toward travel within the Continental US, free onsite housing, and 24/7 studio access. Applications open February 15; residencies take place September through June, 1–2 years after application.
calls.summary: Fully funded darkroom residency with weekly stipend, materials budget, travel assistance, and onsite housing in Rosendale, NY.
prose: The Studio Residency Grant is Women's Studio Workshop's flagship residency program — distinct from the teaching-focused Art-in-Ed Workspace Residency, this grant supports artists working independently on their own practice without a teaching component.

Residency length is 4 to 6 weeks. WSW's facilities include five distinct studios: intaglio, letterpress, papermaking, screenprinting, and darkroom photography. Residents choose which studio they want to work in, with technical advice and production assistance available throughout the residency.

The grant is unusually well-funded for a printmaking and photo residency. Each resident receives a $350 per week stipend plus up to $500 for materials and up to $250 toward travel within the Continental US. Free on-site housing is included, with 24/7 studio access throughout the residency.

The application timeline is unusual: residencies take place September through June, but typically 1 to 2 years after the application is submitted. This long lead time lets WSW match residents to specific studio time blocks based on the work proposed.

Eligibility is open to artists at any career stage. There is no application fee. Applications go through Submittable and require a current resume, 300-word project description, up to 10 images with image script (title, medium, dimension, date), and an optional indication of interest in WSW's other residency programs. The 2026 application window opens February 15 and closes May 15 at 11:59 PM EST; results announced July.

calls.title: Women's Studio Workshop — Anita Wetzel Residency Grant 2026
calls.description: 4–6 week fully funded residency for mature artists aged 45 and older at Women's Studio Workshop in Rosendale, NY. Honors the legacy of Anita Lynn Wetzel. Work in any of five studios: intaglio, letterpress, papermaking, screenprinting, or darkroom photography. Grant includes $350/week stipend, up to $500 for materials, up to $250 toward travel within the Continental US, free onsite housing, and 24/7 studio access. Residencies take place September through June, 1–2 years after application.
calls.summary: Fully funded darkroom residency with stipend and housing, dedicated to mature artists aged 45+. Rosendale, NY.
prose: The Anita Wetzel Residency Grant is Women's Studio Workshop's age-specific track of the Studio Residency Grant program — reserved exclusively for mature artists aged 45 and older. The grant honors the legacy of Anita Lynn Wetzel.

Funding and structure mirror WSW's main Studio Residency Grant: 4 to 6 weeks of residency with a $350 per week stipend, up to $500 for materials, and up to $250 toward travel within the Continental US. Free on-site housing is included, with 24/7 studio access throughout the residency.

Studio options are the same as the regular Studio Residency Grant: intaglio, letterpress, papermaking, screenprinting, or darkroom photography. Residents work independently on their own practice but may request studio assistance from WSW staff.

Eligibility is restricted to artists 45 years and older. There is no application fee. Applications go through Submittable using the regular Studio Residency Grant form with the "Anita Wetzel Residency Grant" box checked. The 2026 application window opens February 15 and closes May 15 at 11:59 PM EST; results announced July; residency takes place September through June, 1–2 years after application acceptance.

calls.title: Stories: Narrative Photography
calls.description: Curated international group photography exhibition exploring narrative and storytelling. Seeking photographs that tell stories — personal or social, literal or symbolic, about persons, communities, objects, or places. All creative photographic interpretations welcome. Curated by Zsolt Bátori (PhD, Rutgers; founder/director PH21 Gallery; Photolucida board member) and Borbála Jász (art historian; Photolucida juror). Curator's choice receives three free entries for future PH21 exhibitions. Up to three honorable mentions. Special rate for students, unwaged, and low-income economies (€15–20). Images submitted by email as JPEG, longest side max 1280px. Early bird deadline May 18 at reduced rates; final deadline May 25. Exhibition at PH21 Gallery in Barcelona's Gothic Quarter, July 25 – August 18, 2026.
jury: Zsolt Bátori, Photographer & Philosophy of Art
Borbála Jász, Art Historian & Philosophy of Art
calls.summary: Curated group show on narrative and storytelling. Physical exhibition in Barcelona's Gothic Quarter, July–August. Student rates available.
prose: PH21 Gallery is a curatorial gallery operating from Barcelona's Gothic Quarter (the gallery relocated from Budapest more than a decade after its founding). "Stories: Narrative Photography" is the gallery's themed call inviting work that tells stories — about persons, communities, objects, and places — through personal, social, literal, or abstract visual interpretation.

All creative photographic approaches are welcome. The brief favors images that carry implication beyond their immediate subject, whether through sequencing, captioning, single-frame implication, or multi-image series.

The 2026 exhibition runs July 25 through August 18, 2026 at PH21's Barcelona gallery in the Gothic Quarter. The Curator's Choice winner receives three free entries for future PH21 themed group exhibition calls (up to 15 images per entry); up to three honorable mentions are also recognized.

Selection is by curators Zsolt Bátori (PhD Rutgers, founder and director of PH21 Gallery, Photolucida board member) and Borbála Jász (art historian, Photolucida juror). Acceptance is competitive — curators have final selection authority.

Entry fees are tiered. Standard rates run €25–€45 for 3 to 15 photos at early-bird (closing May 18, 2026), rising to €30–€50 at final deadline (May 25, 2026). Discounted rates of €15 (early bird) or €20 (final) are available for students, unwaged persons, and applicants from low-income economies. Submissions are made by email as JPEGs at maximum 1280 pixels on the longest side. Eligibility is open globally to photographers 18 and over.

calls.title: PORTAL
calls.description: Juried photography exhibition exploring the theme 'at the edge of becoming.' Seeking photographs depicting transition as a condition — figures between visibility and disappearance, spaces suggesting restricted entry, suspended moments, or structurally unstable compositions. The strongest images will resist resolution, embodying transition rather than describing it. Juried by Douglas Stockdale (visual artist, editor, educator; founder of PhotoBook Journal; work in collections at Museo d'Arte Contemporanea di Roma, Beinecke Library at Yale, Reminders Photography Stronghold). All photographic styles and processes accepted. Exhibition June 20 – August 20, 2026.
jury: Douglas Stockdale, Visual Artist & Founder of PhotoBook Journal
calls.summary: Transition & becoming — figures, spaces, suspended moments. Juried by Douglas Stockdale (PhotoBook Journal founder).
prose: Decagon Gallery is an online curatorial platform that runs themed photography exhibitions with published catalogs and social distribution. "PORTAL" is the gallery's open call for photography exploring tension at the edge of transition — images that hold a viewer at the moment a shift is imminent but not yet complete. Literal interpretations (doors, windows, thresholds) are accepted only when the photograph carries inherent tension; the brief favors work that embodies transition rather than describing it.

Cash awards total $1,000 across three placements: $500 first place plus a solo website exhibition, $300 second, $200 third. All selected photographers receive a permanent exhibition page on the Decagon site and inclusion in the published catalog. The 2026 exhibition runs June 20 through August 20.

The 2026 cycle is juried by Douglas Stockdale, founder of PhotoBook Journal and author of the Singular Images blog. His work is held in collections at Museo d'Arte Contemporanea di Roma and the Beinecke Rare Book & Manuscript Library at Yale.

All photographic processes are welcome. Entry fee is $25 for up to 8 images. Eligibility is open to photographers worldwide aged 18 and over. Submissions are JPG at 2100 pixels on the long side, no watermarks or borders. The 2026 deadline is June 3 at 11:59 PM Eastern; results announced June 15.

calls.title: The Emergence Project 2026
calls.description: Annual graduate showcase for recently graduated UK-based photographers (graduated 2023–2026). Free to submit. Gallery covers all printing and installation costs, with work printed on Fujifilm photographic paper and framed in gallery frames. Submit up to 8 images along with a brief statement about your work, graduation details, and why you'd like to participate. Exhibition July 3–31, 2026 at Glasgow Gallery of Photography.
calls.summary: Free graduate showcase for UK photography grads (2023–2026). Gallery covers printing and framing. Glasgow exhibition, July.
prose: The Emergence Project is the Glasgow Gallery of Photography's annual graduate showcase, run as a free open call for recently graduated UK-based photographers. The 2026 cycle is open to anyone who graduated between 2023 and 2026 — a three-year window that captures graduates who may have missed earlier graduate showcases due to pandemic-era programming gaps.

The exhibition runs July 3 through 31, 2026 at the Glasgow Gallery of Photography. The gallery covers all printing and installation costs for selected work, with prints produced on Fujifilm photographic paper and presented in gallery-supplied frames. The selected photographer provides only the digital files.
Submissions are limited to UK-based recent graduates. Submission is free of charge.

Each photographer submits up to 8 images along with a brief statement about their work, their graduation details, and why they'd like to participate. Submissions are made by email via file transfer to submissions@glasgowgalleryofphotography.com. The 2026 deadline is May 30.

calls.title: Across America 2026
calls.description: Photography exhibition celebrating America's diverse and dynamic essence — landscapes, people, culture, or any aspect that embodies the nation's spirit. Up to 3 images forming a cohesive series. Juried by Brian Crowley (landscape/street photographer) and Ron St. Jean (portrait/fine art photographer, 40+ years experience). Exhibition at The Art Center gallery in historic downtown Dover. Artists receive 70% of sale price. All work must be for sale and cannot be removed during the exhibition. Members enter free. Open to US photographers of all levels, 18+. Exhibition July 13 – August 31, 2026.
jury: Ron St. Jean, Portrait & Fine Art Photographer
calls.summary: Photography celebrating America's diverse essence — landscapes, people, culture. Juried exhibition in Dover, NH, July–August.
prose: The Art Center is a community gallery in historic downtown Dover, New Hampshire. "Across America 2026" is the gallery's themed photography exhibition for 2026, inviting work that celebrates America's diverse and dynamic essence — landscapes, people, culture, or any aspect that embodies the nation's spirit. The brief is interpretive: literal documentary, abstract, conceptual, and traditional landscape work are all welcome.

Each photographer submits up to 3 images forming a cohesive series. Selection is by photographers Brian Crowley (landscape and street) and Ron St. Jean (portrait and fine art, 40+ years' practice). The exhibition runs July 13 through August 31, 2026.

All accepted work must be for sale and cannot be removed during the exhibition. Sales terms split commission with the artist receiving 70% of sale price. Members of The Art Center enter free; non-member entry is $25 for up to 3 images.
Eligibility is restricted to U.S. photographers aged 18 and over, at all skill levels. Submissions go through ArtCall. The 2026 deadline is May 31; results announced June 8.

calls.title: Fine Art Photography Awards 2026/2027
calls.description: 13th edition of the international fine art photography contest. 20 categories: Abstract, Architecture, Conceptual, Experimental, Fashion, Fine Art, Landscape, Nature, Night Photography, Nudes, Open Theme, Panoramic, People, Photojournalism, Photomanipulation, Portrait, Seascape, Street Photography, Travel, Wildlife/Animals. Professional and Amateur divisions. Early bird deadline October 11, 2026; final deadline February 14, 2027. Winners announced April 11, 2027. Panel of 15 international jurors. Professional Grand Prize: $3,000 + Fine Art Photographer of the Year title. Amateur Grand Prize: $2,000. Category winners receive gold/silver/bronze awards. Open worldwide.
calls.summary: 13th edition — 20 categories from landscape to street. $3K professional / $2K amateur grand prizes. 15 international jurors.
prose: Fine Art Photography Awards is an international competition founded in 2014 and now running its 13th edition. Submissions are open to amateurs and professionals worldwide across 20 categories: Abstract, Architecture, Conceptual, Experimental, Fashion, Fine Art, Landscape, Nature, Night Photography, Nudes, Open Theme, Panoramic, People, Photojournalism, Photomanipulation, Portrait, Seascape, Street Photography, Travel, and Wildlife/Animals.

The Professional Grand Prize is $3,000 plus the Professional Fine Art Photographer of the Year title. The Amateur Grand Prize is $2,000 plus the Amateur title. Category winners receive Gold, Silver, Bronze, or White badges and certificates; all winners receive gallery showcase and international press coverage.

Entry fees use a tiered structure with separate amateur and professional rates. At early deadline (October 11, 2026): Amateur $19 single / $24 series; Professional $24 single / $29 series. At final deadline (February 14, 2027): Amateur $24 single / $29 series; Professional $29 single / $34 series. Additional categories cost $10 each.

The jury comprises 15 international photographers, including Jaco Marx, Michele Palazzo, Karolina Wojtasik, Tugo Cheng, Jan Møller Hansen, Juan Pablo de Miguel, Anna Tihanyi, and others, with names rotating between editions. Winners are announced April 11, 2027.

calls.title: Black and White
calls.description: Celebrating the power and timelessness of black and white photography — the deep, unending shades of grey. All photographic genres welcome. At least 26 images selected for exhibition at Decode Gallery in Tucson. Selected artists receive complimentary professional printing on Epson printers with Ilford Pearl paper, museum-quality 22×22 white framing and custom matting. 50% commission on sales. Open worldwide to all skill levels. Exhibition July 4 – July 25, 2026.
jury: Holly Hart, Conceptual Fine Art Photographer & Decode Gallery Founder
calls.summary: B&W photography — all genres. Pro printing on Ilford Pearl paper and museum framing included. Exhibition in Tucson, AZ.
prose: Black and White is Decode Gallery's themed call dedicated specifically to monochrome photography — celebrating the depth and tonal range of black and white photography across all genres. The brief is medium-specific rather than subject-specific: portraiture, landscape, documentary, architecture, conceptual, and abstract work all qualify, provided the work is in monochrome.
At least 26 images are selected for the physical exhibition at Decode Gallery in Tucson, Arizona, running July 4 through 25, 2026.

What's unusual: the gallery covers all professional printing on Epson printers with Ilford Pearl paper, museum-quality 22×22 inch white framing, and custom matting. The artist provides only the high-resolution JPEG. Prints are retained in the gallery's flat files for two years after the exhibition for further promotion.
Sales terms split commission 50/50. Selected work is also promoted across Decode's website and social media. Selection is by Decode founder Holly Hart, a conceptual fine art photographer.
Entry fees: $40 for 5 images or $45 for 10 images. Eligibility is open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers. The 2026 deadline is May 23, with selection announced approximately June 6.

calls.title: Global Ability Photography Challenge 2026
calls.description: 5th edition of the world's largest inclusive photography competition, exclusively for persons with disabilities. Open to all styles — documentary, portrait, street, conceptual, abstract, or experimental. No theme restriction, no age limit. Top 20 photographs exhibited in Ahmedabad, India, with works featured across media and global campaigns. Custom trophies by designer Michael Foley. Award ceremony June 24, 2026. Travel and accommodation support provided for winners. Over 4 editions, GAPC has reached 8 million people and 50,000+ participants from 30+ countries. Organized by Not Just Art (Youth4Jobs) with Adani GreenXTalks.
calls.summary: Free photography competition exclusively for persons with disabilities — ~$20K in prizes, top 20 exhibited in Ahmedabad.
prose: The Global Ability Photography Challenge (GAPC) is an inclusive photography competition exclusively for persons with disabilities. Founded approximately in 2022, the 2026 cycle is the 5th edition. The program is organized by Not Just Art / Youth4Jobs in partnership with Adani Plus and other sponsors, and the organizers describe it as the largest disability-led photography competition globally.

There is no thematic restriction. Submissions span all approaches — documentary, portrait, street, conceptual, abstract, or experimental. The brief encourages, but does not require, work capturing stories of inclusion, dignity, resilience, hope, and the everyday lives of persons with disabilities.

Cash prizes total approximately ₹17,00,000 ($20,000 USD) across ten placements: 1st ₹5,00,000; 2nd ₹3,00,000; 3rd ₹2,00,000; and 4th through 10th at ₹1,00,000 each. The top 20 photographs are exhibited in Ahmedabad, India, with custom trophies designed by Michael Foley. Travel and accommodation are sponsored for selected winners attending the award ceremony.

Eligibility is restricted to persons with disabilities; there is no age restriction. Submission is free. Each photographer submits a maximum of 3 photos in JPEG format, RGB, maximum 2000 pixels on the longest side, minimum 4 MB file size, with no watermarks or identifying marks.

Across its first four editions, GAPC reports reaching 8 million people, 50,000+ lives inspired, and participants from 30+ countries. The 2026 deadline is May 25; results announced before the June 24 award ceremony.

calls.title: #HopperHappens Juried Photography Exhibition
calls.description: Photography-only juried exhibition inspired by the #HopperHappens Instagram series — real-world moments evoking Edward Hopper's style, light, and mood. 55 photographs selected and displayed across 55 businesses and nonprofits in Nyack, NY, birthplace of Edward Hopper. $1,000 in cash prizes: First $500, Second $300, Third $200, plus Juror's and Visitor's Choice awards. Juror: Richard Tuschman, celebrated for his 'Hopper Meditations' series. Exhibition June 1 – July 5, 2026. Open internationally, ages 18+. Work must be completed after January 1, 2020 and never previously exhibited at EHHM. MFA student discounts available.
calls.summary: Photography inspired by Hopper's light and mood — 55 works displayed across 55 Nyack venues. Juror: Richard Tuschman.
prose: The Edward Hopper House Museum operates from Hopper's childhood home in Nyack, New York. The #HopperHappens series began on the museum's Instagram, collecting real-world photographs that evoke Hopper's light, mood, and compositional sensibility — the painter's domestic American spaces translated into photographic seeing. The juried exhibition extends that Instagram premise into a physical group show.

The 2026 juror is Richard Tuschman, a photographer best known for his Hopper Meditations series, which restages Hopper paintings as constructed photographic dioramas. The selection structure is unusual: 55 photographs are chosen and dispersed across 55 different businesses and nonprofits throughout Nyack — the show is the town for the duration.
Cash prizing is $1,000 total: first $500, second $300, third $200, plus Juror's and Visitor's Choice awards. The exhibition runs June 1 – July 5, 2026.

Eligibility is open internationally to photographers 18+. Submitted work must be completed after January 1, 2020 and never previously exhibited at the Edward Hopper House Museum. MFA student discounts on entry fee are available.
Submission is through ArtCall with up to 3 images. Fee is $30 for members and $60 for non-members. The 2026 deadline was May 3; results announced May 11, 2026.

calls.title: Narrative
calls.description: Photography exhibition exploring visual storytelling through single images or cohesive series. Documentary, street, conceptual, staged, and experimental approaches welcome. Exhibition at Chico Art Center gallery, August 15 – September 18, 2026, with opening reception September 4. Member fee $25. Free exhibition catalog via Blurb. Opportunity to sell work (30% commission to center). Previously exhibited work at CAC ineligible.
calls.summary: Photography exhibition on visual storytelling — documentary, street, conceptual, staged, or experimental approaches.
prose: Chico Art Center is a community arts gallery at 450 Orange Street, Suite 6 in Chico, California. "Narrative" is the gallery's open call for photography that explores visual storytelling — work that communicates a narrative through a single image or cohesive series, whether personal journey, cultural or historical commentary, political statement, or fiction.

All photographic mediums and styles are welcome — documentary, street, conceptual, staged, experimental — with no thematic constraint beyond the storytelling brief. AI-generated images are not currently accepted. Work previously exhibited at CAC is ineligible.

Selected work is exhibited at Chico Art Center August 15 through September 18, 2026, with an opening reception on September 4. The gallery handles installation. Each artist receives a free copy of a printed exhibition catalog produced via Blurb, and selected work is promoted through the gallery's website and social channels.
Sales are facilitated by the gallery, which requests a 30% donation but pays the artist the full listed price. Artists are responsible for shipping and insurance.

Entry fee is $35 (general) or $25 for CAC members. Submissions take up to 7 images via JotForm. The 2026 deadline is June 14 at 11:59 PM. Selection is by Gallery Director Cameron Kelly with a CAC board member.

calls.title: Flatland Feature — Issue 2
calls.description: Online photography feature showcasing photographers' work in a series format as a virtual gallery experience. Selected photographers' work featured for six months on the MWCP website (July–December 2026). Each feature consists of 10–20 images with an accompanying artist statement and biography. Visitors can view and purchase photographs online (50% commission). Open internationally, all subject matter and genres accepted.
calls.summary: Online portfolio feature — 10–20 images showcased for 6 months on MWCP website. All genres, open internationally.
prose: Midwest Center for Photography (MWCP) is a US-based online photography platform that runs themed exhibitions and feature programs. Flatland Feature is the platform's online series-portfolio program — a slot for extended bodies of work rather than single-image group shows.

Selected photographers receive a six-month feature on the MWCP website, July through December 2026. Each feature consists of 10–20 images presented with an accompanying artist statement and biography — closer to a gallery solo than a group exhibition entry.
Visitors can view and purchase photographs through the feature page. MWCP takes 50% commission on sales; photographers retain rights.
Eligibility is open internationally, with no restriction on subject matter or genre. Submission is through MWCP's website. Fee is $100 for 10 images. The 2026 Issue 2 deadline was May 1.

calls.title: The Art of Abandonment
calls.description: International open call exploring abandoned and rediscovered objects, locations, and structures. Photographers examine what these forgotten spaces reveal about humanity, memory, and the passage of time. Online exhibition June 1 – July 1, 2026. Curator's Choice, Director's Choice, and Honorable Mentions awarded. Blind jury process — juror sees only the image and title.
calls.summary: Themed exhibition exploring forgotten structures, objects, and places — what they reveal about humanity and time.
prose: TCG Gallery (also operating as Chateau Gallery) is an online curatorial platform that runs themed photography exhibitions with published catalogs. "The Art of Abandonment" is the gallery's open call for photography exploring abandoned and rediscovered objects, locations, and structures — work that examines what forgotten spaces reveal about humanity, memory, and the passage of time.

Approximately 35 images are selected for the online exhibition, running June 1 through July 1, 2026. The selection structure includes Curator's Choice and Director's Choice awards plus Honorable Mentions. The jury is structured as a rotating assortment of past exhibitors, curators, editors, and arts professionals using a blind jury process — jurors see only the image and its title.
Selected work is included in the published catalog, promoted across the gallery's website and social media with attribution, and offered for sale through the gallery (which retains 30% commission).

Eligibility is restricted to photographers aged 18 and over. AI-generated and AI-altered work is not accepted. Citizens of countries under U.S. comprehensive sanctions (Iran, Cuba, North Korea, Sudan, Syria, Belarus, Russia) cannot submit.

Entry fee is $15 for up to 3 images, with merit-based and hardship waivers available. Submissions are JPG at minimum 1200 pixels on the longest side, 500 KB minimum file size. The 2026 deadline is May 25 at 11:59 PM; notification May 27.

calls.title: Encontros Da Imagem Award 2026
calls.description: Open call for the 36th edition of Encontros da Imagem, one of Europe's oldest photography festivals, founded in 1991 in Braga, Portugal. Three projects selected for solo exhibitions during the festival across multiple northern Portuguese cities, September 18 – November 1, 2026. One overall winner receives €2,000. Seventeen further projects included in a collective video screening. Theme: Territory And Identity. Projects must use photography or video with coherent narrative structure, produced within the last five years. Maximum three projects per applicant.
calls.summary: Major European photo festival (36th edition). €2,000 prize + solo exhibition. Theme: Territory And Identity. Open worldwide.
jury: Arianna Catania, Independent Curator & Photo Editor
Arianna Rinaldo, Independent Curator & Photography Consultant
prose: Encontros da Imagem is one of Europe's longer-running photography festivals, founded in 1991 in Braga, Portugal. The 2026 edition is the festival's 36th, running September 18 through November 1, 2026 across multiple cities in northern Portugal. The festival's main award and its photobook award (separately covered) are the two flagship prize tracks.

The 2026 theme is "Territory and Identity" — though the open call explicitly does not require submitted work to align with the theme. Selection is based on coherent narrative structure rather than thematic fit.

The selection structure is layered. The grand prize winner receives €2,000 cash. Three projects (including the grand prize winner) are selected for solo exhibitions during the festival. Seventeen additional projects are included in a collective video screening — bringing total recognized projects to 20.

The 2026 jury comprises Arianna Catania (independent curator and photo editor), Alexia Alexandropoulou (independent curator), and Arianna Rinaldo (independent curator and photography consultant who has appeared on multiple Italian/Portuguese juries throughout 2026).

Eligibility is open globally to artists 18 and over. Each applicant submits up to 3 projects, with each project containing 15 to 20 images and a brief synopsis. Work must have been produced within the last five years. Both photographic and video practices are eligible. Entry fee is €35 per submission. Submissions go through Picter; the deadline is May 10, 2026 at 9:59 PM.

calls.title: 31st National Competition 2026
calls.description: Soho Photo Gallery's 31st annual National Competition. Approximately 60 photographs selected for exhibition at the gallery's spacious W23rd Street location in Chelsea, New York. Cash prizes for first ($400) and second ($200) place. Third place and up to four honorable mentions receive prizes from sponsor Archival Methods. Juror: Joanna Lehan, Manager of Curatorial Projects at Museum of the City of New York. Open to photographers who are residents of the United States. Exhibition July 2026.
calls.summary: Annual photo competition at Soho Photo Gallery NYC. ~60 works exhibited. $400 first, $200 second. US residents only.
jury: Joanna Lehan, Manager of Curatorial Projects, Museum of the City of New York
prose: Soho Photo Gallery is a photographer-run cooperative gallery in New York, founded in 1971 by photojournalists. It bills itself as the longest-running cooperative photography gallery in the city. The gallery is now located on W23rd Street in Chelsea, having moved from its original SoHo location.

The National Competition is the gallery's annual juried exhibition. The 2026 edition is the 31st. Approximately 60 photographs are selected for the show. Cash prizes go to first place ($400) and second place ($200). Third place and up to four honorable mentions receive prizes from sponsor Archival Methods. The 2026 juror is Joanna Lehan, Manager of Curatorial Projects at the Museum of the City of New York, with prior curatorial work at ICP and bylines in photography journals.

Eligibility is restricted to photographers 18 and over who are US residents. Gallery members are excluded. AI-generated work is not accepted. Previous winners may apply but must submit different photographs; no previously exhibited work.

Submission is through the CaFÉ platform. Files are JPEG, longest dimension max 1220 pixels at 72 DPI. Up to 12 images. Fee is $55 for 1–5 images, $5 per additional image. If selected, work must be gallery-quality printed, mounted, framed, and pre-wired for hanging — maximum width 48 inches including frame. The gallery commission on sales is 30%.
Key 2026 dates: deadline May 9; notification June 7; work delivery June 18; exhibition June 24 – July 12; opening reception June 25; pickup July 14.

calls.title: BLACK & WHITE
calls.description: International juried photography exhibition at Praxis Gallery in Minneapolis celebrating monochrome photography as a deliberate creative choice. Up to 74 images selected for exhibition June 20 – July 11, 2026. Awards include Juror's Choice (free entry to three future calls) and Directors' Choice (free entry to two future calls), plus eight honorable mentions. Members receive 10 images for the price of 5. Free submissions available for artists experiencing financial hardship. Juror: Sandrine Hermand-Grisel, fine art photographer, printmaker, and founder of All About Photo.
calls.summary: Monochrome juried exhibition at Praxis Gallery Minneapolis. Up to 74 works selected. Open internationally.
prose: Praxis Photo Arts Center is a Minneapolis nonprofit gallery and educational center for fine art photography. BLACK & WHITE is the gallery's recurring international juried exhibition focused on monochrome photography as a deliberate creative choice — not as a default or technical limitation.

Up to 74 images are selected for the physical exhibition at Praxis Gallery, running June 20 – July 11, 2026. Awards are entry-credit-based rather than cash: Juror's Choice receives free entry to three future Praxis calls; Directors' Choice receives free entry to two; plus eight honorable mentions.
The 2026 juror is Sandrine Hermand-Grisel — fine art photographer, printmaker, and founder of All About Photo, the international photography platform.

Eligibility is open internationally to photographers 18+. Submission is through Smarter Entry with 1–10 images. The fee is $35 for 5 images; Praxis members receive 10 images for the price of 5. Free submissions are available for artists experiencing financial hardship.
The 2026 deadline was May 3; results announced May 14, 2026.

calls.title: Thresholds 2026: Up, Close and Personal
calls.description: Annual street photography exhibition at the Los Angeles Center of Photography, one of LA's leading photography institutions. 2026 theme: Up, Close and Personal — intimate street photography. Digital projection exhibition and in-person opening event at LACP Helms Design District, May 7–31, 2026. Open to international photographers of all skill levels. Prizes: 1st place $500 plus one-year LACP membership, 2nd place $500 LACP gift card, 3rd place $250 LACP gift card. Juror: Michaela Norah Mohrmann, assistant curator at UC Irvine Langson Orange County Museum of Art. Members receive 25% discount on fees.
calls.summary: Street photography exhibition at LACP LA. $500 first place. Digital projection show + opening event. Open worldwide.
prose: Thresholds is the Los Angeles Center of Photography's annual street photography exhibition. LACP is one of LA's principal photography institutions — a nonprofit with a school, gallery, and exhibition program. The 2026 theme is Up, Close and Personal — intimate street photography rather than wide observational work.
Selection is by Michaela Norah Mohrmann, assistant curator at UC Irvine Langson Orange County Museum of Art. Single-juror selection.

The exhibition is digital projection plus an in-person opening event, running May 7–31, 2026 at LACP's Helms Design District location. Cash prizes: first $500 plus a one-year LACP membership; second $500 LACP gift card; third $250 LACP gift card.
Eligibility is open to international photographers of all skill levels. Submission is through Submittable with 1–35 images. Fee starts at $25 for one image; LACP members receive a 25% discount.
The 2026 deadline was April 21; results announced April 28, 2026.

calls.title: Light Dreams
calls.description: Juried exhibition of alternative and historical process photography at Light Art Space gallery in Silver City, New Mexico. Theme explores light as an internal, psychological, and symbolic presence — where light and dreams intersect through hand-made photographic processes. Accepted media: cyanotype, platinum/palladium, silver gelatin, wet-plate collodion, gum bichromate, and other alternative processes. Digital negatives acceptable but straight digital and AI-derived work ineligible. 3D and experimental work encouraged. Open internationally, ages 18+. Gallery actively invites LGBTQ+, Black, Latinx, Indigenous, and artists of color. Exhibition July 4 – September 6, 2026, with reception July 5. Student rate $20.
calls.summary: Alt-process juried show in New Mexico. Cyanotype, platinum, wet-plate & more. Open worldwide, student rate $20.
prose: Light Art Space is a gallery at 209 West Broadway in Silver City, New Mexico, with a program focused on alternative and historical process photography. "Light Dreams" is the gallery's juried exhibition for 2026 — the brief explores light as an internal, psychological, and symbolic presence, asking how light and dreams intersect through hand-made photographic processes.

Eligible media span the full range of alt-process work: cyanotype, platinum/palladium, silver gelatin, wet-plate collodion, gum bichromate, and other historical and alternative processes. Digital negatives are acceptable as long as the print itself involves a hand-made process. Straight digital and AI-derived work are ineligible. 3D and experimental approaches are explicitly encouraged.

The 2026 jury is Jill Enfield, the photographer and educator known for her own substantial alt-process practice and her instruction on collodion, wet plate, and other historical techniques. The exhibition runs July 4 through September 6, 2026, with an opening reception July 5. Sponsor support is provided by Freestyle75.
The gallery actively invites submissions from LGBTQ+, Black, Latinx, Indigenous, and artists of color, framing this not as a separate track but as part of the broader open call.

Entry fee is $35 for 3 images, with a $20 student rate. Submissions go through CaFÉ. Eligibility is open globally to artists 18 and over. The 2026 deadline is May 19 at midnight MST; results announced May 24.

calls.title: COAL Prize 2026 — The Night
calls.description: Annual art and ecology prize from French foundation COAL. 2026 theme: The Night — defending darkness as a common good, a major ecological issue for regeneration of life, a refuge, and a right to rest. Main prize: €12,000 grant plus creative residency at Domaine de Belval (François Sommer Foundation). Special Jury Prize: €3,000. Centre Wallonie-Bruxelles mention: €2,000 plus exhibition. Ateliers Médicis mention: residency near Paris. Ten artists nominated by committee, winners chosen by jury. Submit single PDF (max 30MB) with project description, technical note, budget, 2+ HD visuals, CV, and portfolio. Open worldwide, all disciplines including photography and lens-based media.
calls.summary: €12,000 art & ecology prize with residency. Theme: defending darkness. Jury Prize €3,000. Free, open worldwide.
prose: COAL is a French foundation focused on the intersection of contemporary art and ecology. The annual COAL Prize is awarded to a project addressing an environmental theme that shifts each year. The 2026 theme is The Night — framed as defending darkness as a common good, a major ecological issue for regeneration of life, a refuge, and a right to rest.
Selection structure: ten artists are nominated by an internal committee, and the final winners are chosen by an external jury.

The main prize is €12,000 plus a creative residency at Domaine de Belval, run by the François Sommer Foundation. The Special Jury Prize is €3,000. There are two additional partner mentions: the Centre Wallonie-Bruxelles mention (€2,000 plus exhibition) and the Ateliers Médicis mention (residency near Paris).
Eligibility is open worldwide across all disciplines — including photography and lens-based media. The award is project-based: applicants submit a proposal rather than a finished body of work.

Each application is a single PDF (max 30MB) including project description, technical note, budget, 2+ HD visuals, CV, and portfolio. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was April 28; results announced Autumn 2026.

calls.title: 1st Photobook Grants 2026
calls.description: Fourth edition of the 1st Photobook Grants supporting photographers who have never published a monograph. Three grants of €5,000 each in three categories: photographers from the Global South (Africa, Caribbean, Southeast Asia, Latin America, Middle East), French photographers or those residing in France (SAIF grant), and female photographers of any nationality. Must partner with an independent French publisher and provide a letter of commitment. Supported by the French Ministry of Culture and SAIF. Winners announced June 2026; books must be published by November 30, 2027.
calls.summary: Three €5,000 grants for debut photobook projects. Categories: Global South, French, and female photographers. Free, needs French publisher.
prose: The 1st Photobook Grants is a French photobook program initiated by the Eyes Wide Open association, the cultural production entity of The Eyes label. The program is supported by France's Ministry of Culture and SAIF (Société des Auteurs des arts visuels et de l'Image Fixe). The 2026 cycle is the fourth edition.

The program is unusually targeted: each cycle awards three separate €5,000 grants in three category-specific tracks. The Global South grant is reserved for photographers from Africa, the Caribbean, Southeast Asia, Latin America, or the Middle East. The SAIF grant is reserved for French photographers or photographers residing in France. The third grant is open to female photographers of any nationality.

All three grants share the same project requirement: photographers who have never previously published a monograph. The grant supports the production of a first photobook, with the structural requirement that applicants must partner with an independent French publisher and submit a letter of commitment from that publisher with their application — making this as much a publisher-photographer matchmaking program as a cash grant.

Submission is free. Applicants submit a single PDF (maximum 25 MB) via Google Form. The 2026 application window runs February 17 through May 17, with winners announced in June 2026. Books must be published by November 30, 2027 — a 17-month production window from announcement.

calls.title: Ten x Ten – 18th Annual Small Works
calls.description: Annual small works exhibition at the Midwest Center for Photography in Wichita, Kansas (November 14 – December 31, 2026). Celebrates creative expression within the square photographic format. All works are 10"×10" and priced at $200 each. MWCP provides printing at no cost to selected artists. Open to all photographers internationally.
calls.summary: Annual 10"×10" square-format exhibition at MWCP, Wichita. Affordable collectible works, MWCP prints at no cost.
prose: Ten x Ten is the Midwest Center for Photography's annual square-format exhibition, now in its 18th year. The brief is unusually concrete: every accepted print is exactly 10 inches by 10 inches, and every print is sold at the same price — $200 each — for the duration of the show. The format levels the field across genres and career stages and produces a uniform grid hang that has become the show's signature.

MWCP is a small photography-focused space in Wichita, Kansas. Selected work is exhibited both physically and online; MWCP covers all printing costs for accepted entries, which is unusual for a juried show at this scale. A $30 frame rental is the only out-of-pocket expense for selected artists who want their work framed for the wall.

Submissions are open internationally to photographers working in any process — film, digital, iPhone, or alternative. The 2026 exhibition runs November 14 through December 31, with the submission deadline September 1.

calls.title: FOTOHOF>CALLING
calls.description: Biennial open call for contemporary photographic projects. Around 25 artists are selected for online publication on the FOTOHOF>CALLING platform and in the FOTOHOF>CALLING Magazine. 10 finalists are invited to present their projects in Salzburg on October 3, 2026, with an open-air projection on Inge-Morath-Platz. Projects must be no older than three years and never exhibited in institutional settings (museums, galleries, festivals). Student/university work and residency programs are exempt from this rule. Open to artists who reside, work, or stay in Europe.
calls.summary: Biennial call for contemporary photo projects. 25 selected for publication, 10 finalists present in Salzburg. Open to European artists.
prose: FOTOHOF is a long-running photography institution in Salzburg, Austria — a gallery, archive, and publishing platform. FOTOHOF>CALLING is its biennial open call for contemporary photographic projects. The call's structure is publication-plus-presentation rather than competition-prize.

Selection has two tiers. Around 25 artists are selected for online publication on the FOTOHOF>CALLING platform and in the FOTOHOF>CALLING Magazine. From these, 10 finalists are invited to present their projects in person in Salzburg on October 3, 2026 — with an open-air projection event on Inge-Morath-Platz, the public square named for the Magnum photographer.

Eligibility is restricted by recency and prior exposure: projects must be no older than three years and must not have been exhibited in institutional settings (museums, galleries, festivals). Student/university work and projects done within residency programs are exempt from this rule.
Geographic eligibility: artists who reside, work, or stay in Europe.
Application is free, with up to 12 images per project. Submission is through the FOTOHOF>CALLING website. The 2026 deadline was April 26; final presentation October 3, 2026.

calls.title: Martin House Creative Residency 2026
calls.description: 2–4 week project-based residency at Frank Lloyd Wright's Darwin D. Martin House in Buffalo, New York. Residents live in the Gardener's Cottage on campus and create new work inspired by the architecture, design, landscape, and social history of Martin House. Open to artists working in any discipline including photography, writing, and research. Residents receive $5,000 stipend paid in two installments and up to $1,000 travel allowance for non-local applicants. Residency term runs June–October 2026. Must deliver a free public program, performance, or exhibition sharing work with the community. Requires US social security number. Application window March 30 – May 13, 2026.
calls.summary: 2–4 week residency at Frank Lloyd Wright's Martin House. $5,000 stipend + $1,000 travel. Work inspired by architecture and design.
prose: The Martin House Creative Residency is hosted at the Darwin D. Martin House (125 Jewett Parkway, Buffalo, NY 14214), Frank Lloyd Wright's Prairie-style masterpiece designed for businessman Darwin D. Martin and built between 1903 and 1905. The complex is one of Wright's most ambitious residential designs and a National Historic Landmark.

The residency is project-based: applicants must propose work directly inspired by the architecture, design, landscape, or social history of the Martin House. The program is unusually broad in disciplinary scope — visual artists, writers, researchers, and creative makers from any field can apply, with photography explicitly eligible.

Residency length is 2 to 4 weeks onsite, either consecutively or split across multiple visits within the June through October 2026 term. Each resident receives a $5,000 stipend (paid in two installments — 50% on arrival, 50% on completion) plus up to $1,000 in travel expenses for non-local participants. Housing is provided in the Gardener's Cottage on the Martin House campus — a private bedroom and bathroom with utilities and high-speed wi-fi included.
Residents are required to deliver a free public program, performance, exhibition, or other creative presentation during or after the residency, sharing work with the Buffalo community.

Eligibility requires applicants to have a U.S. social security number (including permanent residents, OPT holders, and Indigenous peoples eligible under the Jay Treaty). Individual applicants only — collectives are not eligible. The program is free to apply. The 2026 application window runs March 30 through May 13, 2026.

calls.title: Loghaven Artist Residency 2027
calls.description: Residency on 90 acres of forested land in Knoxville, Tennessee for practicing artists at any career stage. Sessions range from 2–6 weeks between February and October 2027. All fellows receive an $850/week living stipend, travel subsidy ($400–$800 on a sliding scale), and up to $200 in materials shipping reimbursement. Disciplines include visual arts, writing, dance, music composition, theater, and interdisciplinary work. Applicants must be 21+, live 120+ miles from Knoxville, and have legal US work authorization. International artists are not eligible. Applications open June 1, 2026. Submit 8 JPEG images for visual art via SlideRoom.
calls.summary: 2–6 week residency on 90 forested acres. $850/week stipend plus travel subsidy. Visual arts, writing, and more.
prose: Loghaven is an artist residency on 90 acres of woodland at 1001 Loghaven Drive in Knoxville, Tennessee. Artists are housed in five historic log cabins that have been rehabilitated and modernized, with access to purpose-built studio space on the grounds.

The 2027 program runs across six sessions of varying lengths: a four-week February cycle, a six-week April–May cycle, a two-week June cycle for fellows only, a two-week July cycle for teaching/faculty artists, a two-week September cycle, and a four-week October–November cycle. Applicants choose their preferred session at submission.

Financial support is unusually substantive for a residency: an $850 per week living stipend for the duration of the stay, a sliding-scale travel subsidy of $400–$800, and up to $200 reimbursement for materials shipping. Disciplines accepted include visual arts, writing, dance, music composition, theater, and interdisciplinary work.

Eligibility is restricted: artists must be at least 21 years old, hold U.S. work authorization, live at least 120 miles from Knoxville, and not be enrolled in a degree-seeking program. International artists are not eligible. Two professional references are required.

The application fee is $25, with waivers available June 1–July 15. Applications open June 1 and close July 15, 2026 at midnight Eastern Time. The selection panel — a national committee of artist peers and arts professionals — meets August through September, with applicants notified by November 1.

calls.title: FMoPA 2026 International Photography Competition
calls.description: International photography competition open to photographers worldwide. Submit up to 15 images across 7 categories: People/Portraits, Places/Landscape, Nature/Science/Animals, Documentation/Photojournalism, Still Life, Abstract, and Conceptual. Best in Competition receives $1,000 cash prize. Category winners receive goods and services. Winning works exhibited June 16 – August 2, 2026 at FMoPA in Tampa's Ybor City District.
calls.summary: International photography competition. $1,000 grand prize and exhibition at FMoPA Tampa. 7 categories.
jury: Jessica Jarl, Global Director of Exhibitions, Fotografiska
Hiromi Nakamura, Curator, Tokyo Metropolitan Museum of Photography
Elena Paraskeva, Photographer and Art Director
Bärbel Reinhard, Photographer, Curator and Educator
Kristen Roles, Photographic Artist and Educator
prose: The Florida Museum of Photographic Arts (FMoPA) is a Tampa-based museum dedicated to photography, located in Tampa's Ybor City Historic District. The annual International Photography Competition is the museum's flagship juried open call.

The 2026 edition runs across seven categories: People/Portraits, Places/Landscape, Nature/Science/Animals, Documentation/Photojournalism, Still Life, Abstract, and Conceptual. Eligibility is open globally to photographers 18+.
Best in Competition receives $1,000 cash. Category winners receive goods and services rather than additional cash. Winning works are exhibited at FMoPA from June 16 to August 2, 2026.

The 2026 jury is built from international institutions: Jessica Jarl (Global Director of Exhibitions, Fotografiska), Hiromi Nakamura (Curator, Tokyo Metropolitan Museum of Photography), Elena Paraskeva (photographer and art director), Bärbel Reinhard (photographer, curator and educator), and Kristen Roles (photographic artist and educator).
Submission is through Picter with up to 15 images. Fee is $10. The 2026 deadline was April 22; results announced May 13, 2026.

calls.title: Fotograf Magazine 2026 Open Call
calls.description: Open call for publication in Fotograf Magazine, a leading international photography publication based in Prague. Two selected projects published in the next printed issue. Open to professionals, amateurs, and students submitting independent fine-art photography or moving-image projects. Submit CV, portfolio PDF, and project description with images via email.
jury: Felix Hoffmann, Curator and Director, FOTO ARSENAL WIEN
Peter Watkins, Visual Artist and Lecturer, FAMU
calls.summary: Publication opportunity in leading international photography magazine based in Prague. Two projects selected for print.
prose: Fotograf Magazine is an international photography publication based in Prague. The annual open call selects work for inclusion in a printed issue — two projects are selected for publication.

The brief is open across format — independent fine-art photography or moving-image projects are both eligible. The magazine accepts work from professionals, amateurs, and students without distinction.

The 2026 jury reflects the magazine's institutional reach: Felix Hoffmann (Curator and Director, FOTO ARSENAL WIEN), Markéta Kinterová (Editor-in-Chief, Fotograf Magazine), Michaela Nagyidaiová (visual artist), Marta Szymańska (curator), and Peter Watkins (visual artist and lecturer at FAMU, the Prague film school).
Submission is by email — applicants send a CV, portfolio PDF, and project description with images. Fee is €35 per project. The 2026 deadline was April 30; results announced July 30, 2026.

calls.title: Grenze Arsenali Fotografici 2026 Open Call
calls.description: Open call for the ninth edition of Grenze - Arsenali Fotografici international photography festival in Verona. Theme: Nachleben. Three artists selected for exhibition during the festival opening September 2026.
jury: Aida Redžepagić & Jelena Janković, Sarajevo Photography Festival
David Pujado, Belgrade Photo Month Founder
Simone Azzoni, Co-Founder & Artistic Director, Grenze
calls.summary: International photography festival in Verona. Theme: Nachleben. Three artists exhibited. Strong international jury.
prose: Grenze – Arsenali Fotografici is an international photography festival held annually in Verona, Italy. The 2026 edition is the festival's ninth. The festival's open call selects three artists for exhibition during the festival opening in September 2026.

The 2026 theme is Nachleben — a German term taken from Aby Warburg's art-historical vocabulary, referring to the afterlife or survival of images and forms across time. The brief invites work that thinks photography in relation to memory, persistence, and the recurrence of visual motifs.

The 2026 jury draws from a network of European photography festival directors: Aida Redžepagić & Jelena Janković (Sarajevo Photography Festival), David Pujado (founder of Belgrade Photo Month), Marta Szymanska (director of Fotofestiwal in Łódź), and Grenze's own Simone Azzoni (Co-Founder and Artistic Director) and Francesca Marra (President).
Submission is by email with 10–20 images. Fee is €28. The 2026 deadline was April 30; results announced May 30, 2026.

calls.title: Photography 4 Humanity / Fotografiska Global Prize 2026
calls.description: Global photography prize exploring the theme HOME — safety, belonging, identity, memory, loss, and place. Open to photographers worldwide. Selected photographs exhibited at United Nations Headquarters in New York on Human Rights Day (December 10, 2026), guest-curated by James Nachtwey.
calls.summary: Theme: HOME. Selected work exhibited at UN Headquarters NYC, curated by James Nachtwey. Free entry.
jury: Pauline Benthede, Global VP Artistic Direction & Exhibitions, Fotografiska
Sophia Emmerich, Lead Editor, Fotografiska Emerging Platform
prose: The HOME open call is a joint initiative by Photography 4 Humanity, Fotografiska, and the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights. The brief is the single word "home" — interpreted across safety, belonging, dignity, identity, memory, loss, and place — and the call is positioned as a human rights project rather than a conventional photography prize.

Selected work is exhibited at the United Nations Headquarters in New York on Human Rights Day, December 10, 2026. The exhibition is guest-curated by James Nachtwey, with Pauline Benthede (Fotografiska's Global VP of Artistic Direction & Exhibitions) and Sophia Emmerich (Lead Editor of the Fotografiska Emerging Platform) joining selection.

The selection structure has three tiers: one Main Image, ten Runners-up, and twenty Honorable Mentions — 31 photographers in total. Submissions are limited to three images per applicant. Only lens-based photography is accepted (analog or digital); AI-generated or prompt-based images are explicitly excluded.
There is no entry fee. The call is open to photographers worldwide aged 18 and over, with explicit emphasis on emerging artists. The deadline is July 12, 2026; results are announced October 5, 2026.

calls.title: Minimalist Photography Awards 2026
calls.description: Seventh edition of the international award celebrating minimalist photography as a visual language. Open to photographers worldwide. Submit single images or series (2–7 images) across 12 categories including Abstract, Architecture, Fine Art, Landscape, Long Exposure, Portrait, and Street. Grand prize: €2,000 cash, hand-crafted trophy, title of Minimalist Photographer of the Year, and inclusion in the official annual book. Earlybird deadline May 1; final deadline June 2, 2026.
calls.summary: International award for minimalist photography. €2,000 grand prize, book publication, and exhibition. 12 categories.
calls.ai: Only accepted if incorporating a real photograph
jury: Milad Safabakhsh, Founder, Minimalist Photography Awards
prose: The Minimalist Photography Awards is an international competition focused exclusively on minimalist photography as a visual language. The 2026 cycle is the 7th edition; the awards have been running annually since the first edition in 2019. The program is based in Bregenz, Austria, and was founded by photographer Milad Safabakhsh.

Submissions are accepted across 12 categories: Abstract, Architecture, Fine Art, Landscape, Long Exposure, Portrait, Street, and others. Photographers may submit single images or series of 2 to 7 images per category.

The Grand Prize Winner receives €2,000 in cash, a hand-crafted trophy, and the title "Minimalist Photographer of the Year," along with inclusion in the official annual book and gallery exhibition opportunities. Category winners are featured in the annual book and online showcase.

The 2026 jury comprises Sylvia Janschek (photographer), Matthias Weissengruber (photographer), Leon Boch (photographer), and founder Milad Safabakhsh, with the international panel rounding out across editions.

Entry fees are tiered with an early bird deadline May 1 and final deadline June 2, 2026 (23:59 UTC). Eligibility is open globally to photographers 18 and over. AI-generated work is accepted only if it incorporates a real photograph; fully AI-generated work is excluded.

calls.title: Villa Lena Foundation — Artist Residency 2027
calls.description: Residency program for artists of all disciplines in a 19th-century villa in Tuscany, Italy. Residencies run 4–5 weeks between April and October 2027. Includes studio space, accommodation, and half-board meals five days a week. Residency fee of €150/week covers room, studio, and meals. Artists must donate a completed work to the foundation's collection. Access to ceramic and wood workshops, screening room, and weekly excursions.
calls.summary: 4–5 week residency in a Tuscan villa with studio, accommodation, and meals. €150/week residency fee. All disciplines.
prose: Villa Lena Foundation operates an artist residency from a 19th-century Tuscan villa on a 500-hectare estate near Pisa. The 2027 program runs residencies of 4–5 weeks between April and October. Multidisciplinary by design — artists across visual arts, photography, music, writing, and performance work alongside one another.

The residency provides a private studio, accommodation in a renovated farmhouse on the estate, and half-board meals five days per week. Beyond the basics, residents have access to ceramic and wood workshops, a screening room, and a program of weekly excursions in the surrounding countryside.

The cost structure is unusual: residencies are not free. Artists pay a €150-per-week residency fee that covers room, studio, and meals. Residents are also required to donate a completed work to the Villa Lena Foundation collection at the end of their stay.

Eligibility is open to artists of all disciplines and any career stage. Application requires a PDF portfolio, submitted via Google Forms. Application fee is €21. The 2027-cycle deadline was May 3, 2026; results announced November 2026.

calls.title: Taylor Wessing Photo Portrait Prize 2026
calls.description: One of the world's most prestigious portrait photography competitions. Open to photographers worldwide, aged 18+. Submit up to 6 portraits taken after 1 January 2025. First prize £15,000, second £3,000, third £2,000. Selected works exhibited at the National Portrait Gallery in London from November 2026 to January 2027. The prize celebrates contemporary portraiture, interpreting 'portrait' in its widest sense — photography concerned with portraying people with an emphasis on their identity as individuals.
calls.summary: Premier international portrait prize. £15,000 first prize. Exhibition at National Portrait Gallery, London, Nov 2026–Jan 2027.
prose: The Taylor Wessing Photo Portrait Prize is the National Portrait Gallery's annual portrait photography competition, sponsored by international law firm Taylor Wessing. The prize is held within an institution dedicated specifically to portraiture, which shapes selection — the gallery is interested in photography concerned with portraying people with an emphasis on identity as individuals.

The brief interprets 'portrait' broadly: studio, environmental, candid, conceptual, and self-portraiture are all eligible. Submitted photographs must have been taken after January 1, 2025 — recency-restricted to recent work.

Selected works are exhibited at the National Portrait Gallery in London from November 2026 to January 2027 — a flagship public-facing exhibition slot. Cash prizes: £15,000 (first), £3,000 (second), £2,000 (third).

Eligibility is open globally to photographers 18+. Each photographer may submit up to 6 images. Fee is £22 per image. Submission is through the National Portrait Gallery's competitions portal. The 2026 deadline was April 21; results announced November 2026 alongside the exhibition opening.

calls.title: EMERGE 2026
calls.description: Annual fellowship for emerging photographers. Open to all emerging photographers worldwide working in any photographic medium.
