calls.summary: Seven $5,000 grants for emerging sports photographers plus mentorship. Up to 3 additional $2,500 grants.
prose: The Doug Pensinger Photography Fund (DPPF) was established to support emerging and early-career sports photographers. The fund's annual grants program is one of the few dedicated funding mechanisms specifically for sports photography rather than documentary or fine-art categories.

Eligibility is restricted to photographers with fewer than three years of cumulative paid professional sports photography experience. Open worldwide except countries under active US sanctions. AI-generated work is not accepted.

Selection structure has two grant tiers. The main grants: seven photographers each receive $5,000 for career development plus an expenses-paid trip to the Sports Photography Gathering (September 16–18, 2026). The Gathering is the fund's annual professional convening — selected grantees attend at no personal cost. Up to three of the seven main grantees are eligible for an additional year-long mentorship with members of the fund's Advisory Board.
Development Grants: up to three additional applicants receive $2,500 each as a smaller-scale grant track.

The 2026–27 mentors are Jean Fruth, Bob Martin, and Jamie Schwaberow — all working sports photographers. Submission is through Picter, with 20 images. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was May 1; results announced July 1, 2026.

calls.title: Bowness Photography Prize 2026
calls.description: Australia's richest photography prize, now in its 21st year. Open to Australian citizens or permanent residents (12+ months). Winner receives $50,000 AUD and acquisition into MAPh's permanent collection. Two Honourable Mentions receive $2,500 each. Wai Tang Commissioning Award of $10,000 for a future exhibition. People's Choice Award of $5,000. Finalists exhibited at MAPh gallery. Accepts still photo-based media including analogue and digital photography produced within the past year. Up to 3 works per $55 entry. AI permitted only if not the substantial or overriding input. Entries open April 16, 2026.
jury: Natasha Bullock, Senior Curator of Photography, NGV
Petrina Hicks, Artist & Previous Bowness Prize Winner
calls.summary: Australia's richest photography prize. $50,000 AUD winner. 21st year. Australian citizens/residents only.
prose: The Bowness Photography Prize is Australia's richest photography prize, awarded annually by the Museum of Australian Photography (MAPh) at Wheelers Hill, Victoria. The 2026 cycle is the 21st edition. The prize is named for William and Sandra Bowness, longtime supporters of the museum.

Cash prizes are substantial: a $50,000 AUD main prize plus acquisition of the winning work into MAPh's permanent collection. Two Honourable Mentions receive $2,500 each. The Wai Tang Commissioning Award provides $10,000 toward a future MAPh exhibition. The People's Choice Award is $5,000.

Eligibility is restricted to Australian citizens and permanent residents of at least 12 months' standing. Submissions are limited to still photo-based media, including analogue and digital photography, produced within the past year. AI is permitted only if it is not the substantial or overriding input — fully AI-generated work is excluded.
Each $55 AUD entry covers up to 3 works. Finalists are exhibited at MAPh gallery. The 2026 application window opens April 16; the deadline is June 14, with the winner announced September 17, 2026.

calls.title: Flanelle Print No. 47 — July 2026
calls.description: Montreal-based fashion and arts magazine (est. 2012) accepting submissions for Print No. 47, publishing July 2026. Open to artists, photographers, and designers worldwide. Selected work featured in quarterly print and digital magazine with international distribution. Two-phase review process. Work must be unpublished and exclusive to Flanelle. Paid upgrade options available for cover placement and priority publishing.
calls.summary: Montreal fashion and arts magazine. Quarterly print and digital with international distribution. Est. 2012.
prose: Flanelle Magazine is a Montreal-based fashion photography, arts, and culture publication, founded in 2012. The magazine publishes quarterly in January, April, July, and October, with each issue produced in both print and digital formats and distributed internationally.

Print No. 47 publishes July 2026. Submissions are accepted from artists, photographers, and designers worldwide. Each photo set must include a minimum of 10 photographs following the issue theme and mood board. Editorials must be unpublished and exclusive to Flanelle.

Standard print submissions are free. Optional paid upgrades are available for cover contests, advertorial placement, or priority publishing. The magazine uses a two-phase review process, with selected artists notified individually after editorial review.

Selected work appears in the quarterly print issue and digital edition with international distribution, plus possible social media exposure across the magazine's channels. Selected artists receive digital versions of their published spreads on request. Submissions go through Kavyar (kavyar.com/flanellemag); the Print No. 47 deadline is June 1, 2026.

calls.title: Embracing Our Differences 2027 Outdoor Exhibition
calls.description: International outdoor juried exhibition in its 23rd year. 50 selected artworks are displayed as billboard-sized panels (16 ft × 12.5 ft) in public parks in Sarasota and St. Petersburg, Florida, from January to April 2027. Three awards: $2,000 Best-in-Show Adult, $2,000 Best-in-Show Student, $2,000 People's Choice. Work must reflect themes of diversity, inclusion, kindness, and respect. Accepts photography, painting, drawing, mixed media, digital art. Horizontal orientation only. No limit on entries per artist. 150-word artist statement required. Over 5.2 million visitors since 2004. AI-generated work not accepted.
calls.summary: 50 artworks displayed as billboard-sized panels in Florida parks. Themes: diversity, inclusion, kindness.
jury: Blind judging panel of artists, curators, and art professionals
prose: Embracing Our Differences is an international juried public-art exhibition that has run annually since 2004, now in its 23rd year. Selected artworks are displayed as billboard-sized panels — 16 feet by 12.5 feet — in public parks in Sarasota and St. Petersburg, Florida, from January through April. Since the program's founding the exhibitions have drawn over 5.2 million visitors collectively, making it one of the most heavily-visited outdoor art shows in the United States.

Fifty artworks are selected per cycle. Three cash awards of $2,000 each are given: Best-in-Show Adult, Best-in-Show Student, and People's Choice. The brief asks for work that reflects diversity, inclusion, kindness, and respect, with the panel format favoring strong horizontal compositions readable at billboard scale.

Eligible media span photography, painting, drawing, mixed media, and digital art — work must be horizontal in orientation, and AI-generated submissions are not accepted. There is no fee, no limit on entries per artist, and a 150-word artist statement is required.
Submissions go through Zealous. The 2027 cycle deadline is July 1, 2026, with results announced in early fall.

calls.title: Night Aesthetics
calls.description: Open call exploring the visual world of the night. Looking for works that engage with light, movement, atmosphere, intimacy, and the energy that appears when the day lets go. Whether captured on a crowded dance floor, in a quiet street, or somewhere in between. Welcomes lens-based photography in all forms including analog and digital. Three winners each receive €2,500 and feature on the Fotografiska Emerging platform. In partnership with Jägermeister.
jury: Atiba Jefferson, Staff Photographer Thrasher Magazine & Canon Explorer of Light
Julia Schoierer, Portrait & Street Photographer, Berlin
calls.summary: Exploring the visual world of the night — light, movement, atmosphere. Three winners receive €2,500 each.
prose: Night Aesthetics is a thematic open call on Fotografiska Emerging — the photography platform run by Fotografiska, the international photography museum with locations in Stockholm, Tallinn, New York, Berlin, and Shanghai. The 2026 edition is run in partnership with Jägermeister.

The brief asks photographers to engage with the visual world of the night — light, movement, atmosphere, intimacy, and the energy that appears when the day lets go. Subject matter is open: a crowded dance floor, a quiet street, or anywhere between. Lens-based photography in all forms, including analog and digital. AI-generated work is not accepted.
Three winners each receive €2,500 plus a feature on the Fotografiska Emerging platform.

The 2026 jury is Atiba Jefferson (staff photographer at Thrasher Magazine and Canon Explorer of Light), Karl Hab (photographer working in aviation, architecture, and fashion), and Julia Schoierer (Berlin-based portrait and street photographer).

Eligibility is open globally to photographers 18+. Submission is one image per entry through the Fotografiska Emerging platform. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was April 30; results announced May 20, 2026.

calls.title: The 2026 Lumen Prize
calls.description: Leading international award for art created with technology, now in its 15th year. Three categories: Legacy Futures, Systems & Structures, and Experiential Innovation, each with a $5,000 prize. The Jury also selects one Gold Award Winner receiving $15,000. Works may include film, photography, AI-generated art, interactive installations, VR experiences, and more. Finalists announced August, winners announced November. Awards ceremony at Kunstsilo Museum in Norway.
jury: Melanie Lenz, Digital Curator, V&A Museum
Rachel Falconer, Senior Lecturer & Head of Digital Arts Computing, Goldsmiths University London
Myriam Achard, Chief New Media Partnerships & PR, PHI
Christiane Paul, Adjunct Curator Digital Art, Whitney Museum
Ulrich Schrauth, Artistic Director, UBS Digital Art Museum
Annie Bicknell, Curator Public Programmes, Tate
calls.summary: Leading award for art created with technology. 15th year. $15,000 Gold Award. Categories include AI, VR, and more.
prose: The Lumen Prize is an international award for art created with technology, established in approximately 2011 and now running its 15th annual edition. The 2026 cycle has a total prize pool of $30,000 distributed across multiple categories, plus several specialized award tracks.

Three main category awards of $5,000 each: Legacy Futures (works engaging past, present, and future), Systems & Structures (works examining cultural, ecological, technological, or social systems), and Experiential Innovation (interactive, immersive, or participatory works). One Gold Award of $15,000 is selected from across all categories. A separate Student Award of $2,000 is sponsored by HKUST and requires enrollment in a BA, BFA, MFA, MA, PhD, or equivalent program.

Additional special awards: a Special Commendation Award of $5,000 for BIPOC female artists in generative art; the Carla Rapoport Award of $1,000 plus project development support; the Nordic Award of $1,000 for Nordic country artists; and a MUTEK Forum Opportunity (presentation slot, no cash).
Eligible work spans film, photography, AI-generated art, interactive installations, VR experiences, generative work, and other technology-engaged practices. AI is explicitly accepted.

Selection is two-stage: an International Selectors Committee (50+ members) curates the finalists; a distinguished 8-member Jury Panel selects winners, including curators from Tate (Annie Bicknell), V&A (Melanie Lenz), and Whitney Museum (Christiane Paul). Entry fee is $45. The 2026 cycle accepts submissions January 26 through May 23, 2026; finalists announced August; winners November; awards ceremony at Kunstsilo Museum, Norway.

calls.title: Nest — Group Exhibition
calls.description: Group exhibition exploring how creative practice nurtures wellbeing, inspires reflection, or aids recovery. Open call for art created in response to lived experience of mental health, disability, or health journey. All mediums welcome including photography, painting, film, sculpture, ceramics, poetry, and installation. Curated by photographic artist Livvy Eden. Exhibition runs 22 May – 6 June 2026 at 103 Walcot Street, Bath. Selected artists asked for £25 participation donation.
calls.summary: Exploring how creative practice nurtures wellbeing, aids recovery. Open to lived experience of mental health. Bath, UK.
prose: Fringe Arts Bath is the UK contemporary arts platform that runs an annual fringe festival in Bath. Nest is a 2026 group exhibition curated by photographic artist Livvy Eden — exploring how creative practice nurtures wellbeing, inspires reflection, or aids recovery.

The brief asks for art created in response to lived experience of mental health, disability, or health journey. The exhibition is multidisciplinary by design: photography, painting, film, sculpture, ceramics, poetry, and installation are all eligible. AI-generated work is accepted but must be disclosed.
Selected artists exhibit at 103 Walcot Street, Bath, May 22 – June 6, 2026.
Application is free. Selected artists are asked for a £25 participation donation — payment is conditional on selection rather than upfront. Submission is by email.
The 2026 deadline was April 10.

calls.title: Michael P. Smith Fund for Documentary Photography 2025
calls.description: Annual grant honoring legendary New Orleans documentary photographer Michael P. Smith. Awards cash prizes and exhibition opportunities to Gulf Coast photographers whose work combines artistic excellence and a sustained commitment to a cultural documentary project. Open to photographers residing in Gulf Coast states: Texas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama, Georgia, and Florida. Subject matter not limited to Gulf Coast region. Grant winner receives $3,000, PhotoNOLA Portfolio Review access, NOPA Palladium membership, and exhibition. Two honorable mentions receive Portfolio reviews and membership. Top 10 finalists listed on NOPA website. Winner donates two prints to NOPA permanent collection.
jury: Alyssa Ortega Coppelman, Photography Consultant & Photo Editor
calls.summary: Annual grant for Gulf Coast photographers. $3,000 winner prize, PhotoNOLA Portfolio Review, and exhibition.
prose: The Michael P. Smith Fund for Documentary Photography is an annual grant administered by the New Orleans Photo Alliance (NOPA). It honors Michael P. Smith, the New Orleans documentary photographer who spent decades photographing the city's musical, religious, and cultural life — work now held in the Historic New Orleans Collection.

The grant supports Gulf Coast photographers whose work combines artistic excellence with sustained commitment to a cultural documentary project. Eligibility is restricted by residency: applicants must reside in Texas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama, Georgia, or Florida. Subject matter, however, is not limited to the Gulf Coast region — the photographer must be from there, the work need not be about there.

What's offered: the winner receives $3,000, access to the PhotoNOLA Portfolio Review, NOPA Palladium-level membership, and a NOPA exhibition. Two honorable mentions receive Portfolio Review access and NOPA membership. The top 10 finalists are listed on the NOPA website. The winner donates two prints to NOPA's permanent collection.
The 2025 cycle judge is Alyssa Ortega Coppelman, photography consultant and photo editor. Submission is through CaFÉ with 10–20 images and a $25 fee. The 2025 deadline was May 4, 2026.

calls.title: Camille Lepage Award 2026
calls.org: Association Camille Lepage – On est ensemble
calls.description: Annual €8,000 award supporting a photojournalist committed to a long-term reporting project. Established by the family of Camille Lepage, the photojournalist killed while reporting in the Central African Republic in 2014. Funded for the tenth year by the SAIF (Société des Auteurs des Arts Visuels et de l'Image Fixe). The award helps a photographer carry out and complete a reporting project already under way. Open to professional photojournalists with no restriction on age, gender, or nationality. Award presented in September 2026 at the International Festival of Photojournalism Visa pour l'Image-Perpignan. The winning report must be completed within one year so that it can be presented at the 2027 festival as an exhibition or evening show.
calls.summary: €8,000 prize for a photojournalist on a long-term reporting project. Free entry, worldwide. Presented at Visa pour l'Image-Perpignan.
prose: The Camille Lepage Award is an annual €8,000 prize supporting a photojournalist on a long-term reporting project. It was established by the family of Camille Lepage, the French photojournalist killed in May 2014 while reporting in the Central African Republic. The 2026 edition is the tenth funded by SAIF (Société des Auteurs des Arts Visuels et de l'Image Fixe).

The structure is unusual for photojournalism prizes: the award is intended specifically to help a photographer carry out and complete a reporting project that is already under way — not to fund a new project from scratch. The €8,000 is a working grant, not a recognition payment.

Eligibility is open to professional photojournalists with no restriction on age, gender, or nationality. The award is presented in September 2026 at Visa pour l'Image-Perpignan, the International Festival of Photojournalism. The winning report must be completed within one year so it can be presented at the 2027 festival as an exhibition or evening show.
Application is free. Submission is through Visa pour l'Image with 10–20 images. The 2026 deadline was May 4.

calls.title: Love & Romance Show
calls.description: Online exhibition exploring how love has transformed alongside cultural and societal changes, and how those shifts shape personal experience today. Submit up to 3 images connecting the theme of love and romance. Virtual exhibition launches May 7, 2026.
calls.summary: Online exhibition exploring how love has transformed alongside cultural and societal changes.
prose: Blue Sky Gallery is the long-running Portland, Oregon nonprofit photography gallery, also known as the Oregon Center for the Photographic Arts. The Love & Romance Show is one of its themed online exhibitions. The 2026 brief asks how love has transformed alongside cultural and societal changes, and how those shifts shape personal experience today.
The framing is generational and historical rather than purely sentimental — applicants are invited to consider love and romance as moving targets shaped by their cultural context.
Selection results in a virtual exhibition that launches May 7, 2026.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is by Google Form with up to 3 images. Application is free.
The 2026 deadline was April 17; results announced May 7, 2026 with the exhibition opening.

calls.title: EDITION 502 — Open Call for Photo Edition
calls.description: Open call for an independent 6×9 photo edition of 12 small photographs. EDITION 502 covers all design, production, and distribution costs. Author receives a percentage of sales. Looking for authors with a clear visual language and comprehensible concept, regardless of education or professional background. Submit 12 photographs with serial character, a cover sheet, and a text (max 2,400 characters).
calls.summary: Independent 6x9 photo edition of 12 small photographs. All production and distribution costs covered.
prose: EDITION 502 is an independent photo-edition publisher producing small-format 6×9 cm photo editions — sets of 12 small printed photographs. The format is intentionally diminutive, between a series of postcards and a small portfolio. The platform's open call selects new editions to publish.
EDITION 502 covers all design, production, and distribution costs. The author receives a percentage of sales rather than an upfront fee — production-share rather than acquisition.

Selection is concept-driven. The platform looks for authors with a clear visual language and comprehensible concept, regardless of education or professional background. The brief is open to photographers without formal photography training.
Each submission includes 12 photographs with serial character, a cover sheet, and a text of up to 2,400 characters. Submission is by email. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was April 30.

calls.title: Texture of Light
calls.description: Photography exhibition exploring light as a tactile, physical medium. Submit images where light feels like a material — surface tension on objects, atmospheric mass in fog or dust, architecture of shadow, or abstract luminescence through long exposures and macro work. Selected images will be printed and displayed matted and framed at Western Market in Washington, DC. Exhibition opens May 2, 2026.
calls.summary: Exploring light as a tactile, physical medium — surface tension, atmospheric mass, architecture of shadow. Washington, DC.
prose: Pro Photo DC is a Washington, DC photography organization. Texture of Light is one of its juried thematic exhibitions. The brief asks for photographs where light functions as a tactile, physical medium — work where light feels like material rather than illumination.
The brief specifies the registers it wants: surface tension on objects, atmospheric mass in fog or dust, the architecture of shadow, or abstract luminescence through long exposures and macro work.
Selected images are printed, matted, and framed for display at Western Market in Washington, DC. The exhibition opens May 2, 2026 — Pro Photo DC handles production for selected work.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is by Google Form with up to 3 images. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was April 1.

calls.title: Anja Niedringhaus Courage in Photojournalism Award 2026
calls.description: Award honoring courageous, high-impact photojournalism by women, nonbinary, and gender-diverse creatives. Submit 12 photographs (6 from 2024–2026, 6 from broader career) plus a 500-word statement. Open to women, nonbinary, and gender non-conforming photojournalists working full-time in journalism. Self-nomination or third-party nomination accepted. Named after Pulitzer Prize-winning photographer Anja Niedringhaus (1965–2014).
jury: Whitney Johnson, President & CEO, Catalina Island Conservancy
Brent Lewis, Photo Editor, The New York Times
Enric Marti, Deputy Director of Photography, Associated Press
Benny Snyder, Photo Editor & Contest Coordinator, Associated Press
Sandra M. Stevenson, Deputy Director of Photography, The Washington Post
Bernadette Tuazon, Director of Photography, CNN Digital
calls.summary: Honoring courageous photojournalism by women, nonbinary, and gender-diverse creatives. Named after Pulitzer winner.
prose: The Anja Niedringhaus Courage in Photojournalism Award is administered by the International Women's Media Foundation (IWMF). It honors Anja Niedringhaus, the Pulitzer Prize–winning Associated Press photographer killed in 2014 while covering the elections in Afghanistan.
The award honors courageous, high-impact photojournalism by women, nonbinary, and gender-diverse creatives. Top prize is $20,000.

The 2026 jury draws from major US news organizations: Brent Lewis (Photo Editor, The New York Times), Enric Marti and Benny Snyder (both Associated Press), Sandra M. Stevenson (Deputy Director of Photography, The Washington Post), Bernadette Tuazon (Director of Photography, CNN Digital), Corinne Dufka (independent researcher/advisor), and Whitney Johnson (President & CEO, Catalina Island Conservancy).

Each application includes 12 photographs (6 from 2024–2026 and 6 from broader career) plus a 500-word statement. Self-nomination or third-party nomination accepted. Eligibility is restricted to women, nonbinary, and gender non-conforming photojournalists working full-time in journalism.
Submission is through Picter. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was March 31; results announced May 2026.

calls.title: LT5 Alternative Photography Show
calls.description: Open call for photographers working in alternative photography — including toy and plastic cameras, Polaroid, pinhole, photograms, and other alternative processes. Submit up to 2 works for exhibition at KALEID Gallery in San Jose, CA. Opening reception May 1 during South First Fridays Art Walk. Exhibition runs May 1–29, 2026. Contact curator via DM or email for submission details.
calls.summary: Toy cameras, Polaroid, pinhole, photograms, and alternative processes. Exhibition at KALEID Gallery, San Jose, CA.
prose: KALEID Gallery is a San Jose, California artist-run gallery. The LT5 Alternative Photography Show is the gallery's recurring call for work made through alternative photographic processes — toy and plastic cameras, Polaroid, pinhole, photograms, and other process-restricted approaches.
Selection is by curator Robertino Ragazza.

Selected work is shown at KALEID Gallery in San Jose, with the opening reception on May 1 during South First Fridays Art Walk — the monthly downtown San Jose gallery event. The exhibition runs May 1–29, 2026.
Eligibility is restricted by process: alternative photography only. Submission is by email with up to 2 works. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was April 12; results announced April 15, 2026.

calls.title: Artphilein Open Call 2026
calls.description: Open call for photographers exploring adolescence from an internal perspective — digital culture, identity negotiation, and contemporary pressures experienced by young people. Submit a single PDF with 10–20 images. Winner receives a solo exhibition at Artphilein Library in Autumn 2026, publication in Artphilein Dossier, and CHF 1,000 cash award.
jury: Caterina De Pietri, Curator, Artphilein Foundation
calls.summary: Exploring adolescence — digital culture, identity, contemporary pressures. Solo exhibition and CHF 1,000 award.
prose: The De Pietri Artphilein Foundation is a Lugano, Switzerland photography foundation that runs an annual open call. The 2026 brief is themed around adolescence from an internal perspective — work engaging with digital culture, identity negotiation, and contemporary pressures experienced by young people.
The brief asks photographers to look at adolescence from inside the experience rather than as observation from outside.
Selection is by Caterina De Pietri, curator of the Artphilein Foundation. Single-juror selection.
The winner receives a solo exhibition at Artphilein Library in Autumn 2026, publication in Artphilein Dossier (the foundation's publication series), and CHF 1,000 cash award.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is by Google Form with a single PDF containing 10–20 images. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was April 15; results announced April 30, 2026.

calls.title: L'Image Satellite 2026
calls.description: Open call for photographers and visual artists working with contemporary still image practices including documentary, experimental, vernacular, and hybrid image forms. Selected artists exhibit at L'Image Satellite festival in Nice, September–October 2026. Artists receive €500 presentation fee, round-trip artwork transport, accommodation, and travel. Submit up to 20 JPEG images via online form and email.
calls.summary: Selected artists exhibit in Nice, Sep-Oct 2026. €500 honorarium, transport, accommodation, and travel covered.
prose: L'Image Satellite is a French photography festival held in Nice, organized by Sept Off, an independent photography association based in southern France. The festival focuses specifically on contemporary still-image practices.

The brief is unusually broad in what counts as photographic work. Eligible approaches include documentary photography, fine art practices, vernacular photography, and experimental work. Eligible presentation formats span printed images, displayed prints, published works, projected images, and animated images — the festival treats photography as a broader domain than the gallery-print tradition.

The festival proper runs three weeks across September and October 2026. Selected artists exhibit for the full duration, with attendance at the vernissage required and participation in installation setup encouraged.

What's covered: a €500 artist presentation fee, round-trip artwork transportation, plus photographer travel and lodging for the festival. The package is structured to ensure artists can meaningfully participate without their own funding.

Submission is free. Each applicant submits up to 20 images in JPEG format at 2400 pixels on the longest side, 300 dpi, accompanied by an optional supplementary PDF (max 20MB) showing broader series or installation views. Submissions are made by email; confirmation arrives within 72 hours of complete submission. The 2026 deadline is May 10.

calls.title: Fabula Works — Duo/Solo Show in Rome
calls.description: Inaugural open call for two photographers to exhibit in a five-week show at Millepiani Gallery in Rome. No thematic restrictions — submit 10–25 photographs as a cohesive series or curated selection. All printing and promotional costs fully covered. Opening reception June 26, 2026. Exhibition runs June 26–July 31, 2026.
calls.summary: Two photographers exhibit at Millepiani Gallery in Rome. No thematic restrictions. All costs covered.
prose: Fabula Works is a curatorial platform launching its inaugural open call in 2026. The first call is for a five-week exhibition at Millepiani Gallery in Rome — running June 26 through July 31, 2026, with an opening reception June 26 at 6 PM. The gallery is open Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 7 PM, with free admission.

Two photographers are selected for the exhibition. The organizers note they reserve the right to present a solo exhibition instead if a single submission warrants it — a deliberate flexibility built into the inaugural call rather than a fixed two-artist format.

There is no thematic restriction. All photography genres are welcome. Selection is based on curatorial coherence and artistic strength — applicants submit 10 to 25 photographs as a cohesive series, two cohesive series, or a curated selection.

Selected photographers receive: full coverage of printing costs, exhibition promotion, and gallery installation. The €25 application fee is described as a non-refundable contribution rather than a competitive submission charge.

Eligibility requires applicants to be 18 or over. Submissions consist of a portfolio PDF, artist biography, and artist statement. AI-generated images are not accepted. The 2026 deadline is Sunday May 17 at 23:59 CET.

calls.title: Rarefied Light 2026
calls.description: Annual statewide juried exhibition with juror Nevada Wier (National Geographic, Smithsonian). Submit 1–20 images of any photographic form except AI-generated work. Selected work travels to galleries in Anchorage, Fairbanks, Juneau, and Cordova from October 2026. Includes three-day workshop (August 14–16) on color, light, action, and pattern in image-making.
calls.summary: Statewide juried exhibition with Nevada Wier (Nat Geo). Travels to four Alaska galleries from October 2026.
prose: Rarefied Light is the Alaska Photographic Center's annual statewide juried exhibition. The 2026 cycle is juried by Nevada Wier, a photographer whose work has appeared in National Geographic, Smithsonian, and Getty Images. The exhibition is restricted to Alaska-based photographers — Rarefied Light is one of the few photography prizes structured specifically around the state.

Selected work tours four Alaska galleries from October 2026 onward, traveling between Anchorage, Fairbanks, Juneau, and Cordova. The traveling format means accepted work reaches audiences across Alaska's geographically dispersed cities — a different kind of exhibition reach than a single venue stop.

The 2026 cycle includes a three-day workshop with the juror on August 14–16, 2026: "Seeing Photographically — Color, Light, Action, Pattern," instruction on converting visual observation into compelling photographs. Workshop fees are $250 (APC member), $300 (non-member), or $275 (member renewal plus workshop). A jury lecture takes place August 13.

Submissions accept up to 20 images of any photographic form except AI-generated work. Entry fees are $15 to $30. Eligibility is restricted to Alaska residents. Submissions go through CaFÉ; the 2026 deadline is June 10 at 10 PM AST, with results in July.

calls.title: Prix Mustaqbal 2026 — Momentum
calls.description: Annual competition promoting emerging contemporary creation. Open to artists aged 18–35, Moroccan or foreign residents in Morocco, working in drawing, painting, installation, photography, or sound art. No thematic constraints. Approximately 15 finalists exhibited at Artorium in Casablanca. Winner receives artist residency at Jardin Rouge and duo-shows in Paris and Casablanca.
calls.summary: Emerging artists 18-35, Moroccan or foreign residents in Morocco. Winner receives Jardin Rouge residency.
prose: Prix Mustaqbal is administered by Fondation TGCC, a Moroccan foundation focused on emerging contemporary creation. The foundation is led by president Meryem Bouzoubaa, and the prize was established in 2021 — the 2026 cycle is the sixth edition. The 2026 theme is "Momentum."

Eligibility is restricted to artists aged 18–35 who are either Moroccan citizens or foreign residents of Morocco. Both trained and self-taught artists are welcome. Eligible media: drawing, painting, installation, photography, and sound art.

Three winners are selected from approximately 15 finalists who exhibit at Artorium in Casablanca. Cash prizes are awarded in Moroccan dirhams (specific amounts are not published on the public landing page). The first-place winner receives an additional substantial prize package: an artist residency at Jardin Rouge (the well-known Moroccan residency) plus two duo-shows — one in Paris (spring 2027) and one at Artorium (November 2027).

Selection is two-phase: initial portfolio review by a panel of artists, professionals, and art critics, then in-person jury defense for finalists. Winners enter a one-year contract with the foundation that includes residency participation, social media content creation, roundtable participation, and children's workshops.

There is no application fee. Applications are made via email and SwissTransfer with 4 to 8 images. The 2026 application window runs February 16 through May 16; exhibition and winner announcement in September 2026.

calls.title: No Place Art — Edition Two: MATERIALITY
calls.description: International open call for artists working in printmaking, painting and mixed media. 80 artists selected for 10-day exhibition at The Handbag Factory in London. 30+ awards from 19 awarding bodies including purchase awards up to £1,000, artist residencies, solo and group exhibitions, mentoring, editorial features, materials vouchers, and workshops.
jury: Conor Rush, Artist & Founder, Starving Artists
Giles Duley, Photographer & CEO, Legacy of War Foundation
Matthew Burrows, Painter & Founder, Artist Support Pledge
Pia Austin-Little, Co-Founder, Austin & Checker Art Advisory
Roland-Philippe Kretzschmar, Founder, The Art Bystander
calls.summary: 80 artists exhibited in London. 30+ awards including purchase awards, residencies, and solo exhibitions.
prose: No Place Art is an artist-led initiative connecting artists with opportunities, professional development, and visibility through curated exhibitions and partner programs. "Edition Two: MATERIALITY" is the platform's themed open call for printmaking, painting, and mixed media work — note that this call is not specifically photography-focused, though photo-based prints and image-led mixed media practice are eligible.

The brief asks for work that engages with materiality as a conversation between the medium, the artist, and the viewer — exploring how surface textures and tactile qualities function as artistic language. Submissions to this edition center on printmaking and painting practices, with framed works accepted up to 2 × 2 meters.

Eighty artists are selected for the exhibition, running September 17 through 27, 2026 at The Handbag Factory in Vauxhall, London. The award structure is unusually rich: 19 awarding bodies offer 40+ awards including purchase awards up to £1,000, artist residencies of 1 to 4 months, solo and group exhibitions, materials vouchers from £50 to £500, mentoring programs of 3 to 12 months, and gallery representation up to 1 year.

Selection is by a jury that includes Aga Kubish (printmaker), Conor Rush (artist and founder of Starving Artists), Geoffrey Howe (mixed media artist), Giles Duley (photographer and CEO of Legacy of War Foundation), Matthew Burrows (painter and founder of Artist Support Pledge), Pia Austin-Little (Austin & Checker Art Advisory), and Roland-Philippe Kretzschmar (The Art Bystander).
Entry fee is £24. Eligibility is open to artists 18 and over. Submissions accept up to 5 images via DappleHQ. The 2026 deadline is May 31; results announced June 22.

calls.title: 59 Rivoli — Artist Residency 2026
calls.description: 6-month artist residency at the iconic 59 Rivoli in the heart of Paris, a former squat turned official artist residence hosting 30 artists with free open studios visited by the public. Open to visual artists and sculptors of all ages, internationally. Residencies begin May 2026.
calls.summary: 6-month residency at iconic 59 Rivoli in Paris — former squat turned official artist residence. Free open studios.
prose: 59 Rivoli is an artist residence in central Paris, located at 59 rue de Rivoli — directly between the Louvre and the Place du Châtelet. The building started as an illegal squat in the late 1990s and has since been formalized as an official Paris artist residence. It hosts 30 artists across multiple floors of free open studios that are visited daily by the public.
The residency runs six months. The 2026 cycle begins in May. Eligibility is open internationally to visual artists and sculptors of any age.

The structural premise distinguishes 59 Rivoli from most residencies: studios are open to the public during gallery hours, with thousands of visitors per week. Residents work with that exposure as part of the practice.
Application is free, made through Google Form with a single PDF dossier. The 2026 deadline was April 17.

calls.title: LensCulture Critics' Choice 2026
calls.description: Global competition where 20 leading photography critics and curators each select 3 photographers. Up to 60 winners featured in LensCulture online gallery. Top Ten receive $1,000 cash grant each plus international group exhibition at Photo London 2027. Exposure to 3 million global audience. Open to all photographers worldwide.
jury: Alex Pollack, Director of Photography, National Geographic
Anna Planas, Artistic Director, Paris Photo
Cassidy Paul, Managing Editor Digital, Aperture
Claartje van Dijk, Senior Curator, Foam Photography Museum
Crista Dix, Executive Director, Griffin Museum
Darius Himes, International Head of Photographs, Christie's
Enrico Stefanelli, Artistic Director, Photolux Festival
Fiona Shields, Head of Photography, The Guardian
Jane Yeomans, Senior Photo Editor, Bloomberg
Jessie Wender, Photo Editor, The New York Times
Rhea Combs, Director of Curatorial Affairs, National Portrait Gallery
Rose Shoshana, Owner & Director, Rose Gallery
Taous R. Dahmani, Curator, The Photographers' Gallery
Xavier Canonne, Director, Musée de la Photographie
Yuri Yamada, Curator, Tokyo Photographic Art Museum
calls.summary: 20 leading critics each select 3 photographers. Top Ten receive $1,000 and exhibition at Photo London 2027.
prose: LensCulture Critics' Choice is one of LensCulture's annual competitions. The structural premise distinguishes it from most photo prizes: rather than a single jury voting on a shortlist, 20 leading photography critics and curators each independently select 3 photographers from the entries, producing up to 60 winners — a curated network selection rather than a competitive ranking.

The 2026 panel of 20 critics is drawn from major photography institutions and publications: Anna Planas (Artistic Director, Paris Photo), Alex Pollack (Director of Photography, National Geographic), Claartje van Dijk (Senior Curator, Foam), Crista Dix (Executive Director, Griffin Museum), Darius Himes (International Head of Photographs, Christie's), Fiona Shields (Head of Photography, The Guardian), Jessie Wender (Photo Editor, The New York Times), Jim Casper (Editor-in-Chief, LensCulture), Rhea Combs (National Portrait Gallery), Yuri Yamada (Tokyo Photographic Art Museum), and others.

The Top Ten — a smaller subset selected from the 60 — each receive a $1,000 cash grant plus inclusion in an international group exhibition at Photo London 2027. Up to 60 winners are featured in a LensCulture online gallery and exposed to LensCulture's 3-million-person global audience.

Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through LensCulture with 1–10 images. Fee structure: free for one image, $10 per additional image. The 2026 deadline was April 22; results announced May 1, 2026.

calls.title: Analog Sparks — International Film Photography Awards 2026
calls.description: International awards discovering and promoting analog photographers worldwide. Categories: Architecture, Fine Art, Human, Lifestyle, Nature, Photo Journalism, Technique, Zines & Photo Books. Accepts color/B&W film, instant film, collodion, alternative techniques, and hybrid analog-digital (no purely digital). Winners exhibited at House of Lucie in Athens and Ostuni.
calls.summary: Discovering and promoting analog photographers. Exhibited at House of Lucie in Athens and Ostuni.
prose: Analog Sparks is an international competition specifically for film and analog photography, founded by Hossein Farmani (founder of the Lucie Foundation and IPA) and Reka Koti. Submissions are accepted in eight categories: Architecture, Fine Art, Human, Lifestyle, Nature, Photojournalism, Technique, and Zines & Photo Books.

The competition accepts color and black-and-white film, instant film, collodion, alternative techniques, and hybrid analog-digital workflows where the original capture was on film. Purely digital work is not accepted. The main prize is €1,000, and category winners are exhibited at House of Lucie galleries in Athens and Ostuni.

The 2026 jury comprises Barna Erdesz (art director and gallerist), Danial Shah (documentary photographer), Eva Szombat (visual artist), Hossein Farmani (founder), Ibrahim Mursal (visual artist and writer), Kenro Izu (photographer), Kira Krasz (visual artist), Mikkel Horlyck (photojournalist), Mo Laudi (curator), and Wanda Martin (Canon Ambassador).

Entry fees follow a tiered deadline structure with progressively lower discounts: 10% off through January 23, 5% off through March 15, then standard rates through May 15, June 19 (extended), and the final deadline July 31. Eligibility is open to photographers 18 and over worldwide, including students and emerging artists.

calls.title: Athens Photo Festival 2026
calls.description: Major international photography festival at Benaki Museum / Pireos 138. Approximately 80 artists selected for exhibition across 3,000+ square meters. Production costs covered, two-night accommodation provided. Additional opportunities include portfolio reviews, Talent Lab, artist residency (€600 honorarium). All genres welcome — fine art, conceptual, documentary, installation.
calls.summary: Major international festival at Benaki Museum. ~80 artists exhibited across 3,000+ sqm. Production costs covered.
prose: Athens Photo Festival is the major international photography festival held annually in Athens, Greece. The festival's main exhibition runs at the Benaki Museum / Pireos 138 — Athens's principal venue for contemporary art programming.

Approximately 80 artists are selected for the festival exhibition across 3,000+ square meters of exhibition space. Production costs are covered by the festival, plus two-night accommodation in Athens for selected artists.

Beyond the main exhibition, selected artists access additional opportunities: portfolio reviews, Talent Lab (the festival's mentorship program), and an artist residency component with a €600 honorarium.
All genres welcome — fine art, conceptual, documentary, installation. Eligibility is open globally.
Submission is through the festival's website with up to 20 images. Fee is €25. The 2026 deadline was March 17; results announced March 30, 2026.

calls.title: Griffin Museum — Material Work: Toil & Grace
calls.description: Online exhibition exploring the difficulty and beauty of labor in all forms — artistic, physical, emotional, intellectual, domestic, agricultural, industrial, invisible, and performative. Images of work that feel earned, revealing humanity found in toil. Online exhibition April 20 – May 20, 2026.
calls.summary: Exploring the difficulty and beauty of labor in all forms. Images of work that feel earned. Free online exhibition.
jury: Crista Dix, Executive Director, Griffin Museum of Photography
prose: The Griffin Museum of Photography is the Winchester, Massachusetts photography museum, one of the major US photography institutions. Material Work: Toil & Grace is one of its themed online exhibitions.

The brief takes labor as subject: the difficulty and beauty of work in all its forms — artistic, physical, emotional, intellectual, domestic, agricultural, industrial, invisible, and performative. The selection is interested in images of work that feel earned — humanity found in toil rather than romanticized labor.
Selection is by Crista Dix, Executive Director of the Griffin Museum.
Selected work is shown in an online exhibition running April 20 – May 20, 2026 on the Griffin Museum's website.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is by Google Form, single image. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was April 10; selection announced April 20, 2026 with the exhibition opening.

calls.title: RBSA Summer Show 2026
calls.description: Largest annual open exhibition at RBSA Gallery in Birmingham. All techniques and media welcome including photography and digital. Open to UK and international artists. £600 first prize, £300 second prize, plus highly commended certificates.
calls.summary: Largest annual open exhibition at RBSA Gallery Birmingham. All techniques and media. £600 first prize.
prose: The Royal Birmingham Society of Artists (RBSA) is a Birmingham-based artist-led society dating to 1814. The Summer Show is its largest annual open exhibition at the RBSA Gallery in central Birmingham — open submission across all media.

All techniques and media are accepted: painting, drawing, printmaking, sculpture, mixed media, photography, and digital work. The show is open to UK and international artists with no eligibility restriction by career stage.
Prizes are £600 (first), £300 (second), and a set of highly commended certificates. Selected works hang in the RBSA's main gallery space.
Submissions are through Typeform with up to 3 images. Fee is tiered (£13–£39, with reduced rates for RBSA Friends and members). The 2026 deadline was May 5; results announced May 21, 2026.

calls.title: Womanhood
calls.description: Sixth quarterly open call from Photobook Cafe and Rapid Eye Darkrooms exploring the theme of Womanhood with guest judge Francesca Allen. Open to anyone engaging with or experiencing Womanhood in all its forms. 35 selected photographers featured in group exhibition and printed zine at The Photobook Cafe in London. Three Best in Show winners receive a complimentary group exhibition with printing by Rapid Eye Darkrooms and curation by Francesca Allen.
calls.summary: Exploring Womanhood in all its forms — group exhibition and zine. Guest judge Francesca Allen.
calls.verifyNote: Site shows 2025 dates — this is a typo on their end. Press release confirms 2026. Do NOT change the deadline.
prose: The Photobook Cafe is a London photography venue with a café, exhibition space, and bookstore focused on photobooks. Rapid Eye Darkrooms is a London photographic printing service. Together they run a quarterly themed open call. Womanhood is the sixth cycle in the series.

The brief is open in approach: anyone engaging with or experiencing Womanhood in any of its forms. The theme is held broadly — work doesn't need to be by women, but it needs to engage with Womanhood as subject.
The 2026 guest judge is photographer Francesca Allen.

Selection structure has two tiers. Thirty-five selected photographers are featured in a group exhibition and printed zine at The Photobook Cafe in London. From the 35, three Best in Show winners receive a complimentary group exhibition with printing by Rapid Eye Darkrooms and curation by Francesca Allen.
Submission is through Photobook Cafe's website with 2 images per entry. Fee is £25. The 2026 deadline was April 20; results announced April 25, 2026.

calls.title: EXPOSED feat Witty Books Dummy Award 2026
calls.description: International competition to publish an unpublished photobook. Winning project edited and published by Witty Books (400+ copies). 20 finalist dummies exhibited at Torino Photo Festival. Open to photographers and collectives with completed but unpublished editorial layouts.
calls.summary: Competition to publish an unpublished photobook via Witty Books. 20 finalist dummies exhibited at Torino Photo Festival.
prose: EXPOSED is the Torino photography festival; Witty Books is the Turin-based independent photobook publisher. The Dummy Award is a joint project between the two organizations: a photobook dummy competition with a publication outcome.
The brief is open in subject but specific in stage: applicants submit completed but unpublished editorial layouts. Both individual photographers and collectives are eligible.

Selection structure: the winning project is edited and published by Witty Books in an edition of 400+ copies. Twenty finalist dummies are exhibited physically at Torino Photo Festival — providing extended exposure beyond the single winner.
Selection is by Tommaso Parrillo (Witty Books), Giulia Ninotta (EXPOSED), and photographer Karla Hiraldo Voleau.
Submission is by email with one PDF dummy. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was April 19; results announced early May 2026.

calls.title: 43rd Center Annual
calls.description: Houston Center for Photography's annual group exhibition, now in its 43rd year. Seeks to highlight current themes, technologies, and practices in photography. Features diverse works from HCP members worldwide — emerging, mid-career, and established photographers. Two artists selected for $500 HCP Juried Membership Honoraria. This year juried by Asha Iman Veal, curator for globally collaborative exhibitions of contemporary art. Exhibition runs June 4 – August 16, 2026.
jury: Asha Iman Veal, Curator and Professor, School of the Art Institute of Chicago
calls.summary: Houston Center for Photography's annual group exhibition. Juried by Asha Iman Veal. $5,000 MFAH purchase award.
prose: Houston Center for Photography (HCP) is a Houston-based nonprofit photography institution. The Center Annual is its longest-running group exhibition. The 2026 edition is the 43rd cycle.

The brief surveys current themes, technologies, and practices in photography rather than holding to a fixed theme. Eligibility is restricted to HCP members worldwide — emerging, mid-career, and established photographers all eligible.
Selection is by Asha Iman Veal, curator for globally collaborative exhibitions of contemporary art and Professor at the School of the Art Institute of Chicago.
Two artists are selected for $500 HCP Juried Membership Honoraria. Selected work is shown in the physical exhibition at HCP's Houston gallery, June 4 – August 16, 2026 — a long summer run.
Submission is through Submittable with up to 5 images. Application is free for HCP members. The 2026 deadline was April 19; results announced early May 2026.

calls.title: ZRNO Festival 2026 — Open Call
calls.description: International festival of alternative photography. Seeking analog photographers working with alternative and noble processes — cyanotype, wet plate, collodion, and experimental techniques. Single works or cohesive bodies of work welcome. Theme: Unfocus to see.
jury: Drago Vejnovic, Professor, Academy of Arts Banja Luka
Ivana Brezovac, Professor, Academy of Arts Novi Sad
calls.summary: International festival of alternative photography. Analog and noble processes. Theme: Unfocus to see.
prose: ZRNO Festival is an international festival of alternative photography held in Skopje, North Macedonia. The festival is process-restricted by design: it focuses on analog and noble processes — cyanotype, wet plate, collodion, and experimental techniques. The 2026 theme is Unfocus to see.
The brief accepts both single works and cohesive bodies of work. Submitted work must engage with at least one alternative process — not standard digital or film capture.

The 2026 jury reflects the festival's focus on alternative and noble processes: Anne-Mette S. Sommer-Kelter (Polaroid photographer), Drago Vejnovic (Professor, Academy of Arts Banja Luka), Eva Schlogl (visual artist and architect), Pep Minguez (Director, Revela'T Festival), Ivana Brezovac (Professor, Academy of Arts Novi Sad), Natasa Takac (visual and media artist), Florian Kopr (photographer and printmaker), and Sasho Alushevski (alternative photographer).
Selection results in inclusion in the festival exhibition. Submission is by email with up to 4 images. Fee is €21. The 2026 deadline was April 20; results announced May 15, 2026.

calls.title: PN Awards 2026 — Book Prize & Project Grant
calls.description: Annual book prize honoring innovation in photography scholarship, expression, and dissemination. Project grant supports emerging scholars, curators, and artists with funds to complete works in progress.
jury: Lucy Gallun, Curator of Photography, MoMA
Ileana L. Selejan, Lecturer, University of Edinburgh
Giulia Paoletti, Associate Professor, University of Virginia
calls.summary: Book prize for innovation in photography scholarship. Project grant for emerging scholars and curators.
prose: The Photography Network is a membership-based academic and curatorial organization for photography scholars, historians, curators, and artists. The PN Awards run two parallel programs: the Book Prize and the Project Grant.

The Book Prize honors innovation in photography scholarship, expression, and distribution. Eligible work includes edited volumes, exhibition catalogs, photobooks, and scholarly monographs — the prize is open to authored or edited work by current Photography Network members. The structure is unusual in that it treats the photobook as scholarship rather than purely as artistic output.

The Project Grant supports emerging scholars, curators, and artists with funds to complete works in progress — publications, articles, exhibitions, or research projects. Both programs require English-language submissions.

The 2026 jury comprises Lucy Gallun (Curator of Photography at MoMA), Ileana L. Selejan (Lecturer at the University of Edinburgh), and Giulia Paoletti (Associate Professor at the University of Virginia). The deadline is June 15, 2026, with results announced December 2026. Specific prize amounts are not published on the awards landing page; applicants should contact the awards coordinator (photographynetworkawards@gmail.com) for current details.

calls.title: KYOTOGRAPHIE Photo Zine Showcase
calls.description: Special exhibition within the KYOTOGRAPHIE Photobook Fair for emerging artists. Zines shown to international editors, photographers, curators, and publishers. Exhibition May 9–10, 2026 at Rohm Theatre Kyoto.
calls.summary: Zines shown to international editors, curators, and publishers at KYOTOGRAPHIE Photobook Fair in Kyoto.
prose: KYOTOGRAPHIE is the international photography festival held annually in Kyoto each spring. The KYOTOGRAPHIE Photobook Fair runs as part of the festival programming. The Photo Zine Showcase is a special exhibition within the fair specifically for emerging artists.

The format is showcase rather than competition. Selected zines are physically displayed at the festival's Photobook Fair, where they are seen by an audience of international editors, photographers, curators, and publishers attending KYOTOGRAPHIE. The intent is exposure and connection rather than prize.
The 2026 showcase is held May 9–10 at Rohm Theatre Kyoto, the festival's main venue.

Eligibility is restricted to emerging artists. Application is free, made through Google Form. Each photographer submits one zine for consideration. The 2026 deadline was April 20; results announced late April 2026.

calls.title: Fotografiska Emerging Artist Platform
calls.description: Platform with multiple open calls for emerging photographers including exhibitions at Fotografiska museums, the UN Headquarters, and brand collaborations. Also functions as a portfolio page for discovery.
jury: Pauline Benthede, VP Artistic Direction, Fotografiska
calls.summary: Multiple open calls for emerging photographers. Exhibitions at Fotografiska museums and the UN Headquarters.
prose: Fotografiska's emerging program is structured around continuous open calls plus rotating themed cycles. The "Foto of the Day" track runs weekly: seven images selected from open submissions, featured on Fotografiska's website and social channels. Themed calls run alongside it, with regional eligibility for some — Sweden-only for the Stockholm shows, Baltics-and-Finland for Tallinn — and global eligibility for others.

Selected work has been shown at Fotografiska's museum locations in Berlin, Stockholm, and Tallinn. The platform doesn't publish guaranteed compensation; outcomes vary by call. Submissions are free, limited to three images per cycle, and AI-generated work is excluded.

The platform's permanent jury includes James Nachtwey and Pauline Benthede, Fotografiska's VP of Artistic Direction. Themed calls bring in additional jurors specific to each theme. The "Home" call is currently open with a July 12, 2026 deadline; "Foto of the Day" remains continuous.

calls.title: Fotografiska Emerging Portfolio Review 2026
calls.description: Free open call for one-on-one online portfolio reviews with Fotografiska curators. Selected applicants receive a 20-minute review session on July 3, 2026 with Jessica Jarl (Global Director of Exhibitions, Stockholm) and Thomas Schäfer (Director of Exhibitions, Fotografiska Berlin). Open to image-makers of all levels with a cohesive visual project.
jury: Jessica Jarl, Global Director of Exhibitions, Fotografiska
Thomas Schäfer, Director of Exhibitions, Fotografiska Berlin
calls.summary: Free one-on-one online portfolio review with two senior Fotografiska curators. Apply by June 15; review day July 3, 2026.
prose: Fotografiska Emerging is the international photography platform run by Fotografiska, the museum group with locations in Stockholm, Tallinn, Berlin, New York, and Shanghai. The Portfolio Review is a recurring open call where selected photographers get direct one-on-one feedback from senior Fotografiska curators — pitched as a developmental opportunity rather than a prize competition.

Selected applicants are paired with one of two reviewers: Jessica Jarl, Global Director of Exhibitions based in Stockholm, or Thomas Schäfer, Director of Exhibitions at Fotografiska Berlin. Each session runs 20 minutes online in English. Reviews are oriented around understanding where a project is headed — exhibition, editorial, or further development — rather than generic feedback.

Submission is free. Applicants submit a visual project with clear narrative — a series that holds together and functions as a cohesive body of work rather than individual frames. Open to image-makers of all levels with no nationality restriction.
The 2026 deadline is June 15 at 10:00 AM CEST; the review day is July 3, 2026 from 10:00 AM to 3:00 PM CEST. Selected applicants must be available for the review window.

calls.title: PORTRAITS — Hellerau Photography Award 2026
calls.description: Theme: Escapism. 11th edition of the international photography award. €8,000 total prizes (1st: €5,000, 2nd: €2,000, 3rd: €1,000). Series and individual submissions. 50% student discount on fees.
jury: Angela Matyssek, Professor, Dresden University of Fine Arts
calls.summary: Theme: Escapism. 11th edition. €8,000 total prizes. Series and individual submissions. 50% student discount.
prose: PORTRAITS — Hellerau Photography Award is an annual international portrait photography prize organized in association with HELLERAU – European Center for the Arts in Dresden. The 2026 edition is the prize's 11th cycle. The theme is Escapism — portraits made under, around, or about the act of escape, in any direction the photographer reads it.

Total prize fund is €8,000: first prize €5,000, second €2,000, third €1,000. Both series and individual single-image submissions are accepted; up to 20 images per submission. AI-generated work is not accepted.

The 2026 jury is Carena Schlewitt (Artistic Director, HELLERAU), Sim Chi Yin (artist and researcher), Daniel Blochwitz (photographer and curator), Angela Matyssek (Professor, Dresden University of Fine Arts), and Sandra Buschow (photographer and curator).

Submission is through Picter. The fee is tiered €30–€50 depending on submission scale, with a 50% student discount available. Eligibility is open globally. The 2026 deadline was May 3; results announced October 29, 2026.

calls.title: PETARD Magazine Issue #2 — Authentic
calls.description: Print magazine exploring the tension between truth and performance, reality and replica. Accepting editorials, photo essays, performances, and visual projects. Priority for women-led teams and unpublished work. Pop-up exhibition and print launch June 2026.
calls.summary: Exploring tension between truth and performance, reality and replica. Priority for women-led teams. Pop-up June 2026.
prose: PETARD is an indie print magazine. Issue #2 is themed Authentic — the brief explores the tension between truth and performance, reality and replica. The framing positions authenticity as a contested concept rather than an assumed value.

The magazine accepts a wide range of submission types: editorials, photo essays, performances, and visual projects. Photography sits alongside performance documentation and conceptual work rather than as the dominant medium.
Selection priority is given to women-led teams and unpublished work — both stated as criteria, not just preferences.
Selection results in inclusion in the printed magazine plus a pop-up exhibition and print launch event in June 2026.
Submission is by email — applicants send a download link plus a PDF dossier. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was April 16; results announced April 18, 2026.

calls.title: KYOTOGRAPHIE International Portfolio Review 2026
calls.description: International portfolio review with world-class experts in Kyoto, April 17–19. Fujifilm Award and new KYOTOGRAPHIE x Dazed Award for emerging photographers. Open to all ages, nationalities, and career levels.
jury: Thiago Nogueira, Contemporary Art Director, Moreira Salles Institute
Mutsuko Ota, Editorial Director, IMA Magazine
Andrea Holzherr, Culture Director, Magnum Photos Paris
Takahiro Ito, Curator, Tokyo Photographic Art Museum
Federico Estol, Artistic Director, SAN JOSE FOTO
calls.summary: Portfolio review with world-class experts in Kyoto. Fujifilm Award and KYOTOGRAPHIE x Dazed Award for emerging work.
prose: KYOTOGRAPHIE is Japan's major international photography festival, held in Kyoto each spring. The International Portfolio Review is the festival's professional review program — three days of in-person reviews held April 17–19, 2026 alongside the festival.
Two awards run within the review: the Fujifilm Award and the new KYOTOGRAPHIE x Dazed Award for emerging photographers. Top award is ¥100,000.

The 2026 reviewer panel is built from major international institutions and publications: Thiago Nogueira (Contemporary Art Director, Moreira Salles Institute, São Paulo), Yumi Goto (independent curator), Mutsuko Ota (Editorial Director, IMA Magazine), Michael Famighetti (Editor-in-Chief, Aperture), Andrea Holzherr (Culture Director, Magnum Photos Paris), Takahiro Ito (Curator, Tokyo Photographic Art Museum), Marina Paulenka (independent curator), and Federico Estol (Artistic Director, SAN JOSE FOTO).

Eligibility is open globally to all ages, nationalities, and career levels. Reviewers see physical print portfolios — applicants bring printed work to Kyoto rather than submitting digitally for review.
Submission is through JotForm. Fee is ¥2,000. The 2026 deadline was March 31; review weekend April 17–19, 2026.

calls.title: Prix Révélation SAIF x La Kabine 2026
calls.description: Award supporting emerging contemporary photography. €2,000 prize plus exhibition during Festival OFF Arles. 30 finalists projected at La Nuit de l'Émergence with €100 each. Open to professional photographers of all nationalities, 18+.
calls.summary: Award for emerging contemporary photography. €2,000 prize plus exhibition during Festival OFF Arles.
prose: Prix Révélation SAIF x La Kabine is an emerging photography award organized jointly by SAIF (the French Society of Visual Arts Authors) and La Kabine, the Arles photography center. The 2026 cycle is one of the SAIF prizes for visual arts authorship.

The award supports emerging contemporary photography. Top prize is €2,000 plus exhibition during Festival OFF Arles — the parallel program running alongside Rencontres d'Arles, where curators, editors, and gallerists travel each summer.

Selection structure has two tiers. The winner receives the cash prize and Festival OFF exhibition. Beyond that, 30 finalists have their work projected at La Nuit de l'Émergence (the festival's emerging-photography evening event), with €100 each.

Eligibility is restricted to professional photographers, all nationalities, 18+. Submission is through JotForm with 10–15 images. Fee is €5. The 2026 deadline was March 29; results announced June 2026.

calls.title: Fotobus Library Award 2026
calls.description: Annual award recognizing the 10 best photobooks of the year. Winning books exhibited at Rencontres d'Arles and Polycopies festivals. All publishers and bookmakers worldwide eligible. Books published Mar 2025–Mar 2026 in runs of 100+ copies.
calls.summary: Recognizing the 10 best photobooks of the year. Winners exhibited at Arles and Polycopies festivals.
prose: The Fotobus Library Award is administered by Fotobus Society, a Germany-based photography network. The award is structurally distinctive in two ways: the jury is composed entirely of student members of Fotobus Society — bringing a younger curatorial perspective to photobook selection — and selected books become permanent additions to the mobile Fotobus Library, which travels to photography festivals across Europe.

The 2026 cycle recognizes the 10 best photobooks released between March 2025 and March 2026. Winning books are exhibited at two of the most important international photobook venues: Rencontres d'Arles (July 6–12, 2026) and Polycopies in Paris (November 12–15, 2026). Selected work is also featured in the Fotobus Society newsletter, Instagram, and website to a network of 1,700 members.

Eligibility requires the submitted book to be a published work with a minimum 100-copy print run, with photography as the primary medium. Self-published works are accepted alongside trade publications. AI-generated images disqualify the book. Unpublished dummies and dummy books are not eligible — this is a finished-book award.

Submission is free of charge. Submitted books are mailed to Hannover and become part of the mobile Fotobus Library — they are not returned. The 2026 deadline is May 15, with results announced June 2026.

calls.title: Deloitte Photo Grant 2026
calls.description: Theme: Proximities. Open to photographers under 35. €25,000 open call prize plus solo exhibition at Triennale Milano. €50,000 nominations category. Explores social, economic, and relational dimensions of proximity.
jury: Guido Borsani, Chairman, Italian Deloitte Foundation
Bernardino Castro, Director, Portuguese Photography Center
Suzanne Cotter, Director, Museum of Contemporary Art Australia
Sunyoung Kim, Senior Curator, Hanmi Museum
calls.summary: Theme: Proximities. For photographers under 35. €25,000 prize plus solo exhibition at Triennale Milano.
prose: The Deloitte Photo Grant was established in 2023 by Deloitte Italy under the patronage of Fondazione Deloitte ETS, in association with Still Love srl. The grant runs in two parallel tracks: an Open Call for emerging photographers and a Nominations category that brings in invited photographers separately.

The 2026 theme is "Proximities" — investigating new forms of distance in contemporary life (physical, economic, technological, social) and how communities endure despite contemporary pressures. The Open Call is restricted to photographers under 35 years of age.

The Open Call winner receives €25,000 in project funding plus a solo exhibition at Triennale Milano, the major Milan design and contemporary art museum. The parallel Nominations category carries a €50,000 prize. Submission to the Open Call is free.

The 2026 jury, chaired by artistic director Denis Curti, includes Magnum photographers Alec Soth and Bruce Gilden, Suzanne Cotter (Director, Museum of Contemporary Art Australia), Sunyoung Kim (Senior Curator, Hanmi Museum), Bernardino Castro (Director, Portuguese Photography Center), Barbara Ceferin (Owner, Galerija Fotografija), Katarzyna Sagatowska (Curator, Jednostka Gallery), Guido Borsani (Chairman, Italian Deloitte Foundation), and Carlos Idun-Tawiah (the 2025 winner).
Submissions require 10 images. AI-generated work is accepted with mandatory disclosure. Submissions are open March 10 through June 14, 2026; jury voting closes September 6, with results in September.

calls.title: Denis Roussel Award 2026
calls.description: For photographers working with historical and alternative photographic processes including silver gelatin. Submit 7 images and statement. $2,000 main award plus merit awards. Portfolio review prize included.
jury: Christopher James, Professor, Lesley University College of Art and Design
calls.summary: For historical and alternative photographic processes including silver gelatin. $2,000 main award.
prose: The Denis Roussel Award is administered by Rfotofolio, an organization dedicated to showcasing photographers and supporting work in historical photographic processes. The award honors photographer and educator Denis Roussel, who died of cancer in 2017 — Roussel worked across landscapes, portraits, and still life, and the award reflects his belief that "there is beauty everywhere." The prize was established in 2018.

The focus is exclusively historical and alternative photographic processes — silver gelatin, platinum, palladium, gum bichromate, cyanotype, anthotype, salt prints, wet plate collodion, and similar. Inkjet prints are not eligible, and AI-generated work is excluded.

The prize structure is layered: a $2,000 main award; two $500 Merit Awards; a $500 Rfotofolio Merit Award; the Christopher James Award (a one-on-one portfolio review with the longtime juror); and additional sponsor awards from Bostick & Sullivan and Mark Nelson covering chemistry and equipment.

Past winners include Luther Gerlach (2018), Tina Rowe (2019), Lesha Rodriguez (2020), Diana Bloomfield (2021), Henri Blommers (2022), and Lisa Nebenzahl (2023). Christopher James (Lesley University College of Art and Design) has served as juror from 2020–2024.

There is no entry fee (donations optional). Applications require seven edited images and a written statement of up to two paragraphs. The 2026 cycle runs March 5 through June 27; results announced July 19.

calls.title: Lucie Foundation Photo Book Prize 2026
calls.description: Celebrating the most innovative photographic books. Three categories: Book of the Year ($3,000), First Book ($2,000), and Self-Published ($2,000). Open to photographers and publishers worldwide.
jury: Monica Aguilar Villamarin, Visual Artist & Photo Educator
calls.summary: Celebrating innovative photographic books. Three categories. $3,000 Book of the Year. Open worldwide.
prose: The Lucie Foundation Photo Book Prize is the foundation's annual award for photography in book form. Three categories carry cash prizes: Book of the Year ($3,000, awarded to the publisher), First Book ($2,000, awarded to the photographer), and Self-Published ($2,000, awarded to the photographer). The prize structure reflects how photo books actually get made — recognizing publishers for their craft, debut authors for theirs, and independents for going it alone.

Eligible work spans the full range of contemporary photo publishing: traditionally published books and zines, hand-made and limited editions, exhibition catalogues, photography combined with other media, multi-artist anthologies, and single-artist publications. Books must be published between September 2024 and September 2026 to qualify for the 2026 cycle. There is no submission limit per applicant.

Entry fees are $75 for publishers and $50 for photographers on the first submission, with 20% off subsequent category entries of the same book. Submissions require a completed form and a PDF of the book up to 60MB; individual JPG files used for evaluation must be 72 DPI and under 4MB each. Final deadline is September 15, 2026 (midnight ET); winners are announced in fall 2026.

The eleven-juror panel for 2026 includes photographers Martin Schoeller, Jamel Shabazz, Lele Saveri, and Paul Baldonado; editors Merve Arkunlar (212 Magazine) and Elizabeth Krist; and curators Eleni Mouzakiti, Yumi Goto, Emmanuel Iduma (Tender Photos), and Monica Aguilar Villamarin.

calls.title: Insight Foto Festival — Insight Out 2026
calls.description: Open circuit for independent photography exhibitions and projects inspired by the theme ABITO. Open to artists, collectives, and local organizations. Sixth edition of the festival in Varese, Italy.
calls.summary: Independent photography exhibitions and projects exploring the theme ABITO. Sixth edition in Varese, Italy.
prose: Insight Foto Festival is held annually in Varese, in the Lombardy region of northern Italy. The 2026 edition is the festival's sixth cycle. Insight Out is the festival's open circuit for independent photography exhibitions and projects.
The 2026 theme is ABITO — Italian for 'dwelling' or 'habit,' a word that holds both senses. The brief invites projects engaging with how people inhabit places and how habits inhabit people.
The call is structurally inclusive: open not only to individual artists but also to collectives and local organizations. Selected projects exhibit during the festival.
Submission is by Google Form. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was January 25.

calls.title: Bibin Photography Magazine #5 — Body, Form & Condition
calls.description: Quarterly contemporary photography magazine from Afghanistan. Issue #5 explores the body through formalist reading — volume, surface, and condition. 20 photographs selected per edition. Multiple submissions welcome.
calls.summary: Quarterly magazine from Afghanistan. Issue #5 explores the body through formalist reading — volume, surface, condition.
prose: Bibin Photography Magazine is a quarterly contemporary photography magazine from Afghanistan. Issue #5 — Body, Form & Condition takes the body as subject through a formalist lens: volume, surface, and condition rather than identity or narrative.
Twenty photographs are selected per edition. Multiple submissions per applicant are welcome — the magazine doesn't restrict to one image per photographer.
Selection is by Shadi Mousavi, art critic and researcher.
Submission is single-image, made through Fillout. Application is free. Eligibility is open globally. The Issue #5 deadline was March 31, 2026.

calls.title: Penumbra Foundation Workspace Residency 2026
calls.description: 6–8 week residency in New York City with $7,000 honorarium. Access to comprehensive photographic facilities including darkrooms, digital labs, and studio space. Juried by Makeda Best, Natasha Chuk, and Walead Beshty.
jury: Makeda Best, Deputy Director of Curatorial Affairs, Oakland Museum of California
calls.summary: 6–8 week NYC residency with $7,000 honorarium. Darkrooms, digital labs, and studio space at Penumbra Foundation.
prose: Penumbra Foundation is a New York City photography nonprofit with comprehensive photographic facilities — darkrooms, digital labs, and studio space all available to residents. The Workspace Residency is the foundation's main residency program.
The residency runs 6–8 weeks in New York City. Each resident receives a $7,000 honorarium plus full access to the foundation's facilities — production support is the core of what's offered.
Selection is by Makeda Best (Deputy Director of Curatorial Affairs, Oakland Museum of California), Natasha Chuk (media theorist and researcher), and Walead Beshty (artist and educator).
Eligibility is restricted to US-based artists. Submission is through Picter with 10–20 images. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was March 31; results announced May 15, 2026.

calls.title: Penumbra Foundation Risograph Publication Residency
calls.description: Residency to produce a small edition risograph photobook at Penumbra's facilities in NYC. No prior risograph experience required. Juried by Catherine McKinley, Joshua Chuang, and Travis Shaffer.
jury: Joshua Chuang, Director of Photography, Gagosian
calls.summary: Residency to produce a small edition risograph photobook at Penumbra's NYC facilities. No prior experience required.
prose: Penumbra Foundation's Risograph Publication Residency is a separate program from its main Workspace Residency. The premise is specific: produce a small edition risograph photobook at Penumbra's NYC facilities. The residency provides equipment access, technical support, and production guidance.
Notable accessibility: no prior risograph experience is required. The residency is structured to teach the process during production.
Selection is by Catherine E. McKinley (curator and writer), Joshua Chuang (Director of Photography, Gagosian), and Travis Shaffer (artist and educator).
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through Picter with 15–30 images representing the project to be made. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was March 31; results announced May 15, 2026.

calls.title: Generator Cooperative Art Production Fund — Round 10
calls.description: Production bursaries for artists with no restrictions on age, medium, geography, or language. Supports project completion, seed funding, or continuing practice. Evaluated by rotating jury of artists and curators.
calls.summary: Production bursaries for artists. No restrictions on age, medium, geography, or language.
prose: Generator is the cooperative art production fund run by Experimenter — the Kolkata- and Mumbai-based contemporary art gallery and platform. The fund offers production bursaries for artists, structured around project completion, seed funding for new work, or general support for continuing practice.

The structural premise distinguishes Generator from most grants: no restrictions on age, medium, geography, or language. The fund is open across all parameters that other grants typically use to narrow eligibility.
