Selected work is shown in an ephemeral online exhibition on Der Greif's platform — displayed for one month before being archived rather than featured permanently.
Eligibility is restricted to emerging artists. The fee is voluntary — €10 suggested but not required.

Selection is by Der Greif's editorial team: Caroline von Courten (Artistic Director), Francesca Hummler (Community Manager and Program Curator), Ilaria Sponda (Managing Editor and Project Manager), and Carolina Semprucci (Graphic Designer and Assistant Editor).
Submission is through Picter with 1–10 images. The 2026 deadline was April 8; selection announced April 22, 2026.

calls.title: Golden Turtle International Wildlife Festival 2026
calls.description: International wildlife photography competition in 12 categories: Animals in the Environment, Portrait of the Animal, Animal Behaviour, Microcosm, Underwater World, Art and Nature's Image, Landscape, Magic of Plants, Humans and Nature, Reserved Russia, Mobile Photography, and Youth (two age groups). Up to 20 photos per author. Professional jury of international wildlife photographers. Finalists exhibited in Moscow autumn 2026, published in festival album. No zoo photography except Humans and Nature category. No composites or montage. RAW files required from semifinalists.
jury: Andrey Kamenev, National Geographic Russia Photographer
Mario Suárez Porras, Canon Pro Master, Bird Photographer (Spain)
Fernando Faciole, National Geographic Explorer, Conservation Photographer (Brazil)
Anthony Ochieng, National Geographic Explorer, Wildlife Photographer (Kenya)
calls.summary: International wildlife competition in 12 categories. Finalists exhibited in Moscow, published in festival album.
prose: Golden Turtle International Wildlife Festival is an annual international wildlife photography competition based in Russia. The 2026 edition runs across 12 categories: Animals in the Environment, Portrait of the Animal, Animal Behaviour, Microcosm, Underwater World, Art and Nature's Image, Landscape, Magic of Plants, Humans and Nature, Reserved Russia, Mobile Photography, and Youth (with two age groups).

Technical and ethical rules are strict: no zoo photography (except in the Humans and Nature category), no composites or montage, no AI-generated work. RAW files are required from semifinalists for verification.
Top prize is $2,000. Finalists are exhibited in Moscow in autumn 2026 and published in the festival album.

The 2026 jury is built from international wildlife photographers: Andrey Kamenev (National Geographic Russia), Gheorghe Popa (Romania), Mario Suárez Porras (Canon Pro Master, Spain), Cynthia Bandurek (Argentina/Costa Rica), Fernando Faciole (National Geographic Explorer, Brazil), Francesco Pacienza (Italy), and Anthony Ochieng (National Geographic Explorer, Kenya).
Eligibility is open globally. Each photographer may submit up to 20 photos. Application is free, made through the Golden Turtle website. The 2026 deadline was April 7.

calls.title: Sarajevo Photography Festival 2026
calls.description: Opening week June 1-7, 2026. Grand Prix: €2,000 cash. Canon-sponsored professional awards. Eight competition categories. Total prizes ~€7,000.
jury: Simone Azzoni, Professor, Contemporary Art History
Teresa Freitas, Director, Lisbon Street Photo Fest
Timotej Letonja, Founder & Editor-in-Chief, Numéro Netherlands
Fernanda Prado Verčič, Director, Kranj Foto Fest
calls.summary: Opening week June 1-7. Grand Prix: €2,000. Canon-sponsored professional awards. Eight competition categories.
prose: Sarajevo Photography Festival is the international photography festival held annually in Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina. The 2026 opening week runs June 1–7.

The festival's competition runs across eight categories. Total prize fund is approximately €7,000, with the Grand Prix awarding €2,000 cash. Canon sponsors a set of professional-tier awards within the program. AI-generated work is not accepted.

The 2026 jury draws from European photography festival directors and contemporary art figures: Simone Azzoni (Professor of Contemporary Art History, also Co-Founder of Grenze Festival), Marko Drobnjaković (documentary photographer), Teresa Freitas (Director, Lisbon Street Photo Fest), Šejla Kamerić (visual artist), Timotej Letonja (Founder & Editor-in-Chief, Numéro Netherlands), Coline Plançon (curator and coordinator, PhotoSaintGermain), Fernanda Prado Verčič (Director, Kranj Foto Fest), and Ionuț Trandafirescu (Director, Bucharest Photofest).
Eligibility is open to photographers 16+ globally. Submission is through the festival's website with 1–6 images. Fee is tiered €15–€30. The 2026 deadline was April 10.

calls.title: Framed: Black and White
calls.description: Juried black and white group show exploring classic, nostalgic and dynamic translation with diversity of contemporary voices. Portland, OR.
jury: Todd Johnson, Founder & Director, Black Box Gallery
calls.summary: Juried black and white group show. Classic, nostalgic, and dynamic monochrome with diverse contemporary voices. Portland, OR.
prose: Framed: Black and White is the black-and-white-themed cycle of Black Box Gallery's recurring juried exhibition program. Black Box Gallery is a Portland, Oregon photography gallery directed by Todd Johnson, who holds an MFA in Photography from the San Francisco Art Institute and acts as juror for the gallery's calls. The brief seeks classic, nostalgic, and dynamic monochrome work spanning the diversity of contemporary voices working in B&W today.

The selection structure follows the gallery's standard format: 26 photographs are chosen for the physical gallery exhibition, 50 additional for the online gallery annex, and all 76 selected works appear in a printed Blurb catalog.

The gallery covers all printing, matting, and framing for selected work — archival printing on Epson Premium Luster Photo paper. After the exhibition closes, prints stay in the gallery's flat files for two years of ongoing promotion.

Entry fee is $40 per submission of up to 5 photos. Submissions are by email — JPEG, max 1200 pixels longest side, 72 PPI, under 5MB. Eligibility is open worldwide. Sales terms: 50% gallery commission, photographer retains rights and may opt out of sale.
The 2026 deadline was April 10; juror decisions communicated approximately April 17–20, 2026.

calls.title: Hiding in Plain Sight
calls.org: Rhode Island Center for Photographic Arts
calls.description: Exploring the unseen and forgotten. Challenges myths and revalues overlooked subjects. Providence, RI.
calls.summary: Exploring the unseen and forgotten. Challenging myths and revaluing overlooked subjects. Providence, RI.
prose: Hiding in Plain Sight is one of the Rhode Island Center for Photographic Arts (RICPA)'s themed juried calls. RICPA is a Providence-based nonprofit photography gallery and educational center.

The brief is interpretive: photographers are asked to explore the unseen and forgotten — work that challenges myths and revalues overlooked subjects. The framing invites attention to what photography typically misses or treats as background.
Selection is by Lou Jones, photographer. Single-juror selection.
Cash prizes are $250 (first), $150 (second), $75 (third). Selected work is shown in a physical exhibition at RICPA.
Eligibility is open globally to photographers 18+. Submission is through CaFÉ with 3–15 images. Fee is $35. The 2026 deadline was April 10.

calls.title: Queer Conscience 2026 Photography Exhibition
calls.description: 4th annual for LGBTQIA2+ community. Seeking work affirming our own truths and expressing resistance during Pride month. Mill Valley, CA.
jury: Conor Moynihan, Associate Curator, RISD Museum
Nathan Lomas, Gallery Manager, The Image Flow
calls.summary: 4th annual for LGBTQIA2+ community. Affirming truths and expressing resistance during Pride month. Mill Valley, CA.
prose: The Image Flow is a Marin County, California photography center based in San Anselmo. The Queer Conscience exhibition is its annual juried show timed to Pride month. The 2026 edition is the fourth cycle.

Eligibility is restricted to LGBTQIA2+ photographers based in the United States. The brief asks for work affirming our own truths and expressing resistance — the editorial register foregrounds political and personal assertion rather than simply visibility.
Selection is by Conor Moynihan (Associate Curator, RISD Museum) and Nathan Lomas (Gallery Manager, The Image Flow). The 2026 exhibition is timed to coincide with Pride month.
Submission is through ArtCall with up to 5 images. Fee is $40. The 2026 deadline was April 11; results announced April 17, 2026.

calls.title: PPA Photo Award 2026
calls.description: For emerging US photographers. Prize: $2,000 cash, interview, Lenscratch feature, virtual artist talk. Juror: Craig Krull, art dealer.
jury: Craig Krull, Founder, Craig Krull Gallery
calls.ai: AI editing OK, fully generated not accepted
calls.summary: For emerging US photographers. $2,000 prize, Lenscratch feature, virtual artist talk. Juror: Craig Krull.
prose: Pasadena Photography Arts (PPA) is a nonprofit photography organization based in Pasadena, California. The PPA Photo Award is its annual prize for emerging US photographers — career-stage rather than location restricted to Pasadena.
The 2026 juror is Craig Krull, founder of the Craig Krull Gallery in Santa Monica — an established LA-area gallery with a long photography program. Single-juror selection rather than panel.

The winner receives $2,000 cash plus an interview, a Lenscratch feature (Lenscratch is the long-running US fine-art photography platform), and a virtual artist talk with PPA. AI editing is acceptable; fully AI-generated work is not.
Eligibility is restricted to emerging US-based photographers 18+. Submission is through CaFÉ with 10–20 images. Fee is $42. The 2026 deadline was April 26; results announced August 21, 2026.

calls.title: XVI Concurso Internacional de Fotografía sobre Humanización Asistencial
calls.org: Hospital San Juan de Dios de León
calls.description: 16th edition of this international photography competition seeking images that reflect humanization, solidarity, and care in healthcare and everyday life. Photos can depict professional healthcare settings, family, personal, sports, or cultural environments where someone helps a person in need. Open to all adults. Up to 3 photographs per participant. Prizes: €600, €400, €200 plus a weekend stay.
calls.summary: Photography reflecting humanization, solidarity, and care in healthcare and everyday life. Prizes: €600/€400/€200.
prose: The Concurso Internacional de Fotografía sobre Humanización Asistencial is an international photography competition organized by Hospital San Juan de Dios de León, in Spain. The 2026 edition is the 16th cycle.

The brief is thematically narrow: photography reflecting humanization, solidarity, and care — in healthcare settings or in everyday life. Subjects can depict professional healthcare environments, family, personal, sports, or cultural settings where someone helps a person in need. The unifying thread is the act of care.
Cash prizes are €600, €400, and €200, plus a weekend hotel stay for the top winner. AI-generated work is not accepted.
Selection is by Secundino Pérez, Mauricio Peña, and Javier Casares — all photographers.
Eligibility is open globally to adults 18+. Submission is by email with up to 3 photographs per participant. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was April 13; results announced April 24, 2026.

calls.title: light
calls.description: Exploring light as key element. 47 images selected. Exhibition May 8 - June 18, 2026. Juror: Elizabeth Avedon. Johnson City, TX.
jury: Elizabeth Avedon, Curator & Photography Book Designer
calls.summary: Exploring light as key element. 47 images selected. Juror: Elizabeth Avedon. Exhibition in Johnson City, TX.
prose: A Smith Gallery is a photography gallery in Johnson City, Texas, that runs themed juried exhibitions on a recurring schedule. The 'light' call is the gallery's exhibition for work where light functions as the key element of the photograph — its presence, behavior, and quality as subject rather than as a technical condition.
Forty-seven images are selected for the physical exhibition at the gallery, running May 8 – June 18, 2026.
Selection is by Elizabeth Avedon, curator and photography book designer.

AI-generated work is not accepted. Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through the gallery's website with unlimited images per applicant. Fee is $40. The 2026 deadline was April 13; results announced April 24, 2026.

calls.title: Sharing and Caring Cities: Portraits of Collective Urban Life
calls.description: 10th annual photography contest exploring shared urban spaces addressing inequality and climate change. Open to all photographers.
jury: Nikhil Anand, Professor of Anthropology, Penn
Matthew Neff, Director, Undergraduate Fine Arts, Weitzman School
Jennifer Whittaker, Research Scientist, CHOP Policy Lab
calls.summary: 10th annual contest exploring shared urban spaces addressing inequality and climate change.
prose: The Penn Institute for Urban Research (Penn IUR) runs an annual photography contest as part of its public program. The 2026 edition is the 10th cycle, themed Sharing and Caring Cities: Portraits of Collective Urban Life — work engaging with shared urban spaces and how cities address inequality and climate change.
The contest is academic-affiliated rather than a fine-art competition. The brief favors documentary observation of shared infrastructure, public space, and collective practices.
AI-generated work is not accepted.

Selection is by Penn faculty and researchers: Nikhil Anand (Professor of Anthropology), Amy Hillier (Associate Professor), Matthew Neff (Director, Undergraduate Fine Arts, Weitzman School), and Jennifer Whittaker (Research Scientist, CHOP Policy Lab). Top prize is $500.
Eligibility is open to all photographers globally. Submission is through Penn's Qualtrics form with 3 images. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was April 15.

calls.title: Portrait Awards 2026
calls.description: Fourth edition celebrating portrait as a space of presence, responsibility, and authorship amidst visual saturation. Barcelona.
jury: Burkhard Arnold, Gallery Director, in focus Galerie
Erin Hoyt, Executive Director, Filter Photo Festival
calls.summary: Fourth edition celebrating portrait as a space of presence and authorship amidst visual saturation. Barcelona.
prose: Dodho Magazine is a Barcelona-based contemporary photography magazine. The Portrait Awards is one of its themed annual competitions. The 2026 edition is the fourth cycle. The brief celebrates portrait as a space of presence, responsibility, and authorship amidst visual saturation — framing portraiture as a counter-practice to image overproduction.

The 2026 jury draws from the international photography ecosystem: Aline Smithson (Founder & Editor, Lenscratch), Burkhard Arnold (Gallery Director, in focus Galerie), Erin Hoyt (Executive Director, Filter Photo Festival), and Roger Ballen (photographer).
Selected work is published by Dodho Magazine.

Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through Dodho's website with 3, 6, or 12 images. Fee is tiered €30–€60 based on submission scale. The 2026 deadline was April 15; results announced May 1–3, 2026.

calls.title: ViewPoint Gallery International Photography Competition
calls.description: Twelve winners display professionally printed, matted, framed work for one month each from June 2026 to May 2027. Eastern Canada.
calls.summary: Twelve winners displayed professionally printed and framed for one month each, June 2026 to May 2027. Eastern Canada.
prose: ViewPoint Gallery is a photographer-run cooperative gallery in Halifax, Nova Scotia — Eastern Canada. The annual International Photography Competition selects work for the gallery's monthly featured wall.

The structure is unusual: twelve winners are selected, and each receives a one-month featured display from June 2026 through May 2027. Each winner gets the wall for the full month rather than a single group exhibition. Production is gallery-supplied: work is professionally printed, matted, and framed.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is by Google Form with 3 images. Fee is $25. The 2026 deadline was April 15; results announced May 8, 2026.

calls.title: The Cortona on The Move / BarTur Grant
calls.org: BarTur Photo Award / Cortona On The Move
calls.description: Supports photographers with ongoing projects. Honors visual storytellers who push the medium forward with clear authorship. Winners exhibited at Cortona On The Move festival. Note: Cortona On The Move and BarTur Photo Award have announced the conclusion of their collaboration after the first edition.
calls.summary: Supporting photographers with ongoing projects and clear authorship. Winners exhibited at Cortona On The Move festival.
prose: The Cortona on The Move / BarTur Grant was a $30,000 grant supporting professional photographers with ongoing projects, organized as a collaboration between Cortona On The Move (the Italian photography festival held annually in Cortona) and BarTur Photo Award.
The brief honored visual storytellers who push the medium forward with clear authorship. Winners were exhibited at Cortona On The Move festival.
Note: Cortona On The Move and BarTur Photo Award announced the conclusion of their collaboration after this first edition. The 2026 cycle was a one-time joint program.

Eligibility was restricted to professional photographers. Submission was through Picter. Fee was $25. AI-generated work was not accepted. The 2026 deadline was February 13; results announced July 2026.

calls.title: Montgomery Photo Festival 2026
calls.description: Eighth annual festival. Four categories: Color, Monochromatic, Alternative process, Manipulation. No theme; all work acceptable.
calls.summary: Eighth annual festival. Four categories: Color, Monochromatic, Alternative process, Manipulation. No theme.
prose: Montgomery Photo Festival is an annual photography festival held in Montgomery, Alabama. The 2026 edition is the festival's eighth cycle.

The structure runs across four process and approach categories: Color, Monochromatic, Alternative Process, and Manipulation. There is no thematic restriction — subject matter is open. Selection is by category type rather than by topic.
Selection is by Carol McCusker. Total prize pool is $3,500. Selected work is shown in the festival's exhibition program in Montgomery.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through ArtCall with up to 3 images. Fee is $35. The 2026 deadline was April 17; results announced May 22, 2026.

calls.title: LUMINOSITY - The Impact of Light
calls.org: New York Center for Photographic Arts
calls.description: Exploring light's presence, absence, and location. Winners receive $4,000 cash, online gallery feature, catalog publication. New York, NY.
jury: Crista Dix, Executive Director, Griffin Museum of Photography
calls.summary: Exploring light's presence, absence, and location. $4,000 cash prize, online gallery, catalogue. New York.
prose: The New York Center for Photographic Arts (NYC4PA) runs themed juried exhibitions on a recurring schedule. LUMINOSITY — The Impact of Light is the call for work engaging with light as primary subject — its presence, absence, and location.
Selection is by Crista Dix, Executive Director of the Griffin Museum of Photography in Winchester, Massachusetts. Single-juror selection.
Total prize pool is $4,000 cash. Selected work is featured in an online gallery and a published catalog.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through Smarter Entry with unlimited images per entrant. Fee is $40. The 2026 deadline was April 19; results announced approximately May 3–10, 2026.

calls.title: FMoPA International Photography Competition 2026
calls.description: International jury selection. Winning entries printed and exhibited June 16 - August 2, 2026 at Ybor City, Tampa.
jury: Jessica Jarl, Global Director of Exhibitions, Fotografiska
calls.summary: International jury selection. Winning entries printed and exhibited at Ybor City, Tampa, June-August 2026.
prose: The Florida Museum of Photographic Arts (FMoPA) is a Tampa-based museum dedicated to photography, located in Tampa's Ybor City Historic District. The annual International Photography Competition is the museum's flagship juried open call.

The 2026 edition runs across seven categories: People/Portraits, Places/Landscape, Nature/Science/Animals, Documentation/Photojournalism, Still Life, Abstract, and Conceptual. Eligibility is open globally to photographers 18+.
Best in Competition receives $1,000 cash. Category winners receive goods and services rather than additional cash. Winning works are exhibited at FMoPA from June 16 to August 2, 2026.

The 2026 jury is built from international institutions: Jessica Jarl (Global Director of Exhibitions, Fotografiska), Hiromi Nakamura (Curator, Tokyo Metropolitan Museum of Photography), Elena Paraskeva (photographer and art director), Bärbel Reinhard (photographer, curator and educator), and Kristen Roles (photographic artist and educator).
Submission is through Picter with up to 15 images. Fee is $10. The 2026 deadline was April 22; results announced May 13, 2026.

calls.title: CITY Photography Exhibit
calls.description: Capturing personal urban experience from quiet, unnoticed moments to the bustling energy of a metropolis. Santa Fe, NM.
jury: Holly Hart, Fine Art Photographer & Founder, Dusk Gallery
calls.summary: Capturing personal urban experience from quiet moments to bustling energy. Santa Fe, NM.
prose: Dusk Gallery is a Santa Fe, New Mexico photography gallery — a sister gallery to Decode Gallery in Tucson, both founded by fine art photographer Holly Hart. CITY is the gallery's call for work engaging with personal urban experience: quiet, unnoticed moments through the bustling energy of metropolitan life.
The brief is open in approach. Selection is by Holly Hart.

Selected work is shown in a physical exhibition at Dusk Gallery in Santa Fe. The gallery's production model mirrors Decode's — the gallery typically covers professional printing and framing for selected work.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through the gallery's website with 5 or 10 images. Fee is $40–$45. The 2026 deadline was April 16; results announced approximately April 30, 2026.

calls.title: Film Photo Award 2026
calls.description: Three grants of professional film and complimentary processing by Praus Productions. Open to emerging, established, and student photographers worldwide.
calls.summary: Three grants of professional film and processing by Praus Productions. US-based photographers only.
prose: The Film Photo Award is unusual in its prize structure: rather than cash, the award provides three grants of professional film stock and complimentary processing by Praus Productions, the Rochester-based film processing lab.

The grant supports photographers committing to extended film-based projects — the photographer brings the project, the award brings the materials. Selected work is also published on the Film Photo Award platform.
Eligibility is restricted to US-based photographers 18+. Open across career stages: emerging, established, and student photographers all eligible.
Submission is through CaFÉ with 1–15 images. Fee is tiered $25–$35. The 2026 deadline was April 26; results announced late May 2026.

calls.title: HOME Photography Exhibit
calls.description: Home as feeling, memory, sanctuary. Exploring domesticity, heritage, shelter, identity through diverse styles. Tucson, AZ.
calls.summary: Home as feeling, memory, sanctuary. Exploring domesticity, heritage, shelter, and identity. Tucson, AZ.
prose: Decode Gallery is a Tucson, Arizona photography gallery founded by conceptual fine art photographer Holly Hart, who also juries the gallery's open calls. HOME is the gallery's call for work engaging with the multifaceted nature of home — as feeling, memory, sanctuary, physical space, heritage, or identity.
The brief invites domestic spaces, loved ones, landscapes, or personal belonging. The thematic framing is broader than literal residence — what counts as home is left to the photographer.

Selection structure: at least 26 images selected for exhibition at Decode Gallery in Tucson, June 6–27, 2026. The gallery covers production: complimentary professional printing on Epson printers with Ilford Pearl paper, museum-quality 22×22 white framing, and custom matting.

Eligibility is open worldwide to all skill levels. Submission is through the gallery's website with 5 or 10 images. Fee is $40–$45. The 2026 deadline was April 18; results announced approximately May 2, 2026.

calls.title: Masterclasses Program 2026/2027
calls.description: Online masterclasses led by Aaron Schuman, Charlie Engman, Erik Kessels, Salvatore Vitale, and Vasantha Yoganathan.
calls.summary: Online masterclasses by Aaron Schuman, Charlie Engman, Erik Kessels, Salvatore Vitale, and Vasantha Yoganathan.
prose: PhMuseum is a photography-focused educational platform offering online masterclasses, mentorship programs, and competitions. The 2026/2027 Masterclasses Program runs five distinct online masterclasses from October 2026 through May 2027 — an eight-month structured cohort program with a different focus and instructor for each track.

The five masterclasses for 2026/2027: CRITICAE — Documentary Photography, led by Aaron Schuman (photographer and writer). IDEA — Conceptual Thinking, led by Charlie Engman (photographer). CURAE — Artistic Development, led by Erik Kessels (curator and publisher, who has worked across major photobook projects). MEDIAE — Transmedia Storytelling, led by Salvatore Vitale (photographer and editor). FOLIO — Photobook Making, led jointly by Vasantha Yogananthan (photographer) and Cécile Poimbœuf-Koizumi (publisher).

Each masterclass operates as a separate cohort with its own application — applicants choose one track. The format is online and structured around cohort-based learning with selected practitioners working alongside the lead instructor across the program duration.

Specific fees and participant numbers are not published on the program landing page; applicants need to consult the linked masterclass pages for current details. Early-bird and scholarship applications close April 30, 2026; regular applications close May 28, 2026.

calls.title: FOTOFILMIC OPEN 2026
calls.description: Open exhibition featuring contemporary film-based photography. Honourable mentions: Mauro Curti, Melissa Renwick, Sasha Arutyunova, Will Warasila, Scott Offen, Jonah Reenders. Exhibition May 2–31, 2026 at FOTOFILMIC, Bowen Island, BC.
jury: Christopher McCall, Curator, former Director of Pier 24 Photography
Amanda Webster, Photo Editor, The New York Times
calls.summary: Exhibition featuring contemporary film-based photography. Exhibition May 2–31, 2026 at FOTOFILMIC, Bowen Island, BC.
prose: FotoFilmic is a Vancouver-based platform dedicated to contemporary film photography. The annual FOTOFILMIC OPEN is the platform's juried exhibition. The 2026 edition runs May 2–31 at FOTOFILMIC's space on Bowen Island, BC.
The brief is process-restricted: contemporary film-based photography only. AI-generated work is not accepted.
Selection is by Christopher McCall (curator, former Director of Pier 24 Photography), Amanda Webster (Photo Editor, The New York Times), and Clint & Alex Woodside (Deadbeat Club, the publishers).
Eligibility is restricted to analog/film photography. Submission is through FotoFilmic with up to 20 images. Fee is $50. The 2026 deadline was February 28; results announced March 17, 2026.

calls.title: Exposure One Awards - One Shot Photo Contest
calls.description: Black and white photography celebration. Winners receive career-enhancing cash prizes, dedicated digital gallery, artist directory placement.
jury: Lindsey Sharman, Art Gallery of Alberta
calls.summary: Black and white photography celebration. Cash prizes, digital gallery, and artist directory placement.
prose: Exposure One Awards is a contest platform with a recurring schedule of single-image photography contests. The One Shot Photo Contest is its black-and-white-focused single-image cycle.

The 2026 jury is built primarily from established institutions and publications: Beatrice Tamagnini (Vogue), Lindsey Sharman (Art Gallery of Alberta), Shana Lopes (SFMOMA), Susan Ciccotti (Aperture), and Paris Chong (Leica Gallery LA).

Selected work is shown in a dedicated digital gallery on the Exposure One platform, with placement in the platform's artist directory. Total cash prizing exceeds $4,000. AI-generated work is not accepted.
Eligibility is open to photographers 18+ globally. Submission is single-image (1–5 images per entrant), with a tiered fee of $25–$50. The 2026 deadline was May 4; results announced May 27, 2026.

calls.title: The Hopper Prize Grants
calls.description: $13,000 total: 2 artists x $4,500 and 4 artists x $1,000. All visual art media eligible. 30-artist shortlist and online journal.
jury: Misa Jeffereis, Assistant Curator, Contemporary Art Museum St. Louis
calls.summary: $13,000 total: 2 artists x $4,500 and 4 artists x $1,000. All visual art media eligible.
prose: The Hopper Prize runs twice a year, awarding six grants per cycle: two at $4,500 and four at $1,000. Founded in 2018, it awards $26,000 annually across both cycles. There's no medium restriction — recent recipients have worked in photography, painting, sculpture, video, performance, and installation. The prize is open to all career stages and accepts direct applications only; nominations aren't part of the process.

Beyond the cash awards, 30 artists per cycle are archived at hopperprize.org with biographies and links to their websites. That's 60 artists per year placed on the prize's site alongside winners — being shortlisted is roughly five times more likely than winning, and the archive itself functions as a form of recognition.

The current juror is Misa Jeffereis, an assistant curator at the Contemporary Art Museum St. Louis, a non-collecting institution with a contemporary program. The juror rotates each cycle. Application fee is $40. Deadline May 12, 2026; results announced August 28, 2026.

calls.title: 7th Annual Alternative Process Photography Exhibition
calls.description: Seeking work in cyanotype, wet plate collodion, salt printing, anthotype, gum bichromate, lumen printing, platinum/palladium, and other alternative processes.
jury: Brenton Hamilton, Photography Program Leader, UT Rio Grande Valley
Zack Sumner Schomp, Lecturer, CSU East Bay
calls.summary: Cyanotype, wet plate collodion, salt printing, platinum/palladium, and other alternative photographic processes.
prose: The Annual Alternative Process Photography Exhibition is a recurring juried call from The Image Flow (the Marin County, California photography center) in collaboration with Praxis Gallery. The 7th edition was held in 2023.
The brief is process-restricted: cyanotype, wet plate collodion, salt printing, anthotype, gum bichromate, lumen printing, platinum/palladium, and other alternative photographic processes.
Selection was by Diane Chung (Founder, CHUNG 24 GALLERY), Brenton Hamilton (Photography Program Leader, UT Rio Grande Valley), and Zack Sumner Schomp (Lecturer, CSU East Bay).
Eligibility was restricted to US-based photographers. Submission was through ArtCall with up to 3 images. Fee was $35. The 7th-edition deadline was July 24, 2023.

calls.title: SHADOW PLAY 2026
calls.description: Open juried online photography exhibit exploring shadow and light. Any interpretation of the theme welcome. Cash prizes for first, second, and honorable mention.
calls.ai: AI editing OK, fully generated not accepted
calls.summary: Online photography exhibit exploring shadow and light. Any interpretation. Cash prizes.
prose: Cape Cod Art Center is a community arts organization on Cape Cod, Massachusetts, with a regular schedule of themed online juried exhibitions throughout the year. "SHADOW PLAY 2026" is the gallery's themed call exploring shadow and light — work that engages with the interplay between presence and absence, illumination and obscurity. Any interpretation of the theme is welcome.
Cash prizes are awarded for first place, second place, and honorable mentions. Selected work appears in the online juried exhibition with promotion through the gallery's communications channels.

Entry fee is $15 per submission of up to 2 images. Submissions go through Smarter Entry. AI-edited work is permitted; fully AI-generated images are not accepted. The 2026 deadline is May 17, with results announced May 29.

calls.title: 1839 Awards Color Photography Contest
calls.description: Celebrating color photography. Winners receive $4,000 cash prizes, dedicated digital gallery, global artist directory placement.
calls.summary: Celebrating color photography. $4,000 in cash prizes, digital gallery, and global artist directory.
prose: 1839 Awards is a contest platform with a recurring schedule of category-themed photography competitions. The Color Photography Contest is its color-focused cycle. The platform's name references the year of photography's invention.

The 2026 jury is built from established institutions: Alessa Widmer (University of Zurich), Derek Eng (Dwell), Hanna Girma (Serpentine), Hilary Greenbaum (Whitney Museum), Kelly Sidley (Bonhams), and Maia Murphy (Phaidon Press).
Total cash prizing is $4,000. Selected work is shown in a dedicated digital gallery on the 1839 Awards platform plus placement in the platform's global artist directory.

Eligibility is open globally to photographers 18+. Submission is through the 1839 Awards platform with 1–5 images. Fee is tiered $25–$50 by submission scale. The 2026 deadline was April 9; results announced June 5, 2026.

calls.title: Photographic Performance 2026
calls.description: Sixth year. Seeking solo/cooperative exhibitions with conceptual narrative. Photography-based or mixed media welcome; installations considered. Johnson City, TX.
calls.summary: Sixth year. Seeking solo/cooperative exhibitions with conceptual narrative. Photography-based or mixed media. Texas.
prose: Photographic Performance is A Smith Gallery's annual call for sustained, conceptually-driven photographic projects — distinct from the gallery's themed open calls ("imagined", "abandoned", etc.), this call selects four artists for solo or cooperative exhibition rather than group thematic shows. The 2026 cycle is the sixth year of the program.

The call accepts photographic images, mixed media combinations, photography as sculpture, installations, and other formats where photography functions as the conceptual core. The selection criteria emphasize work with conceptual narrative — projects that operate as bodies of thought rather than collections of strong individual images.

Four selected artists each receive a month-long online exhibition (July, August, September, or October 2026), a consultation with gallery directors Amanda Smith and Kevin Tully, a Gallery Talk blog post, and an exhibition catalogue with director foreword and artist statement. Ten additional entries receive written reviews — feedback for non-selected applicants who reached the second-round consideration.

Selection is by Smith and Tully (gallery co-directors). Eligibility is open to professional and amateur photographers internationally. Previously exhibited work at A Smith Gallery is ineligible. AI-generated images are not currently accepted due to copyright concerns.

Entry fee is $75 per proposal (non-refundable). Submissions require 12 to 20 images per project (max 1800 pixels, JPEG, 72 ppi), an artist statement, and a bio. The 2026 deadline is May 18; results announced May 22.

calls.title: reFocus Awards - Black and White Photo Contest
calls.description: International black and white photography contest across 19 categories. Images and series (2–5 images) accepted. Blind two-round judging by editors from The New York Times, Robb Report, and Condé Nast. Winners receive cash prizes, crystal trophies, published interviews, and Artist Directory profiles.
jury: Gabriel H. Sanchez, Photo Editor, The New York Times
Irene Opezzo, Photo Director, Robb Report
Rasha Kahil, Creative Director, HTSI Financial Times
Karin Mueller, Condé Nast Traveller UK
calls.summary: Black and white photography contest with $4,000 in prizes. Trophy, press coverage, artist directory. 19 categories.
prose: reFocus Awards is an international photography competition organization. The Black and White Photo Contest is one of reFocus Awards' themed competitions, focused exclusively on monochrome work. Submissions are accepted across 19 categories: Abstract, Architecture, Landscape, Portrait, Street, Wildlife, and others.

The judging is unusually heavyweight relative to the contest's size — the panel includes Gabriel H. Sanchez (Photo Editor, The New York Times), Irene Opezzo (Photo Director, Robb Report), Rasha Kahil (Creative Director, HTSI Financial Times), Karin Mueller (Condé Nast Traveller UK), and Daniel Melamud (Editor, Rizzoli), alongside curator Carol Olona. The structure is a two-step blind review process with jury selection followed by a public People's Vote Award.

Cash prizes total $4,000 across categories, with top winners receiving $2,500+. Beyond cash, winners receive a custom engraved crystal trophy, a published interview, press release and digital badges, public artist directory profile, placement in the winner's gallery, and international media exposure.

Entry fees are pay-per-entry: $25–$30 (Non-Pro/Pro) for a single image; $40–$50 for a series of 2–5 images. Additional category entries are 50% off. Bundle packs are available: 5 credits for $88–$105, or 10 credits for $175–$210.

Eligibility is open globally to professional and non-professional photographers. Previously published or award-winning images are accepted, and images may be entered to multiple contests simultaneously. AI-generated images are not accepted. Submissions are JPEG or PNG, minimum 1,500 pixels on the longest edge, max 10 MB, no watermarks or logos. The 2026 deadline is May 25; results announced June 17.

calls.title: The Book Project - Street Photography
calls.description: Hardbound books each featuring 10 photographers (5 images each). Sixth call focusing on street photography. Portland, OR.
jury: Todd Johnson, Founder & Director, Black Box Gallery
calls.summary: Hardbound books each featuring 10 photographers. Sixth call focusing on street photography. Portland, OR.
prose: Black Box Gallery's Book Project is a recurring publishing program — distinct from the gallery's themed exhibition calls — where each accepted cycle is published as a 12×12 inch hardbound square book through Blurb Books. The 2026 Street Photography call is the sixth in the Book Project series.

The format is concentrated: 10 photographers are selected, each receiving 5 photographs in the published book. The book is offered for sale through Blurb's print-on-demand network, with photographers retaining all copyright (files are used solely for book printing).

The brief is straightforward: street photography featuring chance encounters and random moments within public places. Selection prioritizes work that operates in the documentary tradition of street photography — observed rather than staged.
The juror is Todd Johnson, founder and director of Black Box Gallery, who holds an MFA in Photography from the San Francisco Art Institute and serves as juror across all Black Box programs.

Entry fee is $40 for a submission of 5 to 10 images. Eligibility is open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers. Application is by email after PayPal fee payment, with image titles and JPEG attachments at 1200 pixels on the longest side, 72 PPI, max 5 MB each. The 2026 deadline is May 25; notification within 7 to 10 days.

calls.title: The Hand Magazine - Issue #53 Summer 2026
calls.description: Submit up to 5 images for Issue #53 of this international publication focused on photographic printmaking and hand-printed work. No theme — variety wanted. Must be a subscriber to submit. Ideal for alternative process artists.
calls.summary: International publication for photographic printmaking and hand-printed work. No theme. Must be a subscriber.
prose: The Hand Magazine is a color print publication that features photographic and printed-media work selected through a juried process. The magazine has run for over 50 issues — Issue #53 marks the Summer 2026 edition.

The Hand has a deliberately atypical editorial position: "There is NEVER A THEME. We want variety." Each issue brings together work across genres and processes — alternative-process prints, photogravures, photopolymer plates, screen prints, hybrid photo-and-print work — chosen for visual interest rather than thematic cohesion. The magazine specifically seeks work that incorporates photographic or printed media, making it especially relevant for alternative-process and hybrid-media practitioners.

Submission is gated by subscription: photographers must subscribe to a single issue (or be existing subscribers) before submitting. Subscription rates vary by region: $15 in the U.S., $20 in Canada and Mexico, $30 elsewhere. Multiple individuals at the same address may submit up to 5 combined images under one subscription.

Each photographer submits a maximum of 5 images per issue. Selection is juried and competitive — the guidelines explicitly note: "There is no guarantee that your work will be printed." Selected work appears in the printed magazine.
The Issue #53 deadline is May 31, 2026. Submissions to thehandmagazine@gmail.com (or thehandmagazine@icloud.com for Kansas residents paying by check or money order).

calls.title: JUST ADD WATER
calls.description: Exploring water — oceans, rain, rivers, puddles. Artists worldwide invited. Online exhibition. Boston, MA.
calls.summary: Exploring water — oceans, rain, rivers, puddles. Online exhibition. Boston, MA.
prose: JUST ADD WATER is a themed open call from Art Fluent, the Boston-based curatorial platform. The brief is the element itself: oceans, rain, rivers, puddles, or even just a hint of blue — work that engages with water as subject matter or as metaphor.

Cash prizes total $1,250: a Best of Show award of $750 and two Director's Choice awards of $250 each. All accepted work is displayed in the online gallery on art-fluent.com. Selection is curated by Creative Director Amy Matteson Neill and an anonymous committee.

Entry fee is $25 for the first work and $10 each additional, up to a maximum of 20 entries per artist. All fine art mediums are accepted: painting, sculpture, photography, video, digital art. AI-generated work is not accepted, and previously exhibited work at Art Fluent is ineligible.

Submissions go through CaFÉ (callforentry.org), which requires a free artist account. Open globally to amateur and professional artists. The 2026 deadline is June 5 (midnight MST), with notifications by July 2.

calls.title: BOTANICALS
calls.org: New York Center for Photographic Arts
calls.description: All photographic processes accepted. Winners receive $4,000 cash, online gallery feature, catalog publication. New York, NY.
calls.summary: All photographic processes accepted. $4,000 cash prize, online gallery, and catalogue. New York.
prose: BOTANICALS is the New York Center for Photographic Arts (NYC4PA) themed call for photography of plant life — flowers, trees, leaves, vines, fruit, gardens, beaches, windowsills, parks, rainforests. The brief is loose: any photographic process and any setting where vegetation is the subject.

Cash prizes total $4,000 across 10 awards: a Grand Prize of $1,100, three First Prizes of $400, three Second Prizes of $325, and three Third Prizes of $250. Beyond the cash awards, 20 Juror Selections and 20 Honorable Mentions are also recognized — featured in the online gallery and catalog with certificates. The winning image is also featured on the NYC4PA website homepage.

The 2026 cycle is juried by Dan Burkholder, photographer known for pioneering work in HDR and mobile photography techniques. All 2D photographic mediums are accepted: print, transfers, encaustic, black-and-white, color, and experimental techniques.

Entry fee is $40 for the first three images, with $10 each additional and unlimited submissions allowed. Eligibility is open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers. Images that have won NYC4PA prizes in the prior two years are not eligible. Submissions go through SmarterEntry; the 2026 deadline is June 7 at midnight Pacific Time.

calls.title: Snider Prize
calls.org: Museum of Contemporary Photography at Columbia
calls.description: For emerging artists in final year of graduate study. Winner: $3,000; two honorable mentions: $500 each. Acquisitions into MoCP permanent collection.
calls.summary: For emerging artists in final year of graduate study. $3,000 winner. Acquisitions into MoCP permanent collection.
prose: The Snider Prize is administered by the Museum of Contemporary Photography (MoCP) at Columbia College Chicago. The prize was established by Lawrence K. and Maxine Snider to support emerging photographers transitioning from graduate study into professional practice.

Eligibility is restricted to artists in their final year of graduate study in photography or photo-related disciplines. The award structure is one main winner and two honorable mentions: the winner receives $3,000 plus acquisition of the winning work into the MoCP permanent collection; honorable mentions receive $500 each. Acquisition into MoCP's collection is the more durable element of the prize — the museum holds significant photography holdings used in exhibitions and academic research.

Recent winners include Ching-Wei Wang (MFA, Parsons, 2025), Claire Warden (MFA, School of the Art Institute of Chicago, 2024), and Sidian Liu (MFA, Parsons, 2023). The pattern across recent cycles favors candidates from major MFA programs, though the prize is not formally restricted to specific institutions.

Submissions go through JotForm and require 10 images plus supporting materials. Entry fee details and jury composition are not published on the prize landing page. The 2026 deadline is June 12 at 11:59 PM; results announced fall 2026.

calls.title: Evolution Grant
calls.description: Unrestricted $1,000 grant per cycle to individual artist with recognized artistic excellence and demonstrated commitment.
calls.summary: Unrestricted $1,000 grant per cycle for individual artists with recognized artistic excellence.
prose: The Evolution Grant is a recurring unrestricted grant from Art Fluent, the same Boston-based curatorial platform that runs themed open calls like HER.SELF and Manipulation & Illusion. Each grant cycle awards $1,000 to one visual artist with the funds explicitly unrestricted — applicants do not need to propose a specific project, and the grant can support any expense that enhances the artist's ability to make work (materials, studio rent, equipment, time off).

Selection is on the body-of-work submitted rather than a single project pitch. Applications require 5 to 20 pieces, an artist statement, and a bio. The 2025 recipient was Mark Guglielmo. Once awarded, artists cannot reapply.
Eligibility is open worldwide to amateur and professional artists. All fine art mediums are accepted except AI-generated work; copies and instructor-guided pieces are excluded.

The application fee is $35 (non-refundable). Submissions go through CaFÉ (callforentry.org), which requires a free artist account. The June 2026 cycle deadline is June 19, 2026 at midnight MST; results announced by July 31.

calls.title: reFocus Awards - Color Photography Contest
calls.description: Celebrating color photography. Winners receive career-enhancing cash prizes and digital gallery placement.
jury: Gabriel H. Sanchez, Photo Editor, The New York Times
Irene Opezzo, Photo Director, Robb Report
Rasha Kahil, Creative Director, HTSI Financial Times
Karin Mueller, Condé Nast Traveller UK
calls.summary: Celebrating color photography. Cash prizes and digital gallery placement.
prose: reFocus Awards is a contest platform with a recurring schedule of category-themed competitions. The Color Photography Contest is the platform's color-focused cycle.

The 2026 jury is built primarily from photo editors and creative directors at major publications: Gabriel H. Sanchez (Photo Editor, The New York Times), Irene Opezzo (Photo Director, Robb Report), Rasha Kahil (Creative Director, HTSI Financial Times), Carol Olona, Karin Mueller (Condé Nast Traveller UK), and Daniel Melamud (Editor, Rizzoli).
Total prize value is $2,500. Selected work is shown in a digital gallery on the reFocus platform. AI-generated work is not accepted.

Eligibility is open globally to photographers 18+. Submission is through the reFocus website with 1–5 images per entry. Fee is tiered $25–$50 by submission scale. The 2026 deadline was April 29; results announced July 15, 2026.

calls.title: Helsinki Analog Festival 2026 - Analog Practice Exhibition
calls.description: International open call for artists using analog processes across various mediums. Celebrating materiality and craftsmanship.
calls.summary: International open call for artists using analog processes. Celebrating materiality and craftsmanship.
prose: Helsinki Analog Festival is held annually in Helsinki, Finland. The Analog Practice Exhibition is the festival's international open call for artists working with analog processes — celebrating materiality and craftsmanship in image-making.
Eligibility is process-restricted: analog photographic practices only. The festival is organized by Finnish Darkroom.
Top prize is €500 plus exhibition during the festival. Submission is through ForPhotographersOnly. Fee is €20.
The 2026 edition deadline was December 14, 2025.

calls.title: 2027 Artist-in-Residence Program
calls.description: One-month artist residency in Syracuse, New York, for photographers and image-based media artists worldwide. Light Work has supported over 400 artists through this program since 1975, many achieving international recognition. Twelve to fifteen artists selected annually. Residents receive a $7,500 stipend, a furnished apartment, 24-hour access to state-of-the-art digital and darkroom facilities, and generous staff support. Selected artists are published in a special edition of Contact Sheet: The Light Work Annual with a commissioned essay. The program partners with Autograph ABP and the Darryl Chappell Foundation.
calls.summary: One-month residency in Syracuse for photographers. $7,500 stipend, apartment, 24-hour darkroom/digital access. Published in Contact Sheet.
prose: Light Work is a non-profit photography center in Syracuse, New York, founded in 1973. Its Artist-in-Residence program — running for over five decades and counting more than 400 alumni — is one of the longest-running photography residencies in the United States. Past residents have included photographers who went on to MacArthur Fellowships, museum acquisitions, and major editorial careers; the alumni list is treated as part of the program's identity.

Each cycle, twelve to fifteen artists are selected for a one-month residency at Light Work's facility (316 Waverly Avenue, Syracuse). Residents receive a $7,500 stipend, a furnished apartment near campus, 24-hour access to Light Work's digital lab and darkroom, and on-staff support. Each resident's work is published in Contact Sheet, Light Work's annual publication, with a commissioned essay.

Eligibility is open globally to artists working in photography or image-based media. There is no application fee. The program is in partnership with Autograph ABP and the Darryl Chappell Foundation, which jointly support specific residency lines for British photographers and Black photographers respectively.

Applications are submitted through SlideRoom (with a physical mail option for those who require it). The 2027 cycle deadline is July 1, 2026. The selection committee reviews applications in late fall, with notifications sent in December.

calls.title: Arte Laguna Prize 2026
calls.description: International competition at Arsenale Nord, Venice. 120 finalists exhibited in 3,000 sq. meters. €10,000 first prize. All contemporary art media welcome.
jury: Sarah Crowe, Assistant Curator, Kunsthalle Wien
Yuko Hasegawa, Curator & Director, 21st Century Museum, Kanazawa
Wang Chunchen, Chief Curator, CAFA Art Museum Beijing
Linzi Stauvers, Artistic Director, Ikon Gallery
calls.summary: International competition at Arsenale Nord, Venice. 120 finalists. €10,000 first prize. All media.
prose: The Arte Laguna Prize was founded in 2006 by Cultural Association MoCA and is now in its 21st edition. The prize is one of Europe's largest cross-disciplinary art competitions, with categories spanning painting, sculpture, installation, photography, video art, performance, virtual and digital art, digital graphics, environmental and land art, urban and street art, and art design.

The main cash prize is €10,000 (subject to 25% withholding tax under Italian law). Beyond cash, 120 finalists exhibit at Arsenale Nord in Venice from November 6 through 29, 2026 — the same Venetian Arsenale site that historically hosts portions of the Venice Biennale. Special prizes additionally include residencies at venues in Venice, Australia, China, Croatia, and Peru, plus gallery exhibitions and corporate commissions.

The 2026 jury comprises seven international curators including Yuko Hasegawa (Curator & Director, 21st Century Museum Kanazawa), Wang Chunchen (Chief Curator, CAFA Art Museum Beijing), Linzi Stauvers (Artistic Director, Ikon Gallery), Hèlio Menezes (curator), Gianluigi Ricuperati (curator and art director), Jemima Kulumba (Co-Founder, WIA), and additional industry-side voices.

Entry fees are tiered by age: artists under 35 pay €97.60, artists 35 and over pay €122. Additional works beyond 5 cost €24.40 each. There is no age limit for entry, and the prize is open to all nationalities and qualifications. The 2026 deadline is June 30; the finalist exhibition opens November 6.

calls.title: IX International Mini Print Cantabria 2026
calls.description: Theme: Open Sea — Reality, imagination and poetics. All printmaking disciplines including digital prints and monotype. Max image/paper: 20x20 cm. Cantabria, Spain.

Eugènia Agustí, Visual Artist & Lecturer, University of Barcelona
Usama Habil, Artist & Assistant Professor, University of Salamanca
calls.summary: Theme: Open Sea. All printmaking disciplines including digital. Max 20x20 cm. Cantabria, Spain.
prose: International Mini Print Cantabria is a printmaking competition held in Santander, Spain, now in its 9th edition (founded 2018). The format is in the name: each work is a "mini print" no larger than 20×20 cm in image and paper dimensions, with the small format chosen to make printmaking accessible across techniques and to scale a large international group exhibition into a manageable space.

The 2026 theme is "Open Sea — Reality, imagination and poetics." All printmaking disciplines are accepted, including traditional techniques (etching, lithography, woodblock, linocut), monotype, and digital prints. Each artist may submit up to three prints.

The main prize pool is €4,000. Selected work is exhibited at the Exhibition Space of the Archive of the Port Authority of Santander from September 11 through December 8, 2026. Entry fees range from €35 to €65 depending on the submission tier.

The 2026 jury comprises three academics from European art universities: Carinna Parraman (Professor at the University of the West of England Bristol and director of the Centre for Print Research), Eugènia Agustí (visual artist and lecturer at the University of Barcelona), and Usama Habil (artist and Assistant Professor at the University of Salamanca). Submissions close July 31, 2026; jury deliberations conclude September 18.

The brief is broad in publishing context: artist books, self-published photobooks, limited editions, zines, and DIY publications all eligible.

calls.title: World Cyanotype Day
calls.description: Annual international celebration of the cyanotype process. Submit your cyanotype work to be featured.
calls.summary: Annual international celebration of the cyanotype process. Submit your cyanotype work to be featured.
prose: World Cyanotype Day is an annual celebration of the cyanotype process — a 19th-century alternative photographic technique that uses iron-based salts and UV light to produce prints in distinctive shades of blue. The event was founded in 2015 by AlternativePhotography.com (itself established in 1999) and runs each year on the last Saturday of September. The 2026 cycle covers September 26 through October 2.

Submissions are free and open to anyone working with the process. Each year carries a theme — 2025's was "Cultivating Community," with the 2026 theme to be announced in spring. The format is single-image submissions: 1080px on the longest side, under 2MB, JPEG only (no PNG, TIFF, or HEIC), with filenames structured as "Name Surname, Title, Country.jpg." No nudes; submissions must follow the year's theme.
Selected work is shown across AlternativePhotography.com's gallery, Facebook, Instagram, Pinterest, BlueSky, and YouTube channels. There is no cash prize.

The event references Anna Atkins — the first woman to illustrate a photography book, using cyanotypes — as part of its lineage. AlternativePhotography.com is a non-profit, runs the event without sponsor backing, and maintains a substantial educational resource library on cyanotype chemistry, paper preparation, and exposure techniques.

calls.title: World Anthotype Day
calls.description: Annual celebration of plant-based photographic printing processes. Entries open August 1; submission deadline October 31 (last Saturday in October).
calls.summary: Annual celebration of plant-based photographic printing processes. Entries open August through October.
prose: World Anthotype Day is an annual celebration of the anthotype process — a 19th-century photographic technique that uses plant-based emulsions and sunlight to make images. The event runs from August 1 through the last Saturday in October each year, with submissions free and open to anyone working with the process. The 2026 cycle closes October 31.

Entries require three components: a written description of the process used (including the plant material, exposure time, and any layering), the final anthotype image at 2,500 pixels minimum, and a photograph of the source plant taken before processing. Each non-member submits a single print, made within the prior twelve months. Files go via WeTransfer, Dropbox, or Google Drive to anthotype@alternativephotography.com.

Selected work is featured across AlternativePhotography.com (~85,000 monthly visitors), the site's Facebook (12,000+ followers), Instagram (14,000), and YouTube channels. Exceptional images are considered for inclusion in the Anthotype Emulsions book series. There is no cash prize — recognition is editorial.

The event was originally held in August but moved to October after a participant survey: 99% of respondents preferred the later window for longer exposure times and access to ripe plant material. AlternativePhotography.com is a non-profit and runs the event without sponsor backing. The site's resource library lists 25+ commonly-used plants — beetroot, blackberry, butterfly pea, turmeric, walnut — and explicitly encourages experimentation with unusual emulsions.

prose: PhMuseum Days is the annual photography festival organized by PhMuseum in Bologna, Italy. The 2026 cycle is the 5th edition, running October 1–4, 2026 at the Ex Ospedale dei Bastardini venue. The 2026 theme is "Archipelago," exploring crisis and new models of coexistence.

The selection structure is layered. At least 3 photographers receive solo exhibitions at the main venue with substantial production support: a production budget of up to €2,500 plus VAT, a €300 artist fee, and a travel contribution scaled by region (€300 for Italy, €500 for Europe, €800 for overseas). One additional photographer is selected for a public billboard installation across 11 sites in Bologna's historical center, with €300 fee plus travel support.

Beyond solo placements, up to 40 images are selected for a sculptural collective installation (running September 19 through October 8 alongside the festival), and up to 20 projects are chosen for video screenings. The MPB Special Mention awards a €1,000 voucher for used photography gear.

The 2026 jury comprises Tara L.C. Sood (photographer/filmmaker), Pacifico Silano (visual artist), Rita Puig-Serra Costa (photographer), and Giuseppe Oliverio (PhMuseum's Founding and Artistic Director).

Entry fee is $38 (extended-deadline pricing). Submissions accept 5 to 20 photos as JPG/PNG at maximum 20MB each. Collaborative projects, works-in-progress, and previously submitted work are all accepted. AI-generated work is accepted but must be disclosed. All applicants receive free festival passes. The 2026 deadline is May 14.
