calls.title: Creatura Magazine Issue 02 — What We Call Home
calls.description: Open call for Issue 02 of this indie print magazine exploring the idea of home — not only as a physical space but as an emotional territory. Selected photographs featured in a collective section of the print edition.
calls.summary: Indie print magazine exploring the idea of home — not only as physical space but as emotional territory.
prose: Creatura is an indie print photography magazine. Issue 02 is themed What We Call Home — exploring the idea of home not only as a physical space but as an emotional territory. The framing makes room for diasporic, transient, and ambivalent readings of home alongside the literal.
Selected photographs are featured in a collective section of the print edition.
Eligibility is restricted geographically to Latin America. Submission is by Google Form. Fee is €15. The 2026 deadline was March 22.

calls.title: F-Stop Magazine Issue #137 — Open Theme
calls.description: No theme — all fine art and documentary photography welcome. Submit up to 12 photographs. One submission per person per issue. Featured artist selected from submissions. Published since 2004.
calls.summary: No theme — all fine art and documentary photography welcome. Published since 2004.
prose: F-Stop Magazine has been publishing themed photography issues online since 2004. Each issue is built around an open call — most issues center on a single category (documentary, conceptual, portrait, landscape, color, abstract, alternative process, photobook), but the magazine also runs periodic Open Theme issues with no category restriction.

Issue #137 is one of these Open Theme issues. The brief: any fine art or documentary photography is welcome. Each issue features a Featured Artist selected from the submissions plus a Group Exhibition with multiple photographers.

Each photographer may submit one entry per issue, up to 12 photographs, with an optional project statement and descriptive captions. Submissions are by email to fstopmagazine@gmail.com. Submission is free.
F-Stop publishes online — selected work appears on the magazine's website and remains in the archive indefinitely. The Issue #137 deadline is May 9, 2026; the issue publishes around June 1, 2026.

calls.title: F-Stop Magazine Issue #138 — Documentary 2026
calls.description: Documentary photography projects — work that focuses on recording events, environments, or everyday life in a straightforward, accurate way. Typically a longer-term focus than photojournalism, about a topic, place, or event. Submit up to 12 photographs with a project statement and/or descriptive captions. One submission per person. Published since 2004.
calls.summary: Documentary photography issue. Longer-term focus than photojournalism. Up to 12 images with project statement.
prose: F-Stop Magazine has been publishing themed photography issues online since 2004. Each issue centers on a single category — documentary, conceptual, portrait, landscape, color, abstract, alternative process, photobook — and runs as an open call to feature multiple photographers per issue. Issue 138 is a documentary photography issue.

The brief for the documentary issue is photography that records events, environments, or everyday life in a straightforward, accurate way. F-Stop draws an explicit distinction from photojournalism: documentary work has longer-term focus on a topic, place, or event, rather than newsworthy moments.

Submissions are free and limited to one per person per issue. Each submission can include up to 12 photographs with a project statement and/or descriptive captions. F-Stop publishes online — selected work appears on the magazine's website indefinitely as part of its archive.
The Issue #138 deadline is July 10, 2026; the issue publishes August 1, 2026.

calls.title: Photo Trouvée Virtual Artist Residency — Spring 2026
calls.description: 10-week virtual residency (April 24 – June 26, 2026) for artists who work with or are inspired by found/family photographs. Weekly Zoom calls, bio/statement workshops, artist talks, group feedback, accountability groups. Only 9 artists selected. Partial scholarships available.
calls.summary: 10-week virtual residency for artists working with found/family photographs. Weekly Zoom calls, only 9 spots.
jury: Juliana Naufel, Co-Founder, Photo Trouvée Magazine
Twiggy Boyer, Co-Founder, Photo Trouvée Magazine
prose: Photo Trouvée is a magazine and platform focused on found and family photographs as artistic source material. The Spring 2026 Virtual Artist Residency is the platform's structured online residency for artists working with or inspired by found/family photographs.

The residency runs ten weeks online: April 24 – June 26, 2026. The structure is intensively scheduled — weekly Zoom calls, bio/statement workshops, artist talks, group feedback sessions, and accountability groups.
Only nine artists are selected per cycle, keeping the cohort small enough for sustained group feedback. Selection is by the magazine's co-founders Juliana Naufel and Twiggy Boyer.
Eligibility is open globally. Fee is $650 — covering the structured program rather than gallery production. Partial scholarships are available for applicants who can't cover the full cost.
Submission is through JotForm. The 2026 Spring deadline was April 13.

calls.title: HNDL Magazine — PRIDE Issue
calls.description: Submissions for the PRIDE issue of HNDL Magazine, an indie publication by and for neurodivergent, disabled, and chronically ill creatives. Accepting art, poetry, creative nonfiction, prose, photography, and zines. Especially seeking candid photography and creative nonfiction. Written pieces max 4 pages, no PDFs. Unpaid — contributors receive a printed copy.
calls.summary: Indie publication by and for neurodivergent, disabled, and chronically ill creatives. Accepting photography and more.
prose: HNDL Magazine is an indie publication by and for neurodivergent, disabled, and chronically ill creatives. The PRIDE Issue is themed around Pride from within the publication's editorial frame — work by creatives who hold both disability and queer identities, and the layered experience that produces.

The publication is multidisciplinary: art, poetry, creative nonfiction, prose, photography, and zines all eligible. The editorial preference for this issue is candid photography and creative nonfiction. Written pieces are capped at 4 pages; no PDFs accepted.
AI-generated work is not accepted. Eligibility is restricted to neurodivergent, disabled, and chronically ill creatives.
The publication is unpaid — contributors receive a printed copy of the issue. Submission is by Google Form with up to 3 pieces. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was March 30.

calls.title: Off The Clock 2026
calls.description: 15th annual curated photo competition showcasing personal work. Juried by Chris Pichler, Founder and Publisher of Nazraeli Press, who selects 100 winning images. Winners receive a printed and PDF catalog, online gallery feature, social media exposure, and framed exhibition at an industry gala in Southern California. No categories, no series restrictions, no creation date restrictions — just your finest personal photography. APA members pay $20/image. No AI-generated content.
jury: Chris Pichler, Founder & Publisher, Nazraeli Press
calls.summary: 15th annual curated competition for personal work. Juror: Chris Pichler (Nazraeli Press). 100 winners, printed catalogue.
prose: Off The Clock is the annual photography competition organized by the American Photographic Artists chapter in Los Angeles (APA Los Angeles). The 2026 edition is the competition's 15th cycle. The premise is in the title: personal work made off the clock — outside commissioned commercial assignments.
The structural premise is unrestricted: no categories, no series restrictions, no creation date restrictions. AI-generated content is not accepted. APA members pay a discounted fee.
Selection is by Chris Pichler, founder and publisher of Nazraeli Press — one of the major US photobook publishers. Pichler selects 100 winning images.
Winners receive a printed and PDF catalog, an online gallery feature, social media exposure, and inclusion in a framed exhibition at an industry gala in Southern California.

Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through the APA website with unlimited single images. Fee is tiered $20–$40 ($20/image for APA members). The 2026 deadline was March 31; results announced June 2026.

calls.title: The Female Show 2026
calls.description: Group exhibition of national and international female artists at Munich Art Gallery in the Kunstareal, running October 15 – November 14, 2026, including Lange Nacht der Münchner Museen. Curated by Josephine Kaiser & Team. Seeks contemporary art by women beyond gender stereotypes and thematic clichés. Smaller formats preferred (up to 50×50 cm). Submit a PDF (max 5 pages, 5 MB) with short CV, artist statement, ~5 example images, Instagram and website. No participation or exhibition fees — only international shipping at artist's expense. Applications accepted in English or German.
calls.summary: Group exhibition of female artists at Munich Art Gallery in the Kunstareal. Contemporary art beyond gender clichés.
prose: Munich Art Gallery is located in the Kunstareal, Munich's central museum quarter. The Female Show is its annual group exhibition for national and international female artists. The 2026 edition runs October 15 – November 14, including Lange Nacht der Münchner Museen — Munich's annual long-night-of-museums event.

Curated by Josephine Kaiser & Team. The brief explicitly seeks contemporary art by women beyond gender stereotypes and thematic clichés. Smaller formats are preferred — up to 50×50 cm — for the gallery's hanging space.
Eligibility is restricted to women artists. Application is free, with no participation or exhibition fees. Selected artists cover only their international shipping cost.
Submission is by email with a single PDF (max 5 pages, 5 MB) containing short CV, artist statement, approximately 5 example images, Instagram, and website. Applications accepted in English or German.
The 2026 deadline was April 8; results announced June 8, 2026.

calls.title: Open Call — Il Reportage in Italia
calls.description: Open call for the 6th edition of Festival del Reportage in Ascoli Piceno (June 26–28, 2026). Seeking reportage photography projects made in Italy — completed or in progress, 15–25 images. At least some photos must be taken after January 1, 2025. Submit via Google Form with a file-sharing link (WeTransfer, Google Drive, etc.). Winner receives €500 cash prize, projection of work at the festival, and full hospitality including travel within Italy, accommodation, and meals. No restrictions on nationality, age, or experience.
calls.summary: Reportage photography projects made in Italy. €500 prize, festival projection, full hospitality. Ascoli Piceno.
prose: Festival del Reportage is held each year in Ascoli Piceno, in the Marche region of central Italy. The 2026 edition is the festival's sixth, scheduled June 26–28. The open call Il Reportage in Italia is the festival's photography track — focused specifically on reportage projects made in Italy.

Submitted projects can be completed or in progress, 15 to 25 images. There's a recency requirement: at least some of the photographs in the series must be taken after January 1, 2025. Eligibility is open globally — no restrictions on nationality, age, or experience.
The prize is €500 plus projection of the winning work at the festival and full hospitality during the festival weekend: travel within Italy, accommodation, and meals.
Application is free. Submission is by Google Form with a file-sharing link (WeTransfer, Google Drive, or similar). Deadline is May 8, 2026.

calls.title: 100 Emerging Artworks of 2026
calls.description: Annual international open call selecting 100 emerging and mid-career artists for a hardcover collector's book distributed globally via Amazon, Barnes & Noble, and art bookstores. All mediums accepted including photography. Submit up to 20 artworks. Top winner receives $1,000 cash prize, 4-page feature spread, and glass trophy. 2nd and 3rd place get 4-page spreads and trophies. All 100 selected artists receive book publication, certificate, and international distribution. Early bird deadline April 4 with reduced fees. 4th edition, previous collaborators include The Jealous Curator and Singulart.
calls.summary: 100 artists selected for a hardcover collector's book distributed globally. $1,000 top prize. All mediums.
prose: 100 Emerging Artworks of 2026 is an annual open call from Arts to Hearts Project, an international art platform that publishes themed art books and runs related open calls. The 2026 edition is the fourth cycle of this title.

100 artists are selected — emerging and mid-career — across all mediums, photography included. The publication is a hardcover collector's book, distributed globally via Amazon, Barnes & Noble, and independent art bookstores. Past collaborator partners include The Jealous Curator and Singulart.

Tiered prizing: the top winner receives $1,000 cash, a 4-page feature spread in the book, and a glass trophy. Second and third place each receive 4-page spreads and trophies. All 100 selected artists are included in the published book, receive a certificate, and benefit from the title's international distribution.
Eligibility is open to artists 18+ globally. Each application can include up to 20 artworks. Fee is $35 (with an early bird discount available before the April 4 cutoff). The 2026 deadline was May 4.

calls.title: Michael P. Smith Fund for Documentary Photography 2026
calls.description: Annual grant honoring legendary New Orleans documentary photographer Michael P. Smith. Awards cash prizes and exhibition opportunities to Gulf Coast photographers whose work combines artistic excellence and a sustained commitment to a cultural documentary project. Submit 10–20 images plus project statement (530 words) and bio via CaFE (Call for Entry). Subject matter not limited to Gulf Coast region. Winners donate two prints to NOPA's permanent collection and submit a final report by August 2026.
calls.summary: Annual grant for Gulf Coast photographers combining artistic excellence with sustained cultural documentary work.
prose: The Michael P. Smith Fund for Documentary Photography is an annual grant administered by the New Orleans Photo Alliance (NOPA). It honors Michael P. Smith, the New Orleans documentary photographer who spent decades photographing the city's musical, religious, and cultural life — work now held in the Historic New Orleans Collection.

The grant supports Gulf Coast photographers whose work combines artistic excellence with sustained commitment to a cultural documentary project. Eligibility is restricted by region: applicants must be from Gulf Coast states. Subject matter, however, is not limited to the Gulf Coast region — the photographer must be from there, the work need not be about there.
Top prize is $3,000. Winners donate two prints to NOPA's permanent collection and submit a final report by August 2026.
Submission is through CaFÉ with 10–20 images plus a 530-word project statement and bio. Fee is $25. The 2026 deadline was February 2.

calls.title: Luz e Sombra — National Photography Competition
calls.description: National photography competition exploring the relationship between light and shadow across themes of heritage, nature, architecture, and daily life. Submit a series of 6 photographs with a conceptual synopsis (1,500 chars) and bio (1,000 chars). Six finalists selected — works published in an artist-edition book, shown in a traveling exhibition at three venues, and featured in the Égide digital gallery. Open to professional and amateur photographers who are Portuguese citizens or residents of Portugal.
calls.summary: Portuguese competition exploring light and shadow. Six finalists published in artist-edition book and traveling exhibition.
prose: Luz e Sombra is a Portuguese national photography competition organized by Égide — Associação Portuguesa das Artes. The brief structures the relationship between light and shadow across four working themes: heritage, nature, architecture, and daily life — open to interpretation across documentary, fine art, and conceptual approaches.
Eligibility is restricted by nationality and residency: Portuguese citizens or residents of Portugal. Both professional and amateur photographers may apply.

Selection structure: six finalists. Total prize pool is €6,000 split as €3,000 (first), €2,000 (second), €1,000 (third). Beyond cash, finalists' works are published in an artist-edition book, shown in a traveling exhibition across three venues, and featured in the Égide digital gallery.

Each application is a series of 6 photographs with a conceptual synopsis (1,500 characters) and biography (1,000 characters). Submission is through the Égide website. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was April 30; results announced May 2026.

calls.title: CPG Mentorship Programme 2026
calls.description: 1:1 mentoring programme pairing artists with established photographers, curators, and mediators for four meetings over six months (May–October 2026), in person or online. Mentees receive CHF 500 project support and free access to two online masterclasses. 2026 mentors include Hannah Darabi, Yann Mingard, Abdo Shanan, Holly Roussell, Jermaine Francis, and others. Open to professional artists and photographers (including self-taught) not enrolled in another programme or academic course. Fluency required in one of: French, English, Italian, Arabic, German, Farsi, or Mandarin.
calls.summary: 1:1 mentoring with established photographers and curators over six months. CHF 500 project support included.
prose: The CPG Mentorship Programme is run by the Centre de la photographie Genève (CPG), the Geneva photography center. The structure is 1:1 mentoring rather than group workshop: each selected mentee is paired with an established photographer, curator, or mediator for four meetings over six months (May–October 2026), in person or online.
Mentees receive CHF 500 project support and free access to two online masterclasses.
The 2026 mentor cohort includes Hannah Darabi, Yann Mingard, Abdo Shanan, Holly Roussell, Jermaine Francis, and others. Each mentee gets one of these as their dedicated mentor for the program.

Eligibility is restricted to professional artists and photographers (including self-taught) not currently enrolled in another programme or academic course. Fluency is required in one of seven languages: French, English, Italian, Arabic, German, Farsi, or Mandarin.
Submission is through the CPG website. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was March 22; results announced May 2026.

calls.title: New Wave Photography Award 2026
calls.description: Biennial award for emerging photographers, judged by 16 international curators and professionals from Taiwan, Japan, South Korea, and Singapore. Submit a series of 15–25 images (created after 2021) with artist statement in Chinese and English (500 words each). Grand Prize receives TWD 100,000 (~$3,000) plus exhibition. Applicants must not have held solo exhibitions at museums, commercial galleries, or art fairs, and no more than 5 group shows. Students and persons with disabilities pay reduced fee of TWD 600.
jury: Chelsea Chua, Program Director, Objectifs Centre for Photography and Filmmaking
Wang Jo Hsuan, Executive Director, Taipei First High School of Art
Pin Leng, Secretary General, Fubon Cultural & Educational Foundation
Chiu Yu-Hsuan, Curator, Tokyo Metropolitan Museum of Photography
Peng-Hui Hou, Assistant Professor, National Taiwan Ocean University
Huang Shih-Tse, Photography Department Head, The Reporter
Ting Tsou, Curator, New Taipei City Museum of Art
Tsai Ming-Jiun, Deputy Director, Asia University Museum of Modern Art
Kimi Himeno, Editor-in-Chief, Akakasha & Founder, PURPLE Gallery
Sunyoung Kim, Senior Curator, Hanmi Museum
Sharleen Yu, Exhibition Curator, Taipei Fine Arts Museum
Tseng Shao-Chien, Professor, National Central University
calls.summary: Biennial award for emerging photographers. Judged by 16 curators from Taiwan, Japan, South Korea, and Singapore.
prose: The New Wave Photography Award is a biennial prize from Lightbox Photo Library, the Taipei-based photography library, exhibition space, and educational platform. The award is structured around emerging photographers — applicants must not have held solo exhibitions at museums, commercial galleries, or art fairs, and no more than five group shows.

Eligibility is geographically focused on Taiwan but the jury is regional. Sixteen jurors from Taiwan, Japan, South Korea, and Singapore — curators from Hanmi Museum, Tokyo Metropolitan Museum of Photography, Taipei Fine Arts Museum, New Taipei City Museum of Art, Objectifs (Singapore), WMA (Hong Kong), and others.
The Grand Prize is TWD 100,000 (approximately $3,000) plus an exhibition.

Submitted projects must be created after 2021 — recent work only. Each application is a series of 15–25 images with artist statement in both Chinese and English (500 words each). Standard fee is TWD 1,200; students and persons with disabilities pay a reduced TWD 600.
Submission is through the Lightbox award portal. The 2026 deadline was April 30; results announced July 2026.

calls.title: Solo Statement — Doesn't Play Well with Others
calls.description: One-night solo takeover of Bushwick Gallery in Brooklyn — a full transformation of the space by a single artist. No shared walls, no compromise. All mediums welcome including photography, installation, performance, and digital. No prior gallery experience required. Submit artist statement (150 words), creative vision for the space, 3–5 recent work images, and two artistic influences. Gallery provides professional photography, press release, and promotional support. Exhibition April 17, 2026.
calls.summary: One-night solo takeover of Bushwick Gallery in Brooklyn. Full transformation of the space by a single artist.
prose: Solo Statement — Doesn't Play Well with Others is a one-night solo takeover of Bushwick Gallery in Brooklyn. The structural premise is unusual: rather than a group show, one artist gets the full gallery space for a single night to transform completely — no shared walls, no compromise.
The brief is open across mediums: photography, installation, performance, digital. No prior gallery experience required.
What's offered: professional photography of the show, a press release, and promotional support from the gallery. The exhibition runs one night on April 17, 2026.
Each application includes an artist statement (150 words), creative vision for the space, 3–5 recent work images, and two artistic influences.
Eligibility is open. Submission is through the gallery's website. Fee is $25. The 2026 deadline was March 27.

calls.title: The Woman Artist Award — 6th Edition
calls.description: Global contemporary art prize celebrating emerging and mid-career women artists. Open theme — any subject, style, or medium including painting, sculpture, photography, performance, installation, and digital art. Winner receives cash prize, engraved glass trophy, book feature interview, website spotlight, and Women in Arts Network membership. Runners-up receive trophies, interviews, and network features.
calls.summary: Global art prize celebrating emerging and mid-career women artists. Open theme, any medium including photography.
prose: The Woman Artist Award is an annual prize from Arts to Hearts Project, a global art platform that runs themed open calls. The 2026 edition is the award's 6th cycle.

Eligibility is restricted to emerging and mid-career women artists 18+ globally. Open theme — any subject, style, or medium including painting, sculpture, photography, performance, installation, and digital art.

The winner receives a $500 cash prize, an engraved glass trophy, a book feature interview, a website spotlight, and Women in Arts Network membership. Runners-up receive trophies, interviews, and network features.
Submission is through the Arts to Hearts Project website. Fee is $12. The 2026 deadline was March 27.

calls.title: Solstice Magazine Issue 71 — Editorial Submissions
calls.description: Submit fashion and editorial photography for publication in Issue 71 of Solstice Magazine, a London-based fashion publication. Send editorial submissions via email.
calls.summary: Fashion and editorial photography for publication in Issue 71 of this London-based fashion magazine.
prose: Solstice Magazine is a London-based fashion publication. The Issue 71 editorial submissions call is open to fashion and editorial photographers — work suitable for the magazine's editorial spreads rather than fine art portfolios.
Submission is structured around fashion-shoot conventions: minimum 5 looks, 3 images per look. The structure favors complete editorials rather than single images.
Selected work is published in Issue 71 of Solstice. Submission is by email. Application is free. Eligibility is open globally. The 2026 deadline was March 21.

calls.title: LSI Women in Photography Grant 2026
calls.description: Grant for women photographers to complete an in-progress personal project. Theme: Where We Stand — seeking work rooted in lived experience, proximity, trust-based relationships, and ethical representation. Submit 10 images, artist statement, project proposal, and budget via Picter. Winner receives $10,000 plus a new Leica camera and lens from Leica North America. Limited to first 100 applicants. Open globally, no Leica camera or LSI membership required.
calls.summary: Theme: Where We Stand. $10,000 grant plus Leica camera and lens. Limited to first 100 applicants.
prose: The LSI Women in Photography Grant is the Leica Society International's annual project-completion grant for women photographers. The 2026 theme is Where We Stand — seeking work rooted in lived experience, proximity, trust-based relationships, and ethical representation. The brief favors documentary and personal-project work over staged or commercial photography.
The grant supports completing an in-progress personal project rather than starting from scratch. Applicants submit a project proposal and budget alongside the work itself.

The award is generous: $10,000 cash plus a new Leica camera and lens from Leica North America. Importantly, the grant has no equipment-brand requirement — applicants do not need to use a Leica camera or be LSI members. It's a brand-supported but not brand-restricted prize.

Application is capped: limited to the first 100 applicants. Eligibility is open globally to women photographers 18+. Submission is through Picter with 10 images, artist statement, project proposal, and budget.
Fee is $35. The 2026 deadline was April 24; results announced May 29, 2026.

calls.title: Roma E'Festival — Street Photography Awards 2026
calls.description: International street photography contest, 3rd edition. Five categories: Single Image (color/open), Black & White, Smartphone, Photographic Project (5–15 images), and AI-Generated (separate judging). Top 3 finalists per category receive prizes from partners Fotodiego, Fowa, and Ricoh GR. All finalists exhibited at Officine Fotografiche in Rome (October 16–18, 2026) and published in international catalogue. Multi-category passes available. No generative AI in street categories.
jury: Gianluca De Dominici, Writer & Photography Editor
calls.summary: Five categories including Smartphone and AI-Generated. Finalists exhibited in Rome. Leica-sponsored prizes.
prose: Roma E'Festival is an international street photography competition organized by Effe4.0 Street Photography, in its third edition for 2026. The festival proper runs October 16–18 in Rome, with finalists exhibited at Officine Fotografiche.

Submissions are split across five categories: Single Image (color/open), Black & White, Smartphone, Photographic Project (5 to 15 images), and AI-Generated images, which are judged separately under their own selection process — generative AI is explicitly excluded from the four conventional street categories. Multi-category passes provide a 50% discount: the EFFE4 PRO pass (€50) covers Street, B&W, and Smartphone; the EFFE4 FULL pass (€70) covers all categories.

Finalists receive a physical print and exhibition for the duration of the festival, inclusion in the official catalogue, a touring exhibition appearing alongside the main festival, and visibility through the festival's website and social channels. Top three finalists per category receive prizes from partners Fotodiego, Fowa, and Ricoh GR — equipment, monographs, solo exhibitions, and editorial reviews depending on category.

The jury comprises ten international photographers and editors: Rui Palha, Pau Buscató, Barbara Di Maio, Liliana Ranalletta, Mario Mencacci, Arez Prod, Claudio Palmisano, Dario Coletti, Sonia Simbolo, and Gianluca De Dominici. Eligibility is open globally; previously published or award-winning work is permitted, except images that won first prize at major international festivals. The deadline is July 31, 2026.

calls.title: Dyonyzine Issue 06 — Second Helpings
calls.description: Asian-American-founded creative arts magazine accepting submissions for Issue 06 themed around food — a meal is never just a meal. Accepting photography, visual art, drawings, paintings, digital illustrations, multimedia works, and more alongside poetry, prose, and essays. Open to all ages, backgrounds, locations, and experience levels. Volunteer-run, completely free to submit.
calls.summary: Asian-American creative arts magazine. Issue themed around food — a meal is never just a meal. Free to submit.
prose: Dyonyzine is an Asian-American-founded creative arts magazine published as a volunteer-run independent project. Issue 06 — Second Helpings is themed around food: the working premise is that a meal is never just a meal.

The magazine is multidisciplinary by design. Submissions accepted include photography, visual art, drawings, paintings, digital illustrations, multimedia works, and a literary side: poetry, prose, and essays. Photography is one part of a broader publication.
Eligibility is open to all ages, backgrounds, locations, and experience levels — no restriction by career stage. AI-generated work is not accepted.
The magazine is volunteer-run and submission is completely free. Each applicant may submit up to 3 entries. Submission is via Google Form.
The Issue 06 deadline was April 28, 2026; selections communicated May 5–8, 2026.

calls.title: FeelsZine Issue 26 — Desire
calls.description: Canadian creative zine accepting submissions for Issue 26 themed around desire. Accepts photography, illustration, collage, typography, and comics. Submit 1–2 works at 6.5×9.5 inches with 0.125-inch bleed. Unpaid publication. Submit via email.
calls.summary: Canadian creative zine. Issue 26 themed around desire. Accepts photography, illustration, collage, and more.
prose: FeelsZine is a Canadian creative zine. Issue 26 is themed around desire — the brief is left open for interpretation across approaches.

The publication is multidisciplinary: photography sits alongside illustration, collage, typography, and comics. Each issue features submissions across these categories rather than restricting to a single medium.

Submission terms: 1–2 works per applicant, sized 6.5×9.5 inches with 0.125-inch bleed for the print layout. The publication is unpaid — contributors are not compensated, but the zine's print distribution carries the work to a small but committed audience.
Submission is by email. Application is free. Eligibility is open globally. The Issue 26 deadline was March 31, 2026; selections published July 2026.

calls.title: FeelsZine Issue 27 — Belonging
calls.description: Canadian creative zine celebrating its 10th anniversary with Issue 27 themed around belonging. Accepts photography, illustration, art, collage, and typography alongside poetry, essays, and fiction. Art submissions require artist statements and 300dpi files if accepted. Prioritizes Canadian content but open internationally. Include a short bio noting your country of origin.
calls.summary: Canadian creative zine's 10th anniversary issue. Theme: belonging. Accepts photography, illustration, collage, and more.
prose: FeelsZine is a Canadian independent zine that publishes biannually, alternating issues between thematic prompts. Issue 27, themed "Belonging," coincides with the magazine's 10th anniversary. Submissions are open across both writing and visual art, with a primarily Canadian editorial focus that also welcomes global contributors.

Accepted writing forms include poetry, personal essays, fiction, and interview proposals up to 1,200 words. Poetry and prose are limited to two pieces per submission unless part of a larger collection. Visual art submissions — photography, illustration, collage, typography — must be accompanied by a short artist statement, with 300dpi files requested if accepted.

Submissions are sent by email (submittofeels@gmail.com) as Word documents or Google Docs (no PDFs), with each entry including a short bio, work description, and country of origin. Previously published work is accepted as long as it is not simultaneously appearing in another Canadian independent magazine during FeelsZine's six-month publication window. The submission deadline is August 30, 2026; Issue 27 publishes in January 2027.

calls.title: Cut+Paste Magazine Issue 17 — Gather
calls.description: Photography magazine Issue 17 themed around autumn gathering — harvest scenes, friends and family, cozy candlelit moments. Accepts portraits (faceless preferred), nature, landscapes, abstract, still life, urban, and macro photography. No nudity or AI art. Pays $15 base plus $5–10 per additional piece if selected.
calls.summary: Themed around autumn gathering — harvest, friends and family, cozy candlelit moments. Pays $15+ if selected.
prose: Cut+Paste Magazine is an indie photography publication. Issue 17 is themed Gather — autumn gathering imagery: harvest scenes, friends and family, cozy candlelit moments.

Accepted work spans portraits (faceless preferred — the magazine prefers anonymous, mood-based portraiture over identifiable subjects), nature, landscapes, abstract, still life, urban, and macro photography. No nudity or AI-generated art.
The magazine pays contributors: $15 base rate plus $5–10 per additional piece selected. Submission is free.
Submission is through the magazine's Google Form. The Issue 17 deadline was April 9, 2026; selections published in September 2026.

calls.title: Outdoor Photography Magazine — Creative Wildlife
calls.description: Submit up to 5 creative wildlife images with captions for publication in Outdoor Photography Magazine (UK). Winner receives Celestron Nature DX 12×56 binoculars (RRP £229). JPG at 300ppi.
calls.summary: Submit creative wildlife images for Outdoor Photography Magazine (UK). Winner receives Celestron binoculars.
prose: Outdoor Photography Magazine is a UK monthly print magazine focused on landscape, wildlife, and outdoor photography, published by GMC Publications. The magazine runs themed reader-submission features in each issue. Creative Wildlife is the magazine's wildlife-focused cycle.

The brief favors creative approaches to wildlife photography rather than straight identification or natural-history-document work — the editorial preference is for compositional and atmospheric strength.
The winner receives Celestron Nature DX 12×56 binoculars (RRP £229).
Submission is up to 5 images at JPG 300ppi with captions. Eligibility is open globally. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was March 31.

calls.title: Outdoor Photography Magazine — Spring Landscapes
calls.description: Submit up to 5 spring landscape images with captions for publication in Outdoor Photography Magazine (UK). Winner receives Komperdell Carbon CXP Pro walking poles (RRP £150). JPG at 300ppi.
calls.summary: Submit spring landscape images for Outdoor Photography Magazine (UK). Winner receives walking poles.
prose: Outdoor Photography Magazine is a UK monthly print magazine focused on landscape, wildlife, and outdoor photography, published by GMC Publications. The magazine runs themed reader-submission features in each issue. Spring Landscapes is the seasonal landscape feature.

The brief is narrow: spring-season landscape photographs only. Selected work appears in the magazine's print pages — readership skews toward serious amateurs and active landscape photographers in the UK and elsewhere.
The winner receives Komperdell Carbon CXP Pro walking poles (RRP £150). Selection is for publication, not cash prize.

Submissions are up to 5 images at JPG 300ppi, with captions. Eligibility is open globally, but the magazine's editorial focus skews UK and European. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was April 30; selections published within 10 weeks of deadline.

calls.title: Zone Magazine — Open Submissions
calls.description: International photography zine accepting submissions year-round. No restrictions on genre. Submit up to 20 JPG images in a ZIP file (20MB max). Open to all ages worldwide.
calls.summary: International photography zine. No genre restrictions. Open to all ages worldwide. Year-round submissions.
prose: Zone is a photography-based publication that opens submissions to any visual artist, with no restrictions on age, medium, or approach. The submission format is unusual for the genre: artists send up to 20 JPG images bundled in a ZIP file, with a strict 20MB cap and no external links or WeTransfer accepted. There is no submission fee, and artists are explicitly invited to submit multiple times throughout the year.

Selected work appears primarily on the magazine's Instagram, where the editorial team curates the rollout — they reserve the right to select a subset from a series, reorder images, and occasionally crop. Some work is grouped with other artists in collective posts. Print publications are produced separately; recent print titles include Z3NE, Amongst the More Irritating Minor Ideas, and Alone Together.

The submission flow is deliberately low-friction. There is no themed brief; an optional bio, artist statement, and Instagram handle accompany the file. Artists receive no guarantee of feature, and the team does not provide individualized feedback on rejections.

calls.title: Burn Magazine — Open Submissions
calls.description: Photography magazine founded by David Alan Harvey (Magnum). Accepts photo essays, slideshows, and multimedia pieces on any subject. Submit as PDF. Images at 1080px shortest side. Features published on homepage with consideration for print.
calls.summary: Photography magazine founded by David Alan Harvey (Magnum). Photo essays and multimedia on any subject.
jury: David Alan Harvey, Founder & Magnum Photographer
prose: Burn was founded by David Alan Harvey in 2008 as an online photography magazine. It accepts work in any photographic genre — documentary, photojournalism, fashion, sports, science, natural history, art photography — with no curatorial preference for one over another. Submissions are sent as a PDF to submissions@burnmagazine.org, with images viewable in an online gallery (password-protected is fine), capped at 1080 pixels on the shortest side. A short explanatory text and artist statement accompany each submission.

Selected essays are published on the magazine's homepage and presented as multimedia pieces rather than flat galleries — slideshows, layered text, sequenced reveals. There is no fixed publication cadence; features run as they are accepted.

There is no submission fee and no eligibility restriction. Editorial leadership beyond Harvey has shifted in recent years, though the current editor is not publicly named. Burn does not run a formal prize or award alongside the open submission — homepage publication is the recognition.

calls.title: Incandescent Zine — Color Film Photography
calls.description: Bi-annual zine exclusively for color film/analog photography. Submit up to 12 color film images. No digital photography. Published by Pine Island Press, Portland, Oregon.
calls.summary: Bi-annual zine exclusively for color film photography. No digital. Published by Pine Island Press, Portland, Oregon.
prose: Incandescent Zine is a bi-annual zine published by Pine Island Press in Portland, Oregon. The publication is process-restricted: color film/analog photography only. No digital photography is accepted.
Each application can include up to 12 color film images. Submission is by email. Application is free.
Eligibility is restricted to analog photography. The 2026 deadline was March 1.

calls.title: Phases Magazine — Open Submissions
calls.description: International contemporary photography magazine publishing 3 portfolios per issue. Submit website link or low-res images.
calls.summary: International contemporary photography magazine publishing 3 portfolios per issue.
prose: Phases is an online photography magazine specializing in international contemporary work, founded in December 2012 by Jerome Montagne (France) and Alexis Vasilikos (Greece). The magazine has published 1,290 portfolios across irregular issues, with three portfolios featured per issue.

Submissions are open continuously, with no formal guidelines or themed brief. Artists send a link to their website, online work, or a few low-resolution attached images to submissions@phasesmag.com. The team receives high submission volume daily and cannot provide individualized responses or feedback — resubmission is encouraged if artists do not hear back.

There is no submission fee. Selected portfolios are published online; the magazine does not specify additional compensation or rights claims beyond publication. The editors' Greek and French base shows in recent contributor lists, with names like Mike Almiroudis, Yorgos Yatromanolakis, Yiannis Trifonopoulos, Gelly Siganou, and Georges Salameh appearing across recent and past selections.

calls.title: Noice Magazine — Open Submissions
calls.description: Print-to-order photography magazine with themed issues focusing on minimalism, social issues, and humor. Submit up to 10 images per themed call. Published as limited edition prints distributed worldwide.
calls.summary: Print-to-order magazine with themed issues. Minimalism, social issues, and humor. Limited editions.

calls.title: Solo Exhibition May 2026
calls.description: Monthly featured photographer showcase. Winner receives a full month online solo exhibition (May 1–31, 2026), permanent gallery presence, exclusive interview, social media promotion, newsletter feature, international press coverage, and commission-free sales. Submit a cohesive project or portfolio of 6–14 images.
jury: Sandrine Hermand-Grisel, Photographer & Founder, All About Photo
calls.summary: Monthly featured photographer showcase. Full month online solo exhibition, interview, and press coverage.
prose: All About Photo runs a recurring Solo Exhibition program — a monthly featured photographer slot rather than a single annual prize. The May 2026 cycle selects one photographer for a full-month online solo exhibition running May 1–31, 2026.

What's offered beyond the main exhibition: permanent gallery presence on the All About Photo platform, an exclusive interview, social media promotion, newsletter feature, international press coverage through the publication's network, and commission-free sales — All About Photo doesn't take a cut from any sales generated through the show.
Selection is by Sandrine Hermand-Grisel, photographer and founder of All About Photo. Single-juror selection.

Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through the All About Photo website with a cohesive project or portfolio of 6–14 images. Fee is $45. The May 2026 cycle deadline was April 21; selection announced May 1, 2026 with the exhibition opening.

calls.title: Solo Exhibition June 2026
calls.description: Monthly featured photographer showcase. Winner receives a full month online solo exhibition (June 1–30, 2026), permanent gallery presence, exclusive interview, social media promotion, newsletter feature, international press coverage, and commission-free sales. Submit a cohesive project or portfolio of 6–14 images.
jury: Sandrine Hermand-Grisel, Photographer & Founder, All About Photo
calls.summary: Monthly featured photographer showcase. Full month online solo exhibition, interview, and press coverage.
prose: All About Photo runs a monthly Solo Exhibition program — each month features a different photographer with a dedicated month-long online presentation. The June 2026 cycle is the next available slot.

The selected photographer receives a full month of online solo exhibition (June 1–30, 2026) featured on All About Photo's homepage, competition gallery, and showroom pages. Beyond the month, the work is permanently archived on the platform with a dedicated 20-image portfolio page, accompanied by an exclusive artist interview and social media promotion across the platform's Instagram, Facebook, and other channels.
Past winners have been featured in major international press outlets. Sales are commission-free — the artist retains 100% of the sale price.

Submission is open to photographers worldwide at any career level. Submissions are 6 to 14 cohesive images forming a project or portfolio. JPEG format, 72 dpi, no watermarks, flattened layers, file size under 2 MB, longest dimension max 1,200 pixels.

Selection is by Sandrine Hermand-Grisel, Founder & Editor of All About Photo. Entry fee is $45. The 2026 deadline is May 19; judging runs May 23–31; the selected photographer's solo exhibition opens June 1.

calls.title: SIYU Award 2026
calls.description: Award for young Swiss photographers (formerly vfg Young Talent Award). Ten finalists exhibited in a group show at Photobastei Zurich with a published catalogue. Three cash prizes awarded through the Alois Ottiger Grant, in memory of Swiss photographer Alois Ottiger (1941–2025). Free theme, all fields of photography. Submissions must be anonymous.
calls.summary: Award for young Swiss photographers. Ten finalists exhibited at Photobastei Zurich with catalogue. Free theme.
prose: The SIYU Award is the rebranded successor to the vfg Young Talent Award — a Swiss photography prize for young photographers. The 2026 edition is the first under the new SIYU name.

Cash prizes are awarded through the Alois Ottiger Grant, established in memory of Swiss photographer Alois Ottiger (1941–2025). Total prize pool is CHF 10,000 across three winners. Ten finalists are exhibited in a group show at Photobastei Zurich, with a published catalogue.

Eligibility is restricted to young Swiss photographers (under 40, with Swiss residency or nationality requirements). Submissions are made anonymously — the jury reviews work blind. Theme is free; all fields of photography are eligible. AI-generated work is accepted.
The 2026 jury is Virginie Otth (photographer and visual artist), Bassma El Adissey (freelance curator), and Gregor Brandli (filmmaker and photographer).
Submission is through Picter with 3–8 images. Fee is CHF 50. The 2026 deadline was April 30; results announced June 13, 2026.

calls.title: Alpine Fellowship Visual Art Prize 2026
calls.description: Annual visual art prize on the theme of JOY. Open to all visual art media including photography, painting, sculpture, video, and installation. One piece per entry, multiple entries allowed as separate submissions. Work must be entirely created without AI.
jury: Sue Grayson Ford MBE, Former Director, Serpentine Gallery & Photographers' Gallery London
Julian Spalding, Former Director of Art Galleries for Sheffield, Manchester & Glasgow
calls.summary: Annual prize on the theme of JOY. All visual art media including photography. No AI.
prose: The Alpine Fellowship Visual Art Prize is the visual art track of the Alpine Fellowship's annual symposium program. Each year carries a single thematic prompt — past themes have included "On Childhood," "On Identity," "On Forgiveness and Retribution," "On Untamed," "On Freedom," "On Language," "On Flourishing," and "On Fear." The 2026 theme is "JOY."

Cash prizes total £5,000 across three placements: £3,000 first place, £1,000 second place, and £1,000 third place. The 2026 jury comprises Sue Grayson Ford MBE (former Director of the Serpentine Gallery and Photographers' Gallery London) and Julian Spalding (former Director of Art Galleries for Sheffield, Manchester, and Glasgow).

The competition is open to all media — painting, sculpture, photography, video, installation — with videos capped at 8 minutes. Submissions are limited to one piece per entry, with multiple entries permitted as separate submissions. Each piece must include media type, date of creation, and dimensions where applicable.

Eligibility is open to all nationalities, with a minimum age of 18 at the time of entry. AI-generated work is explicitly excluded — applicants must confirm their work was created entirely without AI assistance at any stage. The entry fee is £10 per submission. The 2026 deadline is July 1.

calls.title: This Is a Person
calls.description: Portrait photography exploring interior life over surface identity. Seeking images that suggest psychological tension, ambiguity, vulnerability, or contradiction rather than likeness alone. Intentionally selective — approximately 10–12% acceptance rate. One image per selected artist exhibited.
calls.summary: Portrait photography exploring interior life over surface identity. ~10-12% acceptance rate.
prose: Decagon Gallery is an online photography gallery that runs themed juried calls. This Is a Person is its portrait-focused exhibition — but the brief deliberately moves away from likeness-based portraiture. The gallery is asking for images that suggest psychological tension, ambiguity, vulnerability, or contradiction. Surface description of who someone is matters less than what the photograph implies about their interior life.

Selection is intentionally restrictive: roughly 10–12% acceptance rate. One image per selected artist is exhibited, so applicants choose carefully which submission represents the strongest reading of the theme. The 2026 juror is Hossein Fardinfard, a portrait photographer whose own practice works in this register.

Cash prizes total $1,000: $500 (first), $300 (second), $200 (third). Eligibility is open globally to photographers 18+. Submission is through the gallery's website with up to 8 images per entry. Fee is $25.
The 2026 deadline was May 3; results announced May 2026.

calls.title: Monochrome Awards 2026
calls.description: International black and white photography competition with professional and amateur divisions across 14 categories including Abstract, Architecture, Fine Art, Landscapes, Nature, Portrait, Street, and Wildlife. Winners published in annual book and featured in online Winners Gallery.
calls.summary: International B&W competition with 14 categories. Professional and amateur divisions. Annual book.
prose: Monochrome Photography Awards is a competition exclusively for black-and-white photography, founded in 2014 and run annually. Entries are split between two main category groups — Professional and Amateur — with subcategories under each (Architecture, Fine Art, Photojournalism, Portrait, and others). Winners receive the titles "Monochrome Photographer of the Year" (Professional) and "Monochrome Discovery of the Year" (Amateur).

The cash prize pool is $3,000 across the two main categories, with category and subcategory medals stacking on top. Selected work is published in the Monochrome Photography Awards Annual Book — a print collection of first-, second-, and third-place winners plus honorable mention names — which functions as the long-term archive of each edition.

Submission requirements are tight: JPEG at 1200 pixels on the longest side, sRGB or Adobe98 8-bit, no watermarks or borders, no special characters in filenames. The entry portal is profile-based — applicants create an account, upload, and submit only after fees are paid. Early-deadline entries close July 5, 2026; final deadline runs through to November 15, with results announced January 3, 2027.

calls.title: Annual Photography Awards 2026
calls.description: International photography competition (8th edition) celebrating photographers of all levels. Five main categories — Architecture, Fine Art, Nature, People, and Special — with 25 subcategories. Accepts all formats, looking for bold and innovative approaches.
calls.summary: 8th edition. Five main categories, 25 subcategories. Looking for bold and innovative approaches.
prose: Now in its eighth edition, Annual Photography Awards is a worldwide competition open to professionals, amateurs, and students aged 18 and over. Submissions are accepted across five main categories — Architecture, Fine Art, Nature, People, and Special — with 25 subcategories in total. The Special category covers Aerial & Drone, Analog/Film, Minimalism, Night Photography, and Open; the People category includes Documentary, Portrait, Street, Body & Nudes, and Travel & Culture. Each subcategory has its own award track, so a photographer can be a category winner without competing across genres.

The cash prize pool is $5,000, distributed as a $2,500 Grand Prize plus five $500 Category Photographer of the Year awards. Beyond cash, winners and honorable mentions receive downloadable medals and certificates and inclusion in an online gallery on the awards site. Entries are judged anonymously by a panel of 20+ international photographers.

Entry fees follow a tiered structure: $25 for a single image or $35 for a series of up to 8 images at the early bird rate (deadline June 7, 2026), rising to $30 single / $40 series at final deadline (December 13, 2026). The contest is restricted to legal worldwide residents who are the original authors of submitted work. There is no nomination process; artists submit directly through the awards site.

calls.title: HER.SELF
calls.description: Online juried exhibit celebrating women in all their complexities — presence, resilience, beauty, and becoming. Open to all fine art mediums including photography. Artists receive 100% of sale price with no commission.
calls.summary: Celebrating women in all complexities — presence, resilience, beauty, becoming. 100% commission-free sales.
jury: Amy Matteson Neill, Creative Director, Art Fluent
prose: Art Fluent is a Boston-based curatorial platform (1 Washington Mall #1218, Boston, MA 02108) that runs themed online juried exhibitions across fine art mediums. "HER.SELF" is the platform's open call for work honoring women in all their complexities — the brief language emphasizes presence, resilience, beauty, and becoming, with no restriction on whether the artist or the subject is a woman.

Cash prizes total $1,250: a Best of Show award of $750 and two Director's Choice awards of $250 each. Beyond cash, all accepted work is displayed in the online gallery on art-fluent.com, with sales going through the platform at 100% commission to the artist. The selection is curated by Creative Director Amy Matteson Neill and an anonymous committee.

Entry fee is $25 for the first work and $10 each additional, up to 20 submissions per artist. Open globally to amateur and professional artists; AI-generated work is not accepted, and work made under instructor guidance or copied from other sources is excluded. Submissions go through CaFÉ (callforentry.org), which requires a free artist account.
Art Fluent does not provide individualized rejection feedback. The 2026 deadline is July 17 (midnight MST), with notification on August 21.

calls.title: Wider Skies Magazine — Issue 1
calls.description: New photo magazine exploring speculative futurism — not as science fiction, but as a way of noticing the near futures already forming around us. Submit up to 4 film photographs for the first issue. Looking for images that point to possible futures grounded in real life — moments of care, repair, survival, shared responsibility, quiet adaptation, or small signs of change. Film only. Free Kodak Pro 100 film available for those who need it.
calls.summary: New magazine exploring speculative futurism through film photography. Free Kodak film available for those who need it.
prose: Wider Skies is a new photo magazine launched in 2026 by curator Drew Arrieta. Issue 1 is the magazine's debut. The editorial premise is speculative futurism — not as science fiction, but as a way of noticing the near futures already forming around us.

The brief asks for images that point to possible futures grounded in real life: moments of care, repair, survival, shared responsibility, quiet adaptation, or small signs of change. The framing is observational documentary about the slow now rather than imagined or staged speculation.
Eligibility is process-restricted: film photography only — analog capture. AI-generated work is not accepted.
Notable practical support: free Kodak Pro 100 film is available for applicants who need it — the magazine subsidizes material rather than charging for entry.
Selection is by Drew Arrieta. Submission is through the Wider Skies website with up to 4 images. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was April 10; results announced May 2026.

calls.title: Atlas of Ruins Vol.3 — Call for Photos
calls.description: Submit photographs of architectural ruins from anywhere in the world for the third edition of the Atlas of Ruins book. Photos can depict ruins from any historical period — abandoned buildings, crumbling monuments, forgotten infrastructure. Two registration tiers: Early (until Jul 9, €13/1 photo, €25/up to 10), Regular (until Oct 1, €16/€30). Fees exclude VAT. 1st €1,200, 2nd €500, 3rd €300. All participants receive an ebook copy. Best photos from each country featured in the printed book.
calls.summary: Photographs of architectural ruins from anywhere in the world for a printed book. Two registration tiers, prizes up to €1,200.
prose: Atlas of Ruins is a recurring photo book series published by Reuse Italy, a cultural benefit corporation focused on reusing historical heritage through partnerships with architects, institutions, and national organizations. Vol.3 follows two earlier volumes (Vol.1 and Vol.2), both available for purchase on the Reuse Italy site.

The theme is architectural ruins from any historical period and any location worldwide — the open geographical and historical scope means submissions span everything from Roman antiquity through twentieth-century industrial decay. Entries can come from photographers, amateurs, students, architects, or designers, and individuals or collectives may participate.

Cash prizes: 1st place €1,200, 2nd €500, 3rd €300. Country mentions go to the best photo from each represented nation, and all participants receive an ebook copy of the published volume regardless of selection. Selected work appears in the printed Atlas of Ruins — Vol.3 with critical texts from international scholars.

Entry fees follow a tiered structure: early registration (until July 9, 2026) costs €13 for one photo or €25 for 2–10; regular registration (until October 1, 2026) costs €16 for one or €30 for 2–10. VAT is added separately. Submissions are JPEG, minimum 1200 pixels on the longest side, under 5MB, with no logos or watermarks. Higher-resolution files and location data are requested after selection.

calls.title: SVĚTOVA 1 Artist Residency 2026
calls.description: One-month creative residency for an emerging visual artist in Prague. Includes private bedroom, shared 30m² studio in the gallery, production budget of approximately €820, round-trip travel, curatorial support, and opportunities for a public workshop, artist lecture, and exhibition. Open to residents of 39 European countries plus Tunisia. Must not be enrolled in educational programs during the residency. Residency runs November 1 – December 6, 2026.
calls.summary: One-month residency for emerging artists in Prague. Studio, production budget, travel, and exhibition opportunity.
prose: SVĚTOVA 1 is an artist-run gallery and residency space in Prague. The annual residency program selects one emerging visual artist for a one-month creative residency. The 2026 residency runs November 1 – December 6.

The package includes a private bedroom, shared 30m² studio inside the gallery, a production budget of approximately €820, round-trip travel reimbursement, curatorial support, and opportunities for a public workshop, artist lecture, and exhibition during the residency.
Eligibility is restricted by geography: residents of 39 European countries plus Tunisia. Applicants must not be enrolled in educational programs during the residency.
Submission is by Google Form with a single PDF. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was March 23; results announced April 7, 2026.

calls.title: Monograph No. 01
calls.description: Open call for lens-based artists to submit a cohesive photographic project for an individual artist monograph. The selected artist receives full publication support including editing, design, printing, and marketing, plus 20% of the edition. Shortlist of 6 artists announced June 8; they receive published interviews. All submitted artists considered for Editor's Choice issue and digital features.
calls.summary: One artist receives full monograph publication — editing, design, printing, marketing, plus 20% of edition.
prose: No-Type Magazine is a Chicago-based photography publication. Monograph No. 01 is the magazine's inaugural monograph publishing program — an open call for lens-based artists to submit a cohesive photographic project for development into a full artist monograph.

The brief is open: photographic projects of any subject, genre, or process, presented as a cohesive and ambitious body of work ready to be developed into book form. Selection prioritizes work that has the structural depth to sustain a full monograph rather than a strong serial portfolio.

One artist is selected. The selected artist receives full monograph publication by No-Type, with all production costs covered — editing, design, printing, and marketing — plus 20% of the total edition to sell and distribute at the artist's discretion. The selected artist also receives consideration for additional features in the magazine and across No-Type's digital platforms.
Six finalists are selected for published interviews on the magazine's site. All submitting artists are also considered for inclusion in an Editor's Choice issue of the magazine.
Eligibility is open to lens-based artists. Submission fee is $20. Submissions go through Typeform; the deadline is May 31, 2026, with the shortlist announced June 8 and final selection June 15.

calls.title: 37th Annual Juried Photography Show
calls.description: Annual juried photography show in Ithaca, NY. Up to $1,000 in prizes awarded at judge's discretion. Original work not previously exhibited at the gallery is accepted across all photographic media. Post-production manipulation acceptable if based on original photographic process. Images wholly produced by AI are not acceptable. Accepted works must be matted, framed, and ready to hang. 30% commission on sales. Exhibition May 28 – June 27, 2026. Awards ceremony June 5.
calls.summary: Annual juried show in Ithaca, NY. Up to $1,000 in prizes. All photographic media accepted.
jury: 3-5 SOAG artist members + TBA prize judge
prose: State of the Art Gallery (SOAG) is an artist-run cooperative gallery in Ithaca, New York. The Annual Juried Photography Show is its longest-running open call. The 2026 edition is the 37th cycle.

Up to $1,000 in cash prizes is awarded at the judge's discretion — there's no fixed first/second/third structure, leaving the prize judge to allocate as they see fit. AI-only generated images are not accepted, but post-production manipulation is acceptable if based on an original photographic process.
Accepted works must be matted, framed, and ready to hang. The gallery commission on sales is 30%. The exhibition runs May 28 – June 27, 2026; the awards ceremony is June 5.

Selection is by 3–5 SOAG artist members plus a separate (TBA) prize judge. Eligibility is open globally — original work not previously exhibited at SOAG, all photographic media. Submission is through EntryThingy, 1–4 images. Fee is $35. The 2026 deadline was May 1.

calls.title: Homo Technologicus
calls.description: International call exploring the relationship between humans and technology. Seeking works investigating social, environmental, physical, cognitive, and emotional transformations brought by digital innovation. Group exhibition in Rome, November 2026.
calls.summary: Exploring humans and technology — social, environmental, and emotional transformations. Exhibition in Rome.

calls.title: Residency Program 2026
calls.description: One residency for artists working in photography or photo-based media at Herron School of Art + Design. Two-week intensive work period (August 10–21, 2026, fixed dates). $1,000 stipend plus up to $500 travel reimbursement. Includes darkroom facility, studios, and basic chemistry. Housing on CAMi campus for out-of-town residents. Resident must give a talk during or after the residency. Previous Aurora exhibitors (2025–2026) ineligible.
calls.summary: Two-week residency for photo-based media at Herron School of Art + Design. $1,000 stipend. Darkroom facilities included.
prose: Aurora PhotoCenter is an Indianapolis photography organization that runs an annual residency in collaboration with Herron School of Art + Design. The 2026 program selects one artist working in photography or photo-based media for a two-week intensive residency.

The residency dates are fixed: August 10–21, 2026. The resident receives a $1,000 stipend plus up to $500 travel reimbursement, and access to darkroom facility, studios, and basic chemistry. Housing is provided on the CAMi campus for out-of-town residents.
There's a public component: the resident must give a talk during or after the residency.

Eligibility is open, with one exclusion: previous Aurora exhibitors (2025–2026) are not eligible. Submission is through Slideroom with a portfolio and application. Fee is $10. The 2026 deadline was March 31; results announced May 1, 2026.

calls.title: People 2026
calls.description: International photography call exploring the human figure across all approaches including portraits, documentary, street photography, and studio work. Diverse interpretations welcome whether posed or unposed, observed or imagined. Selected work displayed in online exhibition.
calls.summary: Exploring the human figure across all approaches — portraits, documentary, street, and studio. Online exhibition.
prose: Grid Photo Gallery is an online gallery that runs themed photography calls on a recurring schedule. People is the gallery's call for work engaging with the human figure across all photographic approaches.

The brief is open in approach: portraits, documentary, street photography, and studio work all eligible. Diverse interpretations welcome — posed or unposed, observed or imagined. The unifying thread is the human as subject.
Selected work is shown in an online exhibition on the Grid Photo Gallery site.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through the gallery's website with unlimited images (fee per image). Fee is €7 per image. The 2026 deadline was March 31; results announced May 1, 2026.

calls.title: Nature 2026
calls.description: Exhibition exploring how we interact with nature. Seeking images that reveal beauty, power, cruelty, and influence on daily life. Selected work displayed in Glasgow gallery, online gallery, and exhibition catalogue. Exhibition runs July 3-31, 2026.
calls.summary: Exploring how we interact with nature — beauty, power, cruelty, and influence on daily life. Glasgow gallery exhibition.
prose: The Glasgow Gallery of Photography runs themed international juried exhibitions on a recurring schedule. Nature 2026 is the gallery's call for work engaging with how we interact with nature — including beauty, power, cruelty, and nature's influence on daily life. The framing is broader than landscape or wildlife; it's the human-nature relationship.

The gallery's fee structure is unusual: free to submit, with a £48 fee charged only if work is accepted for exhibition. Selected work is shown both in a physical exhibition in Glasgow and in an online gallery, with an accompanying exhibition catalogue.
The exhibition runs July 3–31, 2026.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is by email via file transfer with 1–8 images. The 2026 deadline was March 27; results announced April 1, 2026.

calls.title: Future Days 2026
calls.description: Open theme exhibition asking photographers to represent their vision of the future, whether hopeful or fearful. Interpret the theme at a global, local, or personal level. Selected work displayed in Glasgow gallery, online gallery, and exhibition catalogue. Exhibition runs July 3-31, 2026.
calls.summary: Open theme asking photographers to represent their vision of the future, hopeful or fearful. Glasgow gallery exhibition.
prose: Future Days 2026 is one of the Glasgow Gallery of Photography's recurring themed exhibitions. The brief asks photographers to represent their vision of the future — open in tone (hopeful or fearful, utopian or dystopian) and open in scale (global, local, or personal interpretation).
The gallery's fee structure is staged: free to submit, with a £48 fee charged only if work is accepted for exhibition.
Selected work is shown both in a physical exhibition at the Glasgow gallery and in an online gallery, with an accompanying exhibition catalogue. The exhibition runs July 3–31, 2026.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is by email via file transfer with 1–8 images. The 2026 deadline was March 27; results announced April 1, 2026.

calls.title: Artist in Residence Program 2026
calls.description: Four-week residency for artists advancing contemporary photography. Two artists selected: one slot for a Philadelphia-based artist, one open to all. Includes $3,000 honorarium, waived printer/scanner fees, $1,000 ink and paper credit, and $1,500 travel/housing reimbursement. Residencies run June through November 2026.
calls.summary: Four-week residency advancing contemporary photography. $3,000 honorarium plus ink/paper credit and travel support.
prose: TILT Institute (formerly Project Basho) is a Philadelphia photography institution. The Artist in Residence Program offers four-week residencies for artists advancing contemporary photography. Two artists are selected per cycle: one slot reserved for a Philadelphia-based artist and one open to all.

The residency package is materially substantial: $3,000 honorarium, waived printer and scanner fees during the residency, $1,000 ink and paper credit, and $1,500 travel/housing reimbursement. Residencies run between June and November 2026.
Eligibility is open globally for the open slot; geographically restricted for the Philadelphia slot.
Submission is through Submittable with up to 10 images. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was March 29; results announced April 24, 2026.

calls.title: Outside the Box: Cameraless Photography
calls.description: Exhibition seeking photographic works incorporating cameraless techniques including photograms, chemigrams, lumen prints, chlorophyll prints, phytograms, anthotypes, cyanotypes, and composites blending camera and non-camera methods. 30–40 pieces selected for gallery exhibition (May 30 – July 11, 2026) and website display. Juror's Award $200, Director's Award $150, Honorable Mentions receive catalogue.
jury: Dale Rio, Photographic Artist & Co-founder The Halide Project, MFA Pratt Institute
calls.summary: Photograms, chemigrams, lumen prints, cyanotypes, and composites blending camera and non-camera methods.
prose: PhotoSynthesis is an East Hartford, Connecticut photography organization. Outside the Box: Cameraless Photography is the gallery's call for work made without a camera — photograms, chemigrams, lumen prints, chlorophyll prints, phytograms, anthotypes, cyanotypes, and composites that blend camera and non-camera methods.
The brief is process-restricted by design: at least one cameraless technique must be involved. AI-generated work is not accepted.

Selection structure: 30–40 pieces are selected for both gallery exhibition (May 30 – July 11, 2026) and website display. Cash awards: Juror's Award $200, Director's Award $150. Honorable mentions receive the printed catalogue.
Selection is by Dale Rio, photographic artist and co-founder of The Halide Project, MFA from Pratt Institute.
Eligibility is open to alternative-process work globally. Submission is through EntryThingy with 1–5 images. Fee is $30. The 2026 deadline was March 31; results announced April 13, 2026.

calls.title: X ROID Bonn 2026
calls.description: 7th edition of the international instant art expo dedicated to Polaroid and Fuji Instax photography. Three-day juried exhibition (May 29–31, 2026) at The Stage Gallery in Bonn featuring artist talks, a Pola walk, and creative exchanges. Only original instant photographs accepted — no prints. Accepted formats: SX70, 600, Spectra, 4×5, Packfilm, Polaroid Original, Impossible Project, Fuji Instax (all sizes). Fee includes professional framing. Gallery takes 25% commission on sales. Artwork uninsured during exhibition. In media partnership with Analog Forever.
calls.requirements: Up to 4 Polaroids or 2 large format
calls.summary: 7th edition of the international instant art expo for Polaroid and Fuji Instax. Three-day exhibition in Bonn.
prose: X ROID Bonn is the international instant art expo organized by The Stage Gallery in Bonn, Germany. The expo is dedicated to instant photography — Polaroid and Fuji Instax. The 2026 edition is the 7th cycle.

The 2026 expo runs three days (May 29–31) at The Stage Gallery, structured as a juried exhibition with artist talks, a Pola walk through the city, and creative exchanges between participants. Media partnership with Analog Forever (the analog photography magazine).

The selection is process-restricted: only original instant photographs accepted — no prints. Accepted formats are SX70, 600, Spectra, 4×5, Packfilm, Polaroid Original, Impossible Project, and Fuji Instax in all sizes.
Practical terms: the €225 fee includes professional framing. Gallery takes 25% commission on sales. Artwork is uninsured during the exhibition.
Eligibility is open globally to instant photography. Submission is by email with up to 4 Polaroids or 2 large-format works. The 2026 deadline was March 31.

calls.title: Defiance Zine Open Call
calls.description: Open call for Revoke Collective's first zine on the theme of Defiance. Looking for photographs that challenge, disrupt, or simply refuse. Defiance can take many forms: quiet resistance, bold rebellion, personal freedom, cultural pushback, or moments of quiet nonconformity. Not chasing polish — chasing pulse. Raw vision and unfiltered moments.
calls.summary: Revoke Collective's first zine on the theme of Defiance. Photographs that challenge, disrupt, or simply refuse.
prose: Revoke Collective is an emerging indie photography collective. The Defiance Zine is the collective's first publication, themed around defiance — work that challenges, disrupts, or simply refuses.

The brief reads defiance broadly: quiet resistance, bold rebellion, personal freedom, cultural pushback, or moments of quiet nonconformity. The editorial register favors raw and unpolished work — the brief states the collective is not chasing polish, it's chasing pulse.
Selection results in inclusion in the first Revoke Zine.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is by Google Form with up to 3 images. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was April 6; selections communicated mid-April 2026.

calls.title: Les Mots du Phare Vol. 04: Futur(s)
calls.description: Open call for black-and-white photography for Vol. 04 of Les Mots du Phare, a print publication by Linea Recta Books and Le Phare Collectif. Theme: Futur(s) — imagining what seems impossible, a tomorrow, an after, a continuation. Not the end of the world, but the courage to imagine what is possible. Selected images will be featured in the printed edition alongside text contributions from members of the collective. Submit up to 4 B&W photos combined into one PDF via email.
calls.summary: Black-and-white photography for a print publication. Theme: imagining what seems impossible, a tomorrow.
prose: Les Mots du Phare is a recurring print publication produced by Linea Recta Books and Le Phare Collectif, a Paris-based collective working at the intersection of photography and writing. The 2026 edition is Vol. 04, themed Futur(s) — futures, plural.

The brief frames the theme as imagining what seems impossible: a tomorrow, an after, a continuation. The editorial position is explicit — not the end of the world, but the courage to imagine what is possible. The plural form (Futur(s)) leaves room for multiple, conflicting, or ambivalent readings.

The publication is process-restricted: black-and-white photography only. Selected images are featured in the printed edition alongside text contributions from members of the Phare Collectif — the publication intercuts visual and literary work rather than running them in separate sections.
Each application is up to 4 black-and-white photographs combined into one PDF, submitted by email. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was April 26.

calls.title: I Can Buy Myself Flowers
calls.description: HAZEGALLERY, the curatorial platform of PURPLEHAZE Magazine, invites artists and image-makers to participate in a curated pop-up exhibition in Amsterdam alongside the launch of PURPLEHAZE Print Issue 012. Theme explores autonomy as identity, rituals of independence, intimacy turned inward, beauty chosen rather than granted, solitude as clarity, and desire as self-directed. Accepts fashion, fine art, and documentary photography, works on paper, fine art prints, and short looping video works. Selected artists participate in the June 2026 Amsterdam exhibition and may be published in the print issue.
jury: Irina Rusinovich, Founder & Curator, HAZE Gallery
calls.summary: Pop-up exhibition in Amsterdam exploring autonomy, intimacy turned inward, and self-directed desire. With PURPLEHAZE.
prose: HAZE Gallery is the curatorial platform of PURPLEHAZE Magazine. The 2026 open call I Can Buy Myself Flowers is a pop-up exhibition in Amsterdam timed to the launch of PURPLEHAZE Print Issue 012.

The brief works through related themes: autonomy as identity, rituals of independence, intimacy turned inward, beauty chosen rather than granted, solitude as clarity, and desire as self-directed. The framing is feminist-adjacent without being narrowly gender-restricted in eligibility — the brief asks for work that engages with self-direction and inwardness.
Accepted work spans fashion, fine art, and documentary photography, plus works on paper, fine art prints, and short looping video — multidisciplinary by design.
Selection is by Irina Rusinovich, founder and curator of HAZE Gallery. Selected artists participate in the June 2026 Amsterdam pop-up exhibition and may be published in the print issue.
Submission is through the gallery's website with 3–5 images. Fee is €35. Eligibility is open globally. The 2026 deadline was April 16; results announced June 2026.

calls.title: Fresh Legs 2026
