prose: FiiLTHY GLO is an independent zine for work in the strange and unusual register, drawing from across visual art and writing. Issue 5 is themed "SONDER" — the constructed word for the realization that every passerby is living a life as vivid and complex as one's own. The brief asks for work that engages with the layered, sparsely noticed connections that intertwine people across society.

Submissions are interdisciplinary: photography is accepted alongside painting, collage, mixed media, digital art, sculpture, comic strips, prose, opinion writing, and short stories. Each artist may submit 1 to 5 original works. Visual works should be cleanly presented — well-lit, minimal background clutter. Writing is capped at 900 words per piece, submitted as PDF.

Filenames follow the format ArtistName_Title_Year. Submissions are made via a Google Form linked on the FiiLTHY GLO submissions page. There is no submission fee, and AI-generated work is not accepted. Eligibility requires applicants to be 18 years or older and to submit original work only.

The Issue 5 deadline is June 20, 2026. The zine does not publicly specify what selected contributors receive — applicants should email the zine directly to confirm contributor copies, payment, and other compensation details before submitting.

calls.title: Stanley Greene Foundation Emerging Photographers Grant 2026–2027
calls.description: Annual grant from the Stanley Greene Foundation providing a $10,000 award to emerging visual storytellers at the beginning of their careers to develop impactful visual narratives. The program places particular emphasis on photographers from underserved and diverse communities, expanding access to resources and opportunities to bring their stories to life. Award disbursed in two parts: $8,000 upon award and $2,000 upon submission of final materials. Application requires biography (max 1,500 characters), project description (max 2,000 characters), project proposal (max 3,000 characters), and up to 25 images (72 dpi JPG, minimum 1,500 pixels long dimension, sRGB). Submissions reviewed by three Foundation board members in two rounds. Recipients must provide 15 final digital images and a report detailing fund usage; these materials become part of the Foundation's collection. Open to applicants 18+; current students not eligible (graduating before announcement may apply). Honoring the legacy of war photographer and Noor Images co-founder Stanley Greene.
calls.summary: $10,000 grant for emerging visual storytellers, with emphasis on underserved and diverse communities. Honors Stanley Greene's legacy.
prose: The Stanley Greene Foundation Emerging Photographers Grant honors war photographer Stanley Greene, a co-founder of Noor Images who covered conflict zones from Chechnya through West Africa. The Foundation administers the grant in his name, with explicit emphasis on supporting visual storytellers from underserved and diverse communities at the beginning of their careers.

The grant is $10,000, paid in two installments: $8,000 upon award and $2,000 upon completion of the project, contingent on submission of 15 final digital images and a written report detailing how the funds were used. The completion materials become part of the Foundation's archive. The two-stage payment is designed to ensure projects are actually carried through.

Eligibility requires applicants to be 18 or older and not currently enrolled as students at the time of submission, though those graduating before the decision date may apply. One proposal per person; collaborators are accepted. AI-generated imagery is not permitted in the work samples.

Applications are made through Picter and require a biography (up to 1,500 characters), project description (up to 2,000 characters), project proposal (up to 3,000 characters), and up to 25 images at 72 dpi JPG, sRGB, minimum 1,500 pixels on the long dimension. Selection is by a three-member jury drawn from the Stanley Greene Foundation Board, which meets twice — first for finalists, then for the final decision. Applications open May 1, 2026 and close July 1, 2026 at 11:59 PM EDT. Winners announced August 10, 2026.

calls.title: Quinn Emanuel Los Angeles Artist-in-Residence 2026
calls.description: Four-month studio residency at Quinn Emanuel's Los Angeles office for emerging and mid-career artists working in any discipline, including photography. The selected artist receives $5,000 per month for four months ($20,000 total) plus an art materials allowance of up to $1,500. The residency runs September–December 2026, followed by a one-month exhibition. The studio is located within the Quinn Emanuel LA office with 24/7 keycard access, parking, and full firm support. At least one work from the residency will be incorporated into the firm's permanent collection. Open to artists living in greater Los Angeles only; international applicants accepted if they secure their own visas. Preference given to underrepresented artists in early/mid-career stages. Submit a CV, an 8–10 image PDF portfolio, and a project proposal (one PDF, max 20MB) by 11:59pm PST May 14, 2026.
calls.summary: $20,000 + $1,500 materials. 4-month studio residency at Quinn Emanuel LA office. Open to all media including photography. Greater LA only.
jury: John Quinn, Founding Partner, Quinn Emanuel
prose: Quinn Emanuel is a major U.S. litigation law firm with 32 international offices. The Quinn Emanuel Artist-in-Residence program is run by the firm's Los Angeles office, with selection committee appointed by curator Alexis Hyde and firm name partner John Quinn — making this an unusually large and well-funded artist residency hosted by a corporate entity rather than an arts organization.

The 2026 residency is four months long, running September through December 2026, followed by a one-month exhibition. Each artist receives $5,000 per month for four months ($20,000 total cash) plus an art materials allowance of up to $1,500. The studio is located within the firm's LA office with 24/7 keycard access, parking included, and full firm support during the residency.

At least one work from the residency is incorporated into the firm's permanent collection. The structure is unusual: the firm's collection becomes the long-term home for residency-produced work, with sales opportunities also available through the post-residency exhibition.

Eligibility is restricted to artists living in greater Los Angeles. International artists are welcome but must secure their own visas. Preference is given to underrepresented artists in early-to-mid career stages, working in any discipline (photography, painting, sculpture, video, mixed media). No formal education requirement.
Application is free. Submissions consist of a CV, an 8–10 image PDF portfolio, and a project proposal — combined as a single PDF up to 20MB. The 2026 deadline is May 14 at 11:59 PM PST.

calls.title: Fundación Botín Art Grants 2026/2027
calls.description: Six annual visual arts grants of €23,000 each to support a research project or training in the visual arts. Photography is explicitly included alongside drawing, film/video/new media, mixed-media, painting, sculpture, and craft. Grants run for nine months and cover living expenses, travel, accommodation, studio rental, equipment, and production costs, plus medical insurance for recipients travelling outside their country of residence. One grant prioritizes Spanish artists or Spain residents (5+ years) under age 30 relocating abroad. Applications open to individual artists of any nationality; project must involve practical artistic work, not theoretical study. Online registration is followed by postal submission of up to 40 single-sided A4 pages including ID, CV (3 pages max), project description (10 pages max), and graphic documentation. Applications must be postmarked by Friday, May 8, 2026 (received until May 22 if postmarked by deadline). Results announced before July 17, 2026. Public exhibition at Centro Botín; possible acquisitions for the Foundation's Collection.
calls.summary: Six €23,000 nine-month research grants for international visual artists, photography included. Postal application postmarked by May 8.
prose: Fundación Botín was established in 1964 by Marcelino Botín Sanz de Sautuola and Carmen Yllera. The Visual Arts Grant program has run since 1993 and has supported more than 200 artists. Many former grantees are now internationally established.

The 2026/2027 edition awards six grants of €23,000 each. Funds cover living expenses, travel, equipment, studio rental, and production costs. Medical insurance is included for grantees who need to relocate internationally for the project. Payment runs in tranches: 45% upfront, 25% after the first trimester, 25% after the second, 5% on final report submission. The grant period is nine months.

Eligibility is open to artists of any nationality. One of the six grants is reserved for Spanish citizens or Spain residents (5+ years) under age 30 who are relocating abroad for their project. Projects must involve artistic creation and production, not theoretical research.

What's offered beyond the funding: public exhibition of resulting work at Centro Botín in Santander as part of Itinerarios — the program's annual exhibition, now in its 27th edition. Works may be acquired by Fundación Botín's Art Advisory Committee. Centro Botín retains first-show rights — works exhibit there before any other public presentation. Career tracking and ongoing support continues post-grant.

Applications combine an online registration form and a printed dossier sent by postal mail: ID copy, CV (max 3 pages), project title and 100-word summary, full project description (max 10 pages), graphic documentation on single-sided A4 color prints. Final report due November 12, 2027.
The 2026/2027 deadline is May 8, 2026 (postmark date); physical receipt accepted through May 22 if postmarked by May 8. Results announced before July 17, 2026.

calls.title: 24th DongGang International Photo Festival 2026 Open Call
calls.description: Open call for the 24th DongGang International Photo Festival, held July 17 – October 11, 2026 in Yeongwol, South Korea. Theme: 'The Silence that Shapes' — exploring how humans interpret nature and what we project onto landscapes versus what nature actually reveals. 15–20 artists are selected by the festival's curatorial team, including one 'Artist of the Year' who receives a solo exhibition with production support and travel/accommodation to attend the opening. Other selected artists receive outdoor exhibition space, production assistance, and inclusion in the festival catalog and press. Open to individual artists and collectives worldwide. Submit 8–12 images (JPEG or TIFF, minimum 4000 px on long side) plus CV and an artist statement under 400 words by email or WeTransfer. Notification by June 10, 2026.
calls.summary: 24th DIPF Yeongwol, South Korea. Theme: The Silence that Shapes. 15–20 artists selected. Artist of the Year solo show + travel.
prose: The DongGang International Photo Festival (DIPF) is held annually in Yeongwol, a town in South Korea's Gangwon Special Self-Governing Province along the DongGang River. The 2026 edition is the festival's 24th — DIPF is among the longer-running photography festivals in East Asia.

The 2026 dates run July 17 through October 11. The theme is "The Silence that Shapes" — the brief asks how humans interpret nature and what meaning we project onto landscapes versus the inherent silence of natural spaces. The framing favors work that engages with landscape, environment, and human perception rather than purely portrait or documentary.

Fifteen to twenty artists or collectives are selected from the open call. One is named "Artist of the Year" and receives a solo exhibition with production support, plus travel and accommodation funded by the festival. Other selected artists are exhibited in the main, outdoor, or screening venues with all production and printing handled by the organizers, plus inclusion in the festival catalog, website, and ongoing press coverage.

There is no entry fee. Eligibility is open globally to artists and collectives. Submissions are 8 to 12 photographs in JPEG or TIFF format at minimum 4,000 pixels on the long side, plus CV/biography, an artist statement under 400 characters, and contact information. Selection is by the festival's curatorial team. The 2026 deadline is June 1; results announced by June 10.

calls.title: Inner Landscapes
calls.description: Open call for Mental Health Awareness Month inviting lens-based artists to reflect on mental health and its relationship to everyday life. Considers how internal experiences are shaped by social, cultural, and environmental conditions and expressed through image-making. Welcomes work engaging with care, fatigue, stability, imbalance, support systems, and personal coping strategies. Selected works featured in a one-month online exhibition on Der Greif's homepage (May 15 – June 15, 2026), plus participation in small-group online critique sessions through Der Greif's Face-to-Face program. Selected artists may also be invited to submit their portfolio to Der Greif Studio. Voluntary €5 or €10 donation; financial assistance available on request.
calls.summary: Mental health theme. One-month online exhibition at Der Greif + roundtable critique session with peers. Voluntary fee, vouchers available.
prose: Inner Landscapes is a thematic open call from Der Greif, the Augsburg-based photography platform and print magazine, programmed for Mental Health Awareness Month. The theme asks lens-based artists to reflect on mental health and its relationship to everyday life — how internal experiences are shaped by social, cultural, and environmental conditions and how those experiences are expressed through image-making.

Concrete subjects encouraged: care, fatigue, stability, imbalance, support systems, personal coping strategies. Selection criteria favor artistic quality, conceptual clarity, openness to dialogue, and engagement with identity and community.

Selected works are featured in a one-month online exhibition on Der Greif's homepage running May 15 – June 15, 2026. Selected artists also participate in small-group online critique sessions through Der Greif's Face-to-Face program — peers plus Der Greif facilitators rather than a one-way jury verdict. Selection may also lead to an invitation to submit a portfolio to Der Greif Studio for sales and commission opportunities.

Eligibility is open globally with no experience-level restriction. Submissions are made through Picter, up to 10 images. The fee is voluntary — €5 or €10 suggested. Financial assistance is available on request: applicants in financial hardship can email voucher-special-2@dergreif.org for a 50–100% discount code.
The 2026 deadline is May 10.

calls.title: Drone Photo Awards 2026
calls.description: International aerial photography contest run by Siena Awards (sister event to Siena International Photo Awards). Nine categories: seven single-shot themes (Wedding, Nature, People, Urban, Animals, Abstract, Sport), Videos, and Series (5–9 images). Drone Photographer of the Year receives the Pangea Prize crystal trophy, €500 worth of photography equipment, and €400 toward Siena travel for the Awards Ceremony weekend. Selected work shown in the "Above Us Only Sky" group exhibition. Awards ceremony at Teatro dei Rinnovati on October 10, 2026 during the Siena Awards Festival.
calls.summary: Aerial photography contest. 9 categories, free entry. €500 gear + Pangea trophy + Siena exhibition. Ceremony Oct 10.
prose: The Drone Photo Awards is an annual international aerial photography contest run by Siena Awards, the umbrella organization that also runs the Siena International Photo Awards (SIPA) and Creative Photo Awards. The contest is held alongside the wider Siena Awards Festival in Siena, Italy.

Submissions are accepted across nine categories. Seven cover single-shot themes: Wedding, Nature, People, Urban, Animals, Abstract, and Sport. Two additional categories are Videos and Series (5 to 9 images). All categories require aerial-perspective work — drone, aircraft, or other non-ground vantage. AI-generated images are not accepted.

The overall Drone Photographer of the Year receives the Pangea Prize crystal trophy, €500 worth of photography equipment, and €400 toward travel to the Siena Awards Ceremony weekend. Selected work from across categories is exhibited in the "Above Us Only Sky" group exhibition at the festival, with the awards ceremony held at the historic Teatro dei Rinnovati on October 10, 2026.
Entry is free of charge. Eligibility is open globally. Submissions go through Siena Awards' contest portal at sienawards.com. The 2026 deadline is June 7.

calls.title: F/262 Photography Awards 2026
calls.description: Single-image international photography awards from the inaugural F/262 Festival in Caldas da Rainha, Portugal (a UNESCO Creative City). Four award tracks: F/262 Photography Award (Gold/Silver/Bronze), ZÉ Creative Award, NextGen Award (emerging photographers), and the Thematic Award 'Moldar as Margens / Shaping Shores' tied to the festival's 2026 Water focus. Selected work is exhibited as outdoor public installations across the city during the festival (May 16 – September 13, 2026) and featured in the festival programme, press, and digital platforms. Gold winner receives a solo exhibition at F/262 2028, plus a €500 KOYLAB print voucher, BlackRapid Sport X strap, Outex Camera Pro Kit, and a 1-year SmartAlbums bundle. Silver and Bronze receive €400 and €300 vouchers respectively plus gear and software. Open globally; original work only; images must not have previously received a major international award.
jury: António Pedrosa, Documentary Photographer & Hasselblad Master
Ami Vitale, National Geographic Explorer & Nikon Ambassador
Daria Bonera, Founder & Director, DB Agency
Jacqueline Tobin, Author & Former Editor-in-Chief, Rangefinder
Carine Van Gerven, Founder, Lens op de Mens Festival
Matthew Jordan Smith, Nikon & KoyLab Ambassador
Martin Krystýnek, President, Slovak Association of Professional Photographers
calls.summary: Single-image awards from the inaugural F/262 Festival in Caldas da Rainha, Portugal. Public outdoor installations + 2028 solo show.
prose: F/262 is the inaugural international photography festival of Caldas da Rainha, a UNESCO Creative City in Portugal — the festival's name combines the photographic 'F' (Focus, F-Stop, Family, Fun, Friendship, Freedom) with the city's area code, 262. The 2026 edition runs May 16 – September 13, with the year's curatorial focus on Water as ecological, cultural, and symbolic element. The festival is produced by Associação F/SOS – Fotografia, Solidariedade e Obras Sociais.

The Photography Awards run as a single-image competition across four parallel tracks. The main F/262 Photography Award gives Gold, Silver, and Bronze. The ZÉ Award is a Creative Award for unconventional approaches. The NextGen Award is reserved for emerging photographers. The Thematic Award 'Moldar as Margens / Shaping Shores' ties to the 2026 Water focus.

Selected work is shown as outdoor public installations across Caldas da Rainha during the festival run, with each selected photographer receiving a 50×70 cm fine-art print on Fuji paper, festival programme inclusion, and press/digital visibility. Gold takes a 2028 solo exhibition plus a €500 KOYLAB voucher, BlackRapid Sport X, Outex Camera Pro Kit, and 1-year SmartAlbums bundle. Silver and Bronze receive €400 and €300 vouchers respectively plus gear and software. Other category winners receive €250 vouchers and accessories.

Selection is by an independent international jury of photographers, editors, curators, and cultural leaders, including National Geographic and Pulitzer-winning practitioners. Judging is blind, on narrative strength, visual impact, originality, technical/conceptual coherence, and contemporary relevance.

Submission is through the festival website. Entry fee is €15 per image with no quantity limit; series are not accepted (each image is judged separately). Eligibility is open worldwide with no nationality, age, theme, or equipment restrictions; original work only, and images must not have previously received a major international award. The 2026 deadline is May 31; finalists are announced July 18.

calls.title: F/262 Photo Book Award 2026
calls.description: Annual photobook award from F/262 Festival in Caldas da Rainha, Portugal. Honors the best unpublished photobook project — 'from image to object, from story to print.' One author receives full local production of a 262-copy hand-numbered limited edition in Portugal, in collaboration with publishing partners and local craftspeople. Includes editorial and materials support, ISBN and colophon, launch event at the F/262 Photo Book Club, and international visibility through the festival programme. Open internationally; projects must be unpublished (self-published works of 100 copies or fewer are eligible). Collectives permitted; no entry limit per author (separate fees apply per project). Finalist dummy delivery due August 5, 2026 after July 1 application deadline.
jury: Jacqueline Tobin, Author & Former Editor-in-Chief, Rangefinder
Yegan Mazandarani & William Keo, Four Eyes Editions
Rúben R. Dias, Editorial Designer & Educator
calls.summary: Photobook award from F/262 Festival, Portugal. Winner gets full local production of a 262-copy hand-numbered limited edition.
prose: F/262 is the inaugural international photography festival of Caldas da Rainha, a UNESCO Creative City in Portugal. The Photo Book Award is the festival's dedicated photobook track — a sister program to its photography awards, run during the festival's 2026 edition (May 16 – September 13). The festival's curatorial focus for 2026 is Water as ecological, cultural, and symbolic element.

The award honors the best unpublished photobook project of the year. Eligibility is broad: collectives are permitted, and self-published works with print runs of 100 copies or fewer are still considered unpublished for the purposes of the award. There is no per-author entry limit; multiple projects may be submitted with separate fees.

The winner receives full local production of a 262-copy hand-numbered limited edition produced in Portugal, in collaboration with publishing partners and local craftspeople. The prize includes editorial and materials support, ISBN and colophon, a launch event at the F/262 Photo Book Club, and international visibility through the festival programme. The structure prioritizes book-making craft and local production over a cash prize.

Selection is by an independent jury including Jacqueline Tobin (former editor-in-chief, Rangefinder Magazine), Yegan Mazandarani and William Keo of Four Eyes Editions, designer/educator Rúben R. Dias, and designer João Agostinho. Judging considers narrative strength, editing/sequence/design, production feasibility, and sustainability/innovation.

Submission is through the festival website. Entry fee is €35 per project (non-refundable). The 2026 application deadline is July 1, with shortlisted finalists invited to deliver physical dummies by August 5.

calls.title: Circulation(s) Festival 2027 — 17th Edition Open Call
calls.description: Annual open call for the festival of young European photography, held at CENTQUATRE-Paris and on tour across France and Europe. Now in its 17th edition (Spring 2027). Open to photographers of European nationality and/or resident in Europe at the start of their careers, with no age or training requirements. No theme — selection prioritizes aesthetic quality and artistic relevance. All forms of photographic writing welcome, including projects mixing formats or incorporating video, installation, or sound. Group projects accepted. Approximately 15 photographers selected for festival exhibition. AI-generated images must be disclosed. Selection by the Fetart collective (independent female curators specializing in emerging photography).
calls.summary: Major European festival of young photography at CENTQUATRE-Paris. Free until May 24, then €20. ~15 photographers selected for spring 2027.
jury: Fetart collective — independent female curators specializing in emerging photography
prose: Circulation(s) is one of Europe's longest-running festivals dedicated to emerging photography, organized by the Fetart collective and held annually at CENTQUATRE-Paris in eastern Paris, with off-site programming and tours across France and Europe. The 2027 edition will be the festival's 17th, scheduled for spring 2027.

The open call is intentionally broad. There is no age limit, no training requirement, and no theme. All forms of photographic writing are welcome — including projects that mix formats or incorporate video, installation, or sound. Group projects are accepted. Selection prioritizes aesthetic quality and the relevance of the artistic purpose.

Eligibility is restricted to photographers of European nationality and/or resident in Europe, at the start of their careers, with no prior major exhibition in France. AI-generated imagery must be explicitly disclosed in the application.

Approximately 15 photographers are selected for the festival exhibition. Pre-selection happens in summer 2026; final selection in September 2026; results communicated mid-October; artist names announced in November 2026.

Application is through the festival's online portal via Picter. The early-bird window (April 28 – May 24, 2026) is free; the standard window (May 25 – June 7, 2026) costs €20. The deadline is June 7, 2026 at midnight.

calls.title: Color 2026
calls.description: International call exploring color as a central element of the image — as structure, signal, atmosphere, or disruption. Open to all photographic genres, methods, and subjects, provided color is integral to the image's internal logic. Selected work shown in curated online exhibition. First place receives Photographer of the Month feature with profile interview, priority promotional placement, and a free entry in the next open call. Second and third places highlighted in the virtual exhibition. All selected entries get permanent online display, social media promotion, digital certificate, and a profile page with website link. Selected works may also appear in a printed catalog.
calls.summary: Grid Photo Gallery's call exploring color as structure, signal, or atmosphere. Online exhibition. €7 per image, unlimited submissions.
prose: Grid Photo Gallery is an online gallery that runs themed photography calls on a recurring schedule. Color is the gallery's call for work where color functions as a central element of the image — as structure, signal, atmosphere, or disruption.

The brief is open in approach: any genre, method, or subject is eligible, provided color is integral to the image's internal logic rather than incidental. The call sits alongside the gallery's earlier People 2026 call.

Selected work is shown in a curated online exhibition on the Grid Photo Gallery site. First place is named Photographer of the Month and receives a profile interview, priority promotional placement, and a free entry in the next open call. Second and third places are highlighted in the virtual exhibition. All selected entries get permanent online display, social media promotion, a digital certificate, and a profile page linking to the photographer's site. Selected works may also appear in a printed catalog.

Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through the gallery's website with unlimited images (fee per image). Fee is €7 per image, non-refundable. The 2026 deadline is June 15; the exhibition opens July 1, 2026.

calls.title: Future Photobook Award 2026
calls.org: Coventry University MA Photography & Fast Forward
calls.description: Inaugural award for a photobook or photo-based publication (zine, handmade artist book, printed essay, etc.) by anyone over 18 currently studying at or recently graduated from a Higher Education institution. Winner receives personalised portfolio reviews with each judge plus an exhibition at a Coventry venue. All entrants receive feedback from industry professionals.
calls.summary: Inaugural photobook award for HE students and recent grads. Open to any format including zines and handmade books. Free entry.
prose: The Future Photobook Award is a new prize launched by the MA Photography programme at Coventry University in partnership with Fast Forward, the international research and advocacy network for women in photography based at the University for the Creative Arts (UCA).

The award is intentionally inclusive on format. Submissions can be a finished photobook, a zine, a handmade artist's book, a printed essay, or any photo-based publication — the brief does not prescribe a binding, length, or production method. The intent is to recognise the photobook in its widest sense, including DIY and small-edition forms that often fall outside the criteria of larger photobook prizes.

Eligibility is open to anyone over 18 who is currently studying at, or has recently graduated from, a Higher Education institution. There is no fee. Entry is by post — physical books are submitted to the award via the link in the brief. All entrants receive written feedback from industry professionals. The winner receives personalised portfolio reviews with each of the judges, and the winning publication is shown in an exhibition at a Coventry venue.
The inaugural deadline is August 7, 2026.

calls.title: Photoworks Artist Venturing Labs — EASE: Crete 2026–2027
calls.description: Open call for a UK-based artist to join an art–science fieldwork lab in Crete in autumn 2026, exploring climate, landscape, and deep time alongside scientific teams. £1,000 stipend for the week on site; travel, accommodation, and meals fully covered. 24-month online engagement with EASE partners and Photoworks platform features.
jury: Mark Kasumovic, Artist & Academic, De Montfort University
calls.summary: UK-based artist joins art–science fieldwork lab in Crete. £1,000 stipend, all expenses covered. Climate, landscape, deep time.
prose: Photoworks is the UK's national photography commissioning agency, based in Brighton. Artist Venturing Labs is a programme produced with EASE (Entrepreneurship, Art & Science for Environmental Sustainability), an interdisciplinary research initiative funded by UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) in collaboration with Nottingham Trent University, De Montfort University, and PicturingClimate.org.

The 2026–2027 lab takes place in Crete, with fieldwork across diverse Cretan locations exploring climate, landscape, and deep time alongside the scientific teams resident on the island. The selected artist commits to one week on site (autumn 2026) plus 24 months of online engagement with the EASE network. No academic background, entrepreneurship experience, or prior interdisciplinary practice is required — Photoworks explicitly invites applicants without an EASE-style track record.

The selected artist receives a £1,000 stipend for the week on site. All travel, accommodation, and meals are covered. The artist gets access to scientific teams, fellow artists in the EASE cohort, and Photoworks' venture-building support, with potential features on Photoworks' digital and editorial platforms.

Eligibility is restricted to UK-based artists, per the UKRI funding requirement. Application is via online form with either a 5-page PDF (expression of interest, bio, project examples, available lab dates) or a 3-minute audio or video recording. The deadline is June 29, 2026 at 23:59 BST.

calls.title: Portal: At the Edge of Becoming
calls.description: Photographs that hold the viewer at the edge of something — work where a shift is imminent but not yet complete. Online curated exhibition with catalog inclusion and Instagram feature. First place receives $500 plus a solo webpage exhibition; second $300; third $200. Open worldwide, all photographic styles and processes welcome.
calls.summary: Online photography exhibition on tension and threshold. Juror Douglas Stockdale. $1,000 total + solo webpage.
prose: Decagon Gallery is an online curatorial platform that runs themed photography exhibitions with published catalogs and social distribution. "Portal: At the Edge of Becoming" is the gallery's call for photographs that hold a viewer at the edge of something — where a shift is imminent but not yet complete. The brief asks for work that embodies tension and resists easy resolution, functioning as a threshold rather than a literal representation.

The selection structure is online-first. Selected photographers are featured in a curated online exhibition with a published catalog distributed through Decagon's mailing list and social channels. All accepted artists receive an exhibition page, an Instagram feature, and catalog inclusion. The first-place winner additionally receives a solo webpage exhibition on the gallery site.

Cash awards: $500 first place, $300 second, $200 third. The 2026 cycle is juried by Douglas Stockdale — visual artist, editor, photobook publisher, and founder of PhotoBook Journal. Eligibility is open worldwide; all photographic styles and processes are welcome.
Entry fee is $25 per submission of up to 8 images (JPG, 2100 pixels on long side, no watermarks or borders). The 2026 deadline is June 3, with the exhibition running June 20 through August 20, 2026.

calls.title: A Celebration of Contemporary Photography
calls.description: Open call celebrating the creativity, diversity, and evolving practice of photography today. Aligned with World Photography Day. Up to 35 images selected for the physical Middlebury, Vermont gallery and 40 for the online gallery, with all selected work appearing in the exhibition catalog and remaining permanently on the website. Open worldwide, all subjects, styles, and processes welcome.
calls.summary: PhotoPlace's most inclusive call. World Photography Day exhibition in Middlebury, VT + online + catalog.
prose: PhotoPlace Gallery is a photography gallery in Middlebury, Vermont, that programs juried thematic exhibitions on a rolling schedule. "A Celebration of Contemporary Photography" is one of the gallery's most open and inclusive calls of the year — explicitly framed as a celebration of the creativity, diversity, and evolving practice of photography today.

The exhibition is timed to World Photography Day (August 19) and welcomes all photographic subjects, styles, and processes — from traditional landscape and portraiture to experimental and alternative approaches.

Selection structure is layered: up to 35 images are selected for the physical exhibition in the Middlebury gallery, and up to 40 for the online gallery. All selected work appears in the exhibition catalog, remains permanently on the PhotoPlace website, and receives social media promotion with photographer URL links.
Selection is by Paula Tognarelli (former director of the Griffin Museum of Photography) and Zach Hoffman (Gallery Owner/Director).

AI-generated work is not accepted. Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through the gallery's website. Fee is $39 for up to 5 images plus $6 per additional image. The 2026 deadline is June 8, with the exhibition running August 7 through August 29, 2026.

calls.title: America 250 — Photography Exhibition
calls.description: Ninth national juried photography exhibition celebrating the U.S. Semiquincentennial. Open to USA artists 18+. Photography defined as digital or film camera work, unaltered except minor enhancements. AI-generated work not accepted. $800 in awards: $300 best capture of theme, $200 best traditional, $200 best non-traditional, $100 Award of Merit. Exhibition June 19 – August 1, 2026 at Gallery One in Ellensburg, WA. Jurors: Gail Gibson and C. Meier (Blue Sky Oregon Center for Photographic Arts).
jury: C. Meier, Exhibitions Director, Blue Sky Oregon Center for Photographic Arts
calls.summary: National juried photography show on US 250th anniversary. $800 in awards. Gallery One in Ellensburg, WA.
prose: Gallery One Visual Arts Center is a nonprofit gallery at 408 N Pearl Street in downtown Ellensburg, Washington. The annual America 250 exhibition is the gallery's ninth national juried photography show, the 2026 edition timed for the United States Semiquincentennial — the 250th anniversary of American independence. The brief invites work that engages with the country at this milestone moment.

Photography is defined strictly: work created using a digital or film camera, unaltered except for slight enhancements to lighting, coloration, or contrast. AI-generated work is not accepted. The 2026 jurors are Gail Gibson, gallery director and curator, alongside C. Meier, Exhibitions Director at Blue Sky, the Oregon Center for the Photographic Arts in Portland.

Awards total $800 across four categories: $300 for best at capturing the exhibit theme, $200 for best traditional approach to photography, $200 for best non-traditional approach, and $100 Award of Merit. Selected work is shown at Gallery One from June 19 through August 1, 2026, with the artist receiving 60% commission on sales.

Eligibility is restricted to artists 18+ residing in the United States. Submission is through CallForEntry.org (CaFE). Fees are $20 for the first entry and $10 for each additional, with a maximum of 6 entries. The deadline is May 17, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST; acceptance notifications are sent May 27, 2026.

calls.title: Mrinalini Mukherjee Creative Arts Grant 2026
calls.description: Annual grant from the Mrinalini Mukherjee Foundation supporting innovative and experimental projects by established Indian artists. INR 10 lakhs (approximately USD 12,000) disbursed in two equal installments. Eligible disciplines span the visual arts including painting, sculpture, mural, textile, printmaking, performance art, and lens and media-based art. Open to Indian citizens currently residing in India with a minimum of 15 years of professional practice. Non-Resident Indians, Overseas Citizens of India, and Persons of Indian Origin are not eligible. Individual artists and collectives may both apply.
calls.summary: INR 10 lakhs (~USD 12,000) grant from the Mrinalini Mukherjee Foundation for established Indian artists including lens-based practitioners.
prose: The Mrinalini Mukherjee Foundation honours the legacy of sculptor Mrinalini Mukherjee (1949–2015), one of India's most significant artists, by supporting the work of contemporary Indian artists. The Creative Arts Grant is the foundation's flagship annual award, structured to fund a single ambitious project rather than supplement an existing practice.

The grant amount is INR 10 lakhs — roughly USD 12,000 — disbursed in two equal installments. Eligible disciplines span the visual arts broadly: painting, sculpture, mural, textile, printmaking, performance art, and lens and media-based art, including projects working at the intersection of these forms.

Eligibility is tightly defined. Applicants must be Indian citizens currently residing in India, with a minimum of fifteen years of professional practice after graduate or postgraduate study. Non-Resident Indians, Overseas Citizens of India, and Persons of Indian Origin are not eligible. Both individual artists and collectives may apply.

The brief emphasises innovation and experimentation. The foundation is looking for projects that mark a shift, a new direction, or a willingness to test fresh ideas, materials, and methods rather than continuations of established work. Applications require a project proposal with budget and timeline (up to 1,000 words), a portfolio, and a detailed CV. Submission is free, through the foundation's website. The deadline is May 15, 2026.

calls.title: Guest Room: Annet Dekker & Margriet Schavemaker
calls.description: Open call curated by Annet Dekker (Associate Professor of Cultural Analysis at the University of Amsterdam and co-director of the Centre for the Study of the Networked Image at London South Bank University) with Margriet Schavemaker (Director, Kunstmuseum Den Haag), exploring "The Brilliance of the Mundane." Invites reflections on the unnoticed and the unremarkable — images rooted in everyday life, shaped by happenstance, hasty habits, glitched files, accidental photos, and repetitive imagery — asking how to restore dignity to overlooked visual material and considering how these fragments operate as digital folklore fuelling contemporary image practices. Selected work featured on Der Greif's platform with a face-to-face feedback session from the curators. €250 Guest Room scholarship. Works previously selected in past Der Greif opportunities are not eligible.
calls.summary: Theme: "The Brilliance of the Mundane" — everyday, accidental, and overlooked imagery as digital folklore.
jury: Annet Dekker, Associate Professor of Cultural Analysis, University of Amsterdam
Margriet Schavemaker, Director, Kunstmuseum Den Haag
prose: Guest Room is Der Greif's recurring curator-led open call format. Each edition is shaped by an external curator or curatorial duo who set the theme and selection criteria. This Guest Room is curated jointly by Annet Dekker and Margriet Schavemaker.

Dekker is Associate Professor of Cultural Analysis and MA Coordinator of Archival and Information Studies at the University of Amsterdam, and co-director of the Centre for the Study of the Networked Image at London South Bank University. Schavemaker is Director of Kunstmuseum Den Haag and specialises in modern and contemporary culture, museum practice, and digital art.

The theme is "The Brilliance of the Mundane." The brief asks for reflection on the unnoticed and unremarkable: everyday images shaped by happenstance, hasty habits, glitched files, accidental photos, repetitive imagery. The curators frame these fragments as a form of digital folklore fuelling contemporary image practices, and ask how to restore dignity to images that are typically dismissed.

Selected work is published on Der Greif's platform. Selected artists also receive a face-to-face feedback session with the curators. One artist receives a €250 Guest Room scholarship. Eligibility is open globally; works previously selected in past Der Greif opportunities are not eligible.

Submission is through Picter. The fee is voluntary (PWYC) — €10 suggested but not required, with 50–100% hardship vouchers available by emailing voucher-guestroom@dergreif.org. The deadline is June 6, 2026 at 11:59 PM CET; the resulting online exhibition launches July 2026 on dergreif.org.

calls.title: Der Greif Issue 19 — I Am Because of You, Mother Earth
calls.description: Open call for Der Greif's 19th print issue, guest-edited by Zanele Muholi — the South African visual activist and 2026 Hasselblad Award laureate, known for documenting Black LGBTQIA+ communities and reimagining Blackness. Theme: "I Am Because of You, Mother Earth" — examining environment as inseparable from bodies, histories, and relationships, with Muholi framing the body as a landscape, the face as geography, and breath as atmosphere. Accepts photography, writing, poetry, and essays from contributors worldwide; collaborative submissions encouraged. Selected work is reviewed by Muholi, published in Issue 19 with a free copy plus discounted additional copies, considered for an Artist Feature on dergreif.org, and may participate in Der Greif's Paris Photo 2026 events.
calls.summary: Print issue guest-edited by Zanele Muholi. Theme: "I Am Because of You, Mother Earth" — environment as inseparable from body and breath.
prose: Der Greif is the Munich-based photography magazine and platform founded in 2008, supported by the Alexander Tutsek-Stiftung foundation. The magazine's print issues are guest-edited by a single curator or artist who sets the theme and reviews submissions, with Issue 19 guest-edited by Zanele Muholi.

Muholi is a South African visual activist and photographer based in Cape Town, internationally recognised for documenting Black LGBTQIA+ communities, the Faces and Phases project, and a long-running self-portrait practice that reimagines representations of Blackness. They were named the 2026 Hasselblad Award laureate.

The theme is "I Am Because of You, Mother Earth." Muholi reframes environment as inseparable from the self: the body as a landscape, the face as geography, breath as atmosphere, with water in the blood, minerals in the bones, and soil that feeds the body all positioned as part of the same continuous ecology. The brief invites artists and writers to respond to this framing.

Accepted media include photography, writing, poetry, and essays. Collaborative submissions are encouraged. Selected work is reviewed by Muholi, published in Issue 19 with a complimentary copy plus discounts on additional copies, and considered for an Artist Feature on dergreif.org. Selected contributors may also participate in Der Greif's Paris Photo 2026 programme and related events.
Submission is through Picter. The fee is voluntary (PWYC) — €13 until June 7, then €15, with financial assistance available on request. The deadline is June 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM CET.

calls.title: Jean Giono Photography Contest 2026
calls.description: Free photography contest from the Friends of Jean Giono association, organised in partnership with Regards Alpins (a member association that runs photographic events tied to literature). Photographs — single image or coherent series — inspired by an excerpt from Giono's novel Noé, meditating on extraordinary landscapes and the act of seeing them through a lens. The 2026 Rencontres Giono festival is themed "Giono and Photography," running July 29–August 2 in Manosque; winners are announced at the festival on August 1, 2026. Open to amateurs and professionals of any age and country.
calls.summary: Free contest by Les Amis de Jean Giono and Regards Alpins. Photos inspired by Giono's Noé. Awards at Rencontres Giono, Manosque.

calls.title: UNSTAGED Journal — Materiality
calls.description: Themed issue of UNSTAGED, an independent photography journal dedicated to lens-based inquiries into comforting and discomforting authenticity. The Materiality call, guest curated by Francisco Gonzalez Camacho (@frangccom), seeks works that embrace a connection with the process and create a bridge between photography and other media — such as printmaking — to expand the capacities of the photographic form through alternative techniques, materials, and interventions. Submit 5–10 photographs as JPG files (long edge 2000px, 300 DPI) with project description (max 500 words). Upload work to a public Google Drive and send the link to reach@arek-ratai.com. Name files Name_ProjectTitle_01. Emails with attachments are deleted. Free entry, free print publication for selected photographers.
calls.summary: Free indie photography journal on authenticity. Theme: Materiality. Guest curated by Francisco Gonzalez Camacho. Print publication.
prose: UNSTAGED is an independent photography journal dedicated to lens-based work that engages with comforting and discomforting authenticity. The journal runs themed issues with rotating guest curators. The Materiality call asks photographers to engage with the material side of the medium — surface, texture, substance — and the bridges photography forms with adjacent practices like printmaking.

The call is guest curated by Francisco Gonzalez Camacho (@frangccom). The brief explicitly invites alternative techniques, materials, and interventions — works that treat the photograph as more than a transparent image and engage process as part of the meaning.
Eligible submissions span single images, diptychs, triptychs, and mixed-media approaches. AI-generated work is not accepted.

Each photographer submits 5 to 10 photographs as JPG files (long edge 2000px, 300 DPI) plus a project description up to 500 words. The submission process is unusual: applicants upload work to a publicly accessible Google Drive folder and send the link to reach@arek-ratai.com. Files must be named Name_ProjectTitle_01. Emails with attachments are deleted unread.
Submission is free of charge. Eligibility is open globally. The 2026 deadline is June 15.

calls.title: THAT ONE PHOTOGRAPH
calls.description: Juried single-image call from Decagon Gallery for a photograph carrying emotional weight tied to memory, attachment, intimacy, grief, distance, tenderness, longing, or time. The brief favors images 'never fully left behind' over technical perfection. $1,000 total cash awards across five placements ($500 first plus solo website exhibition, $250 second, $150 third, two $50 honorable mentions). All selected photographers receive a dedicated exhibition page, Instagram feature, and catalog placement. Online exhibition July 1 – September 1, 2026. Open worldwide, all photographic styles and processes.
calls.summary: Single-image call on memory, intimacy, longing. $1,000 awards. Online exhibition + catalog from Decagon Gallery.
prose: Decagon Gallery is an online curatorial platform that runs themed photography exhibitions with published catalogs and social distribution. "That One Photograph" is the gallery's single-image call for the photograph that carries weight tied to memory, attachment, intimacy, grief, distance, tenderness, longing, or time. The brief explicitly de-prioritizes portfolio-best work — the gallery wants images that 'continue to live inside' the photographer rather than technically perfect frames.

Cash awards total $1,000 across five placements: $500 first place plus a solo website exhibition, $250 second, $150 third, and two $50 honorable mentions. A separate Human Presence Nomination offers free entry to a future open call. All selected photographers receive a dedicated exhibition page, Instagram feature, and catalog placement. The 2026 exhibition runs July 1 through September 1.
Selection is by the Decagon Gallery team. All photographic styles and processes are welcome.

Submissions are JPG at 2100 pixels on the long side — no text, watermarks, or borders — plus one short sentence describing what 'continues to live inside' the image. One photograph per entry. Entry fee is $15. Eligibility is open to photographers worldwide aged 18 and over. The 2026 deadline is June 20 at 11:59 PM Eastern; results announced June 28.

calls.title: RED Photography Exhibit
calls.description: Photographs exploring red in any style — documentary, fine art, abstract, or experimental. 26 images selected for exhibition at Dusk Gallery in Santa Fe, NM, August 7–28, 2026. Selected artists receive complimentary professional printing on Luster paper and 24×24 black museum-quality framing. 50% commission on sales. Open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers.
jury: Holly Hart, Fine Art Photographer & Founder, Dusk Gallery
calls.summary: Red in any style — documentary, fine art, abstract, experimental. Free pro printing & framing. Santa Fe, NM.
prose: Dusk Gallery is a Santa Fe, New Mexico photography gallery founded by fine art photographer Holly Hart, who also founded Decode Gallery in Tucson — Dusk operates as Hart's New Mexico project space alongside the larger Tucson program. "RED" is the gallery's themed call asking photographers to explore the color in any photographic style — documentary, fine art, abstract, or experimental approaches all welcome.

Twenty-six photographs are selected for the exhibition at Dusk Gallery, running August 7 through 28, 2026 with an opening reception. Selected work appears in the gallery's published catalog and across social media.

What's unusual: the gallery covers all professional printing on Luster paper, gallery-quality 24×24 inch black museum frames, and white matting from the gallery's collection. The artist provides only the high-resolution JPEG; the gallery resizes without cropping the original composition.
Sales terms split commission 50/50. Photographer retains all rights.

Entry fees: $40 for 5 images, $45 for up to 10. Eligibility is open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers. Submissions require JPEGs at 500KB to 5MB, 4,500 pixels on the longest side. The 2026 deadline is June 25, with notifications within 2 weeks.

calls.title: BBA One Shot Award - Spring 2026
calls.description: Single-image photography prize. 20 images selected for print exhibition at BBA Gallery in Berlin, plus 30 additional images on digital display. First prize: €300 + exhibition + Artsy listing + social media promotion. All production and shipping costs covered.
calls.summary: Single-image photo prize. 20 images exhibited at BBA Gallery Berlin. €300 + Artsy listing. Production covered.
jury: Vishal Shah, Managing & Creative Director, BBA Gallery
Jo Schwab, Photographer & Lecturer, Camera Work Gallery
prose: BBA Gallery is a Berlin-based contemporary art gallery that runs several international prizes across photography, painting, and sculpture. The One Shot Award is the gallery's single-image photography call, running multiple editions per year — the Spring 2026 edition closes May 25.

The format is intentionally minimal: one image, one entry, €19 fee. Twenty selected images are printed and exhibited at BBA Gallery in Berlin; thirty additional images are shown on digital display. The first-place winner receives €300 cash, the exhibition, social media promotion, and an Artsy profile listing — Artsy being the major online art marketplace.

BBA covers all production and shipping costs for selected work. Eligibility is open globally to any artist 18+, any photographic medium or genre. Submission is through the BBA Prizes platform: JPG, PNG, or HEIC up to 3MB, with name, country, image title, and year of creation.

calls.title: FILE NOT FOUND — Archive Residencies 2026
calls.description: International open call selecting ten artists for residencies at cultural archives worldwide, run by Goethe-Institut in collaboration with Gerador. Each residency lasts 2 weeks to 2 months between August 2026 and May 2027, on-site at one of ten participating archives: Acervo Bajubá (São Paulo), The ArQuives (Toronto), China Modern Art Archive (Beijing), documenta archiv (Kassel), Arsenal Filminstitut (Berlin), Kurdistan Center for Arts & Culture (Erbil), Imagine IC & The Need for Legacy (Amsterdam), VEHA Archive (Podlasie), Museu Nacional de Arte Contemporânea (Lisbon), and South African History Archive (Johannesburg). Each selected artist receives €2,000 artist fee, €2,000 production budget, and up to €2,000 for travel and accommodation. Final works exhibited at BLMK (Brandenburgisches Landesmuseum für moderne Kunst) in Cottbus, Germany, in Fall 2027. Open to artists worldwide, all disciplines including photography. Working language English.
calls.summary: Ten artist residencies at archives worldwide. €4,000 + travel + final exhibition at BLMK Cottbus 2027. With Gerador.

calls.title: Men Asleep — 2026 Book & Exhibition Open Call
calls.description: Book and exhibition expansion of the 2025 'Men Asleep' zine compiled by Jordanna Kalman and published by Memory Version. Submit one photograph of a man sleeping. JPEG, 300 dpi, 3000 px on the long side, named Firstname_Lastname.jpeg. Email subject 'Men Asleep Submission' with name, website, and Instagram handle in the body. Entries not following these instructions will not be considered.
calls.summary: Book and exhibition expansion of Jordanna Kalman's 2025 'Men Asleep' zine. One photograph of a man sleeping. Free, open to all.
prose: Men Asleep began as a 2025 zine compiled by Jordanna Kalman and published by Memory Version. Kalman invited fifty women photographers to send a photograph of a man sleeping; nineteen responded, and the resulting 40-page black-and-white zine was inflected by the Gisèle Pelicot case and the contrast between sleep as safety and as vulnerability.

The 2026 open call expands the project into a book and an exhibition. The brief remains spare: one photograph of a man sleeping. The work selected for the 2025 zine ranged from intimate and dreamy to charged with implied threat — the call leaves interpretation to the photographer.

Submission is by email. The image must be JPEG, 300 dpi, with the long side at 3000 pixels, named Firstname_Lastname.jpeg. The email subject must read 'Men Asleep Submission' and the body must include name, website, and Instagram handle. Entries that do not follow these instructions will not be considered.
Entry is free. The deadline is August 1, 2026. The project is run directly by Memory Version; no jury list or selection schedule is published on the call page.

calls.title: PURE ABSTRACTION
calls.description: Online juried exhibit celebrating pure abstraction — shape, color, line, texture, and the rhythm of form. Open to all fine art mediums including photography. Artists receive 100% of sale price with no commission.
jury: Amy Matteson Neill, Creative Director, Art Fluent
calls.summary: Online juried exhibit for pure abstraction across all mediums including photography. 100% commission-free sales. $1,250 in prizes.
prose: Art Fluent is a Boston-based curatorial platform (1 Washington Mall #1218, Boston, MA 02108) that runs themed online juried exhibitions across fine art mediums. "PURE ABSTRACTION" is the platform's open call for work that lets shape, color, line, texture, and form stand on their own — work that is not bound by representation.

Cash prizes total $1,250: a Best of Show award of $750 and two Director's Choice awards of $250 each. Beyond cash, all accepted work is displayed in the online gallery on art-fluent.com, with sales going through the platform at 100% commission to the artist. The selection is curated by Creative Director Amy Matteson Neill and an anonymous committee.

Entry fee is $25 for the first work and $10 each additional, up to 20 submissions per artist. Open globally to amateur and professional artists; AI-generated work is not accepted, and work made under instructor guidance or copied from other sources is excluded. Submissions go through CaFÉ (callforentry.org), which requires a free artist account.
Art Fluent does not provide individualized rejection feedback. The 2026 deadline is August 28 (midnight MST), with notification on September 25, 2026.
